children.translated_text: When the night of <s>Brahmā</s> had passed and the lotus-born one had awakened,

children.text: viṣṇuḥ sisṛkṣur bhūtāni jñātvā bhūmiṃ jalānugām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, wishing to create beings, perceived that the earth had followed the waters.
Delighting in play in the waters, auspicious, at the beginnings of aeons as before,
he assumed the form of a boar and raised up the earth.
His feet were the Vedas, his tusks the sacrificial posts, his teeth the sacrifices, his mouth the altar-pile;
his tongue was fire, his hair darbha grass, his head <s>Brahmā</s>; he was mighty in austerity.
Day and night were his eyes; he was divine, adorned with the lore of the Vedāṅgas.
His nose was clarified butter, his snout the sacrificial ladle; great was the sound of his Sāman chant.
He consisted of <s>dharma</s> and truth, splendid, honored by ordered strides and heroic strides;
his great snout was expiation, his knees were the sacrificial animal; he had a vast form.
His entrails were the Udgātṛ priests, his generative mark was the oblation, and seeds and herbs were his great fruit;
his inner self was the altar, his buttocks were transformed into mantras, and soma was his blood.
His shoulders were the altar-ground, his fragrance the oblation, and he sped toward offerings to gods and ancestors and the rest.
His body was the sacrificial shed; radiant, he was endowed with many consecrations.
His heart was the sacrificial fee, and he was made of the great mantra of yoga, mighty;
his lips were beautiful with the upākarman, and he was adorned with the whirl of the pravargya rite.
His path was the movement of many metres, and the secret Upaniṣads were his seat;
with Chāyā as his wife and helper, he rose like a jeweled horn.
The lord, moving in the waters of the single ocean, lifted the earth, extending to the seas,
together with mountains, forests, and groves, fallen from the waters of the single ocean.
Raising her up on the tip of his tusk, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds,
the primeval god, the great yogin, made the earth again.
Thus, becoming the sacrificial boar and seeking the welfare of beings,
the divine earth, which had formerly gone to Rasātala, was raised up.

children.text: uddhṛtya niścale sthāne sthāpayitvā tathā svake
children.translated_text: Having raised her, set her in a firm place, and likewise in her own station,
<s>Madhusūdana</s> divided the waters contained in her according to their proper places.

children.text: sāmudryaś ca samudreṣu nādeyīś ca nadīṣu ca
children.translated_text: The sea-born waters he placed in the seas, and the river-born waters in the rivers;

children.text: palvaleṣu ca pālvalyaḥ saraḥsu ca sarobhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the pool-born waters in pools, and those born in lakes in the lakes.
He made the seven nether regions, likewise the set of seven worlds,

children.text: dvīpānām udadhīnāṃ ca sthānāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and the various places of the islands and oceans.
He made the guardians of places, the guardians of the worlds, rivers, mountains, and forest trees,

children.text: ṛṣīṃś ca sapta dharmajñān vedān sāṅgān surāsurān ||
children.translated_text: and the seven seers who know <s>dharma</s>, the Vedas with their auxiliaries, gods and antigods,
piśācas, serpents, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and human beings,
animals, birds, deer and the rest, and the fourfold host of beings,
clouds, rainbows, lightning and the like, and many kinds of sacrifices too.
Thus the blessed <s>Varāha</s>, having made this world with its moving and unmoving beings,

children.text: jagaj jagāma lokānām avijñātāṃ tadā gatim ||
children.translated_text: then went by a path unknown to the worlds.
When the god of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>, had gone by an unknown path,

children.text: vasudhā cintayāmāsa kā dhṛtir me bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasudhā</s> thought, 'What support will there be for me?'

children.text: pṛcchāmi kaśyapaṃ gatvā sa me vakṣyaty asaṃśayam
children.translated_text: 'I shall go and ask <s>Kaśyapa</s>; he will undoubtedly tell me,

children.text: madīyāṃ vahate cintāṃ nityam eva mahāmuniḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the great sage always bears concern for me.'

children.text: evaṃ sā niścayaṃ kṛtvā devī strīrūpadhāriṇī
children.translated_text: Having made this decision, the goddess assumed the form of a woman

children.text: jagāma kaśyapaṃ draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavāṃs tāṃ ca kaśyapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and went to see <s>Kaśyapa</s>; and <s>Kaśyapa</s> saw her.
Her eyes were like blue lotus petals, her face like the autumn moon;
she was bright, with locks like swarms of bees and lips like bandhujīva flowers, auspicious.
She had fine brows, very delicate teeth, a lovely nose, and gently bent eyebrows;
her neck was like a conch, her thighs compact, and the region of her hips and buttocks full.

children.text: virejatuḥ stanau yasyāḥ samau pīnau nirantarau
children.translated_text: Her two breasts shone, equal, full, and close together,
like the frontal globes of <s>Indra</s>'s elephant, with the lustre of refined gold.
Her arms were soft as lotus stalks, and her hands like tender shoots;

children.text: rukmastambhanibhāv ūrū gūḍhe śliṣṭe ca jānunī ||
children.translated_text: her thighs were like golden pillars, and her knees were hidden and joined.
Her shanks were hairless and well-proportioned, and her feet exceedingly charming;

children.text: jaghanaṃ ca ghanaṃ madhyaṃ yathā kesariṇaḥ śiśoḥ ||
children.translated_text: her hips were full, and her waist was like that of a young lion.
Her nails were copper-red and full of radiance; her beauty delighted all minds.
With her glances she constantly made the quarters seem filled with blue lotuses.

children.text: kurvāṇāṃ prabhayā devīṃ tathā vitimirā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: With her radiance the goddess likewise made the quarters free of darkness;
she wore very fine white garments and was adorned with the finest jewels.
By the placing of her feet she made the earth seem covered with lotuses;
endowed with beauty and youth, she stood nearby as if modestly restrained.
Seeing that she had come near, <s>Kaśyapa</s> honored her,

children.text: uvāca tāṃ varārohe vijñātaṃ hṛdgataṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and then said to her, 'Fair-hipped one, what is in your heart is known to me.

children.text: dhare tava viśālākṣi gaccha devi janārdanam
children.translated_text: O <s>Dharā</s>, wide-eyed goddess, go to <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: sa te vakṣyaty aśeṣeṇa bhāvinī te yathā dhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He will tell you completely what your future support will be.

children.text: kṣīrode vasatis tasya mayā jñātā śubhānane
children.translated_text: O fair-faced one, I have learned that he dwells in the milk ocean,
by meditative yoga, O lovely-limbed one, through his grace for your sake.'

children.text: ity evam uktā sampūjya kaśyapaṃ vasudhā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Vasudhā</s> then honored <s>Kaśyapa</s>

children.text: prayayau keśavaṃ draṣṭuṃ kṣīrodam atha sāgaram ||
children.translated_text: and set out for the milk ocean to see <s>Keśava</s>.
She saw the ocean of nectar, charming with moonbeams,
crowded with hundreds of waves produced by the agitation of the wind,
resembling hundreds of Himālayas, like another disk of the earth,
as if summoning the earth with its moving hands of waves,

children.text: tair eva śuklatāṃ candre vidadhānam ivāniśam
children.translated_text: and with those very waves, as if continually making whiteness in the moon.
Because <s>Hari</s> was within it, it was free from every stain.

children.text: yasmāt tasmād dhārayantaṃ suśuklāṃ tanum ūrjitām
children.translated_text: From that cause it bore a very white and powerful body,
pale, inaccessible to birds, and situated below the worlds.
Adorned with masses of sapphire, it seemed like the sky turned upside down;
it appeared as if filled with clusters of forests arisen from rows of fruit.

children.text: nirmokam iva śeṣāher vistīrṇāntam atīva hi
children.translated_text: It was very vast at its furthest edge, like the cast-off skin of the serpent <s>Śeṣa</s>;

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra madhyasthaṃ dadṛśe keśavālayam ||
children.translated_text: having seen it, she then saw, standing in its midst, the abode of <s>Keśava</s>.
immeasurable in extent, endowed with indescribable majesty,
there she saw <s>Madhusūdana</s>, lying on <s>Śeṣa</s> as on a couch.
His lotus-like face was hard to discern because of the rays from the jewels on <s>Śeṣa</s> the serpent's hoods;
he shone like a hundred moons and had the radiance of ten thousand suns.
He wore yellow garments, was unshakable, and was adorned with every jewel;
he was resplendent with a sun-colored crown and with earrings.
His pair of feet was being massaged by <s>Lakṣmī</s> with her auspicious hands;
on every side he was attended by weapons that had taken bodily form.
Seeing that lotus-eyed <s>Madhusūdana</s>, she bowed to him;

children.text: jānubhyām avaniṃ gatvā vijñāpayati cāpy atha ||
children.translated_text: having gone down to the earth on her knees, she then made her petition.
"I was raised up by you, O god, after I had gone down to the bottom of <s>Rasātala</s>;
I was set in my own place, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because you desired the welfare of the worlds.

children.text: tatrādhunā hi deveśa kā dhṛtir me bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: But now, O lord of gods, what support will there be for me there?"

children.text: evam uktas tayā devyā devo vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by that goddess, the god spoke these words:
"Good people who delight in the practices of the varṇas and āśramas, wholly devoted to śāstra,

children.text: tvāṃ dhare dhārayiṣyanti teṣāṃ tvadbhāra āhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will uphold you, O <s>Dharā</s>; your burden is placed upon them."
So addressed, <s>Vasumatī</s> spoke to the god of gods:

children.text: varṇānām āśramāṇāṃ ca dharmān vada sanātana ||
children.translated_text: "Tell me the eternal dharmas of the varṇas and of the āśramas.

children.text: tvatto 'ham śrotum icchāmi tvaṃ hi me paramā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: I wish to hear them from you, for you are my supreme refuge.
Homage to you, lord of the gods of gods, destroyer of the power of the gods' enemies;
O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, lord of the world, bearer of conch, discus, and mace;
O <s>Padmanābha</s>, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, mighty in strength and valor;
O one beyond the senses, very hard to cross, O god, bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow;
O <s>Varāha</s>, terrifying one, <s>Govinda</s>, ancient one, supreme person;
O golden-haired one, all-eyed one, embodiment of sacrifice, stainless one;
O lord of field and knower of the field, sleeper upon the ocean of waters;
O mantra, bearer of mantras, inconceivable one, embodiment of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas;
O maker of the creation and dissolution of this entire world;
O knower of dharma and adharma, whose body is dharma, source of dharma, giver of boons;
O <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, immortal one, ether-like one, slayer of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>;
O enlarger of the great, unknowable one, all-pervading one, giver of fearlessness to all;
O excellent one, sinless one, cloud-like one, maker of the world;
O nourisher, abode of the waters, support of consciousness, inactive one;
O seven-headed one, teacher of sacrifice, ancient supreme person;
O fixed imperishable one, lord of the very subtle, lover of devotees, purifier;

children.text: tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvaṃ gatir brahmavādinām ||
children.translated_text: you are the refuge of all the gods; you are the refuge of those who teach Brahman.
Likewise, O supreme person, you are the refuge of those who know what is to be known.
I have taken refuge in you, O lord of the world, the steadfast <s>Vācaspati</s>, the master;
in the auspicious knower of Brahman, the unassailable one, <s>Vasuṣeṇa</s>, giver of wealth;
in the one endowed with the great power of yoga, <s>Pṛśnigarbha</s>, whose flame is sustained;
in great-souled <s>Vāsudeva</s>, lotus-eyed <s>Acyuta</s>;
in the divine teacher of gods and asuras, the all-pervading great lord of beings.
O single emanation, four-armed one, cause of the cause of the world,

children.text: brūhi me bhagavan dharmāṃś cāturvarṇyasya śāśvatān ||
children.translated_text: tell me, Blessed One, the eternal dharmas of the fourfold varṇa order,
joined with the practices of the āśramas, together with their secrets and their summaries."

children.text: evam uktas tu deveśaḥ kṣoṇyā kṣoṇīm abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Kṣoṇī</s>, the lord of gods spoke to <s>Kṣoṇī</s>:

children.text: śṛṇu devi dhare dharmāṃś cāturvarṇyasya śāśvatān
children.translated_text: "Listen, O goddess, O <s>Dharā</s>, to the eternal dharmas of the fourfold varṇa order,
joined with the practices of the āśramas, together with their secrets and their summaries.

children.text: ye tu tvāṃ dhārayiṣyanti santas teṣāṃ parāyaṇān
children.translated_text: The virtuous people who will support you are devoted to those dharmas.
Sit down, fair-thighed one, on this excellent golden seat.

children.text: sukhāsīnā nibodha tvaṃ dharmān nigadato mama
children.translated_text: Seated comfortably, learn the dharmas as I declare them."

children.text: śuśruve vaiṣṇavān dharmān sukhāsīnā dharā tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dharā</s>, seated at ease, listened to the Vaiṣṇava dharmas.

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdraś ceti varṇāś catvāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The varṇas are four: brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra.
Of these, the first three are twice-born.
For them there is a series of rites accompanied by mantras, beginning with conception and ending at the cremation ground.
And their dharmas are as follows.
For a brāhmaṇa, teaching is the duty.
For a kṣatriya, constant engagement with weapons is the duty.
For a vaiśya, the tending of cattle is the duty.
For a śūdra, service to the twice-born is the duty.
For the twice-born, sacrificing and study are duties.
Now, their means of livelihood are these.
For a brāhmaṇa, officiating at sacrifices and receiving gifts.
For a kṣatriya, protection of the land.
For a vaiśya, agriculture, cattle-protection, trade, lending at interest, and maintaining productive sources.
For a śūdra, all crafts.
In distress, the occupation immediately next in order may be used.

children.text: kṣamā satyam damaḥ śaucaṃ dānam indriyasaṃyamaḥ
children.translated_text: Forbearance, truth, restraint, purity, generosity, control of the senses,
non-injury, service to the teacher, visiting sacred fords, compassion,
straightforwardness, freedom from greed, worship of gods and brāhmaṇas,

children.text: anabhyasūyā ca tathā dharmaḥ sāmānya ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and likewise absence of fault-finding: this is called the common dharma.
Now, the dharmas of kings.
Protection of the subjects.
Establishing the varṇas and āśramas each in their own dharma.

children.text: rājā ca jāṅgalaṃ paśavyaṃ sasyopetaṃ deśam āśrayet ||
children.translated_text: And the king should resort to a country that is open, fit for cattle, and furnished with crops.
It should also be chiefly inhabited by vaiśyas and śūdras.
There he should resort to one of the kinds of fort: desert, manned, earthen, water, tree, or mountain fort.
Stationed there, he should appoint heads over each village.
He should appoint superintendents of ten villages,
superintendents of a hundred villages,
and superintendents of districts.
A village head should remedy the faults arising in villages.
If unable, he should report it to the superintendent of ten villages.
If that one too is unable, he should report it to the superintendent of a hundred villages.
If that one too is unable, he should report it to the district superintendent.
The district superintendent too should eradicate the fault by every means.
He should appoint trustworthy men over mines, tolls, ferries, and elephant forests.
The most righteous men in matters of <s>dharma</s>.
Those skilled in matters of wealth.
The brave in the duties of battle.
The fierce in fierce tasks.
Eunuchs among women.

children.text: prajābhyo balyarthaṃ saṃvatsareṇa dhānyataḥ ṣaṣṭham aṃśam ādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of the <s>bali</s> tax from the subjects, he should take annually a sixth part of the grain.
And from all crops.
Two in a hundred from livestock, gold, and garments.
The king should take a sixth share from meat, honey, ghee, medicines, perfumes, flowers, roots, fruits, juices, firewood, leaves, hides, earthen vessels, stone vessels, and wicker goods.
He should not collect taxes from Brahmins.
For they are givers of <s>dharma</s> to the king.
And the king receives a sixth share of the merits and demerits of his subjects.
From merchandise of his own country he should take a tenth share as customs duty.
And from foreign merchandise, a twentieth.
One who moves away from the customs station should incur confiscation of all his goods.

children.text: śilpinaḥ karmajīvinaś ca māsenaikaṃ rājñaḥ karma kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Artisans and those who live by labor should perform one service for the king each month.
The ruler, ministers, fortress, treasury, force, realm, and allies are the constituent elements of the state.
And he should kill those who corrupt them.
In his own kingdom and in another kingdom he should have spies as his eyes.
He should honor good people.
And he should kill the wicked.
Toward enemy, ally, neutral, and intermediate rulers he should employ conciliation, division, gifts, and force, as appropriate and at the proper time.
And he should resort, at the proper time, to peace, war, marching, remaining in place, seeking protection, and a dual policy.
He should set out on campaign in <s>Caitra</s> or in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>.
Or when the other ruler is in distress.
On obtaining a foreign country, he should not abolish the <s>dharmas</s> of that country.
And when attacked by another, he should protect his own realm with all his power.
For kings there is no <s>dharma</s> equal to giving up the body in battle.
Those who are killed while protecting cows, Brahmins, the king, friends, wealth, wives, or life are sharers in the world of heaven.
And also those killed for the sake of preventing mixture of the social classes.
When the king has obtained another's city, he should consecrate there someone belonging to that lineage.
He should not uproot the royal family.
Except in the case of a royal family of ignoble lineage.
He should avoid attachment to hunting, dice, women, and drinking.
And harshness in speech and harshness in punishment.
He should not cause the ruin of wealth.
He should not destroy the sources of revenue.
He should not be one who showers gifts on unworthy recipients.
From mines he should take everything.
Having found a treasure, he should give half of it to Brahmins.
He should put the second half into the treasury.
A Brahmin, having found a treasure, may take it all.

children.text: kṣatriyaś caturtham aṃśaṃ rājñe dadyāt caturtham aṃśaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ ardham ādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: A Kshatriya should give a fourth share to the king, a fourth share to Brahmins, and take half.

children.text: vaiśyas tu caturtham aṃśaṃ rājñe dadyāt brāhmaṇebhyo 'rdhaṃ caturtham aṃśam ādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: But a Vaishya should give a fourth share to the king, half to Brahmins, and take a fourth share.

children.text: śūdraś cāvāptaṃ dvādaśadhā vibhajya pañcāṃśān rājñe dadyāt pañcāṃśān brāhmaṇebhyaḥ aṃśadvayam ādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: And a Shudra, dividing what he has obtained into twelve parts, should give five shares to the king, five shares to Brahmins, and take two shares.
If what was found is discovered after not being reported, he should confiscate it all.

children.text: svanihitād rājñe brāhmaṇavarjaṃ dvādaśam aṃśaṃ dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: From treasure hidden by themselves, except in the case of Brahmins, they should give a twelfth share to the king.

children.text: paranihitaṃ svanihitam iti bruvaṃs tatsamaṃ daṇḍam āvahet ||
children.translated_text: One who says that another's hidden treasure is his own hidden treasure should incur an equal fine.
The king should protect the property of minors, the helpless, and women.

children.text: caurahṛtaṃ dhanam avāpya sarvam eva sarvavarṇebhyo dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having recovered wealth stolen by thieves, he should give it all back to people of all classes.
And if he has not recovered it, he should give it from his own treasury.
He should pacify calamities caused by fate through rites for peace and well-being.
And attacks by enemy armies through constant readiness with weapons.

children.text: vedetihāsadharmaśāstrārthakuśalaṃ kulīnam avyaṅgaṃ tapasvinaṃ purohitaṃ ca varayet ||
children.translated_text: He should choose as priest a man learned in the meaning of the Veda, Itihāsa, and Dharmaśāstra, well-born, without defect, and ascetic.

children.text: śucīn alubdhān avahitān śaktisampannān sarvārtheṣu ca sahāyān ||
children.translated_text: And as assistants in all matters, men who are pure, free from greed, attentive, and endowed with ability.

children.text: svayam eva vyavahārān paśyed vidvadbhir brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdham ||
children.translated_text: He himself should inspect legal proceedings together with learned Brahmins.
Or he should appoint a Brahmin to inspect legal proceedings.

children.text: janmakarmavratopetāś ca rājñā sabhāsadaḥ kāryāḥ ripau mitre ca ye samāḥ kāmakrodhabhayalobhādibhiḥ kāryārthibhir anāhāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king should appoint as assessors those endowed with birth, conduct, and vows, who are the same toward enemy and friend, and who cannot be swayed by litigants through desire, anger, fear, greed, and the like.
And in all undertakings the king should be guided by the yearly astrologer.
He should constantly honor gods and Brahmins.
He should be one who serves elders.
And one who performs sacrifices.
In his realm no Brahmin should sink down afflicted by hunger.
Nor anyone else who is devoted to good action.
And he should grant land to Brahmins.

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca pratipādayet teṣāṃ svavaṃśyān bhuvaḥ parimāṇaṃ dānacchedopavarṇanaṃ ca paṭe tāmrapaṭṭe vā likhitaṃ svamudrāṅkitaṃ cāgāminṛpativijñāpanārthaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: To those to whom he grants it, he should give, for the information of future kings, a document written on cloth or on a copper plate, marked with his own seal, describing their lineage, the measure of the land, and the grant and its boundaries.
And he should not seize land given by another.
He should give all dues to Brahmins.
But he should protect himself on every side.
And he should be pleasing to behold.
And he should possess antidotes and charms for subduing snakes.
He should not use anything unexamined.
He should speak with a smile first.
Even toward those deserving death he should not make a frown.
And he should have punishments imposed on those liable to punishment in proportion to their offences.
He should administer punishment properly.

children.text: dvitīyam aparādhaṃ na sa kasyacit kṣameta ||
children.translated_text: He should not forgive anyone a second offence.
For kings, there is no one who is not punishable if he fails to maintain his own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yatra śyāmo lohitākṣo daṇḍaś carati nirbhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where dark-hued, red-eyed punishment moves about fearlessly,

children.text: prajās tatra vivardhante netā cet sādhu paśyati ||
children.translated_text: there the subjects prosper, if the leader sees rightly.

children.text: svarāṣṭre nyāyadaṇḍaḥ syād bhṛśadaṇḍaś ca śatruṣu
children.translated_text: In his own kingdom he should have punishment according to justice, and toward enemies a severe punishment;
toward friends he should be straightforward, toward the affectionate gentle, and toward Brahmins endowed with forbearance.
For a king of such conduct, even if he lives by gleaning grains,
his fame spreads in the world like a drop of oil on water.

children.text: prajāsukhe sukhī rājā tadduḥkhe yaś ca duḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: The king is happy in the happiness of his subjects, and distressed in their distress;

children.text: sa kīrtiyukto loke 'smin pretya svarge mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: he, endowed with fame in this world, is honored in heaven after death.
The dust seen in a sunbeam standing in a lattice is called a trasareṇu.
Eight of those make one likṣā.
Three of those make one rājasarṣapa.
Three of those make one gaurasarṣapa.
Six of those make one yava.
Three of those make one kṛṣṇala.
Five of those make one māṣa.
Twelve of those make half an akṣa.
Half an akṣa together with four māṣakas is a suvarṇa.
Four suvarṇas make one niṣka.
Two kṛṣṇalas of equal weight make a silver māṣaka.
Sixteen of those make one dharaṇa.
A copper kārṣika is a kārṣāpaṇa.

children.text: paṇānāṃ dve śate sārdhe prathamaḥ sāhasaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Two hundred and fifty paṇas are remembered as the first sāhasa fine;

children.text: madhyamaḥ pañca vijñeyaḥ sahasraṃ tveṣa cottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the middle one should be known as five hundred, and this highest one is one thousand.
Now all perpetrators of great sins, except a Brahmin, are liable to execution.
There is no bodily punishment for a Brahmin.
He should banish a Brahmin from his own country after branding him.

children.text: tasya ca brahmahatyāyām aśiraskaṃ puruṣaṃ lalāṭe kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: And for killing a Brahmin, he should mark on his forehead a headless man.
For drinking liquor, a liquor-banner.
For theft, a dog's foot.
For intercourse with the teacher's wife, a vulva.

children.text: anyatrāpi vadhyakarmaṇi tiṣṭhantaṃ samagradhanam akṣataṃ vivāsayet ||
children.translated_text: In any other capital offense also, he should banish him, with all his property intact and unharmed.
The king should execute makers of forged documents.
And also makers of forged writings.
Poisoners, arsonists, violent robbers, and killers of women, children, and men.

children.text: ye ca dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebhyo 'dhikam apahareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those who steal more grain than ten kumbhas.
More than one hundred of things weighed or measured.
And those of low family who desire the kingdom.
And breakers of embankments.
And those who give shelter and food to violent robbers.
Except when the king is powerless.
Also a woman whose husband is impotent and who transgresses him.

children.text: hīnavarṇo 'dhikavarṇasya yenāṅgenāparādhaṃ kuryāt tad evāsya śātayet ||
children.translated_text: With whatever limb a man of lower varṇa commits an offense against one of higher varṇa, that very limb of his should be cut off.
One who sits on the same seat should be branded on the hip and banished.
One who spits should be made deprived of both lips.
And one who breaks wind should be deprived of his anus.
And one who reviles should have his tongue cut out.

children.text: darpeṇa dharmopadeśakāriṇāṃ rājā taptam āsecayet tailam āsye ||
children.translated_text: The king should have hot oil poured into the mouth of one who, out of arrogance, gives instruction in dharma.

children.text: droheṇa ca nāmajātigrahaṇe daśāṅgulo 'sya śaṅkur nikheyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when he maliciously names the other's name or caste, a spike ten fingers long should be driven into him.
One who falsely states another's learning, locality, caste, or occupation is to be fined two hundred kārṣāpaṇas.
Even one who speaks the truth about a one-eyed or lame person and the like is fined two kārṣāpaṇas.
One who insults teachers is fined two hundred kārṣāpaṇas.
But if an accusation causing another's fall is made, the highest sāhasa fine is imposed.
For one connected with a minor sin, the middle fine.
For insulting elders learned in the three Vedas, and also castes and guilds,
and villages or regions, the first sāhasa fine is imposed.
For an insult involving physical defect, the fine is one hundred kārṣāpaṇas.
But when it involves the mother, the highest fine.
For reviling one of the same varṇa, he is to be fined twelve paṇas.
For reviling one of a lower varṇa, six.
According to the occasion, for insulting one of a higher varṇa, the fine is of corresponding amount.
Or three kārṣāpaṇas.
The same applies in the utterance of abusive speech.
A defeated litigant who has intercourse with a woman of the same varṇa is to be fined the highest sāhasa.
For intercourse with a woman of lower varṇa, the middle fine.
And for intercourse with a cow.
For intercourse with an outcaste woman, he is liable to execution.
For intercourse with an animal, he is to be fined one hundred kārṣāpaṇas.
And one who gives a girl in marriage without declaring her defect is fined the same.
And he must support her.
One who says of an unblemished girl, 'She is blemished,' incurs the highest sāhasa fine.
A killer of an elephant, horse, camel, or cow should be made one-handed and one-footed.
And one who sells meat that should not be sold.
A killer of domestic animals is to be fined one hundred kārṣāpaṇas.
He should give the animal's value to its owner.
A killer of wild animals is fined fifty kārṣāpaṇas.
A killer of birds or a killer of fish is fined ten kārṣāpaṇas.
And an injurer of insects, one kārṣāpaṇa.
One who cuts a fruit-bearing tree incurs the highest sāhasa fine.
One who cuts a flowering tree incurs the middle fine.
One who cuts creepers, shrubs, or vines is fined one hundred kārṣāpaṇas.
For cutting grass, one kārṣāpaṇa.
And all of them must pay the owners the value of what would have been produced from those things.
One who raises his hand threateningly is fined ten kārṣāpaṇas.
With the foot, twenty.
With a piece of wood, the first sāhasa fine.
With a stone, the middle fine.
With a weapon, the highest.
For pulling the foot, hair, garment, or hand, ten paṇas.
One who causes pain without bloodshed is fined thirty-two paṇas.
With bloodshed, sixty-four.
For breaking a hand, foot, or tooth, or cutting off an ear or nose, the middle fine.
And for obstructing movement, eating, or speech, and for giving a blow.
For breaking an eye, neck, arm, thigh, or shoulder, the highest fine.

children.text: ubhayanetrabhedinaṃ rājā yāvaj jīvaṃ bandhanān na muñcet ||
children.translated_text: The king should not release for life from imprisonment one who has destroyed both eyes.
Or he should do the same to him.

children.text: ekaṃ bahūnāṃ nighnatāṃ pratyekam uktād daṇḍād dviguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When many are killing one person, the penalty stated for the offense is doubled for each of them.
The same applies to those nearby, and to those passing along, who do not run to help someone crying out.
All those who cause injury to a person must pay the expense of his recovery.
So too must those who cause injury to village livestock.
A thief of cows, horses, camels, or elephants is to be made one-handed and one-footed.
A thief of goats or sheep is to be made one-handed.
A thief of grain is to be fined eleven times its value.
So too a thief of standing crops.

children.text: suvarṇarajatavastrāṇāṃ pañcāśatas tv abhyadhikam apaharan vikaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who steals more than fifty in gold, silver, or garments is to be mutilated.
For less than that, he is to be fined eleven times the value.

The thief of thread, cotton, cow-dung, molasses, curds, milk, buttermilk, grass, salt, clay, ashes, birds, fish, ghee, oil, meat, honey, bamboo, cane, earthen vessels, or metal vessels is to be fined three times the value.
So too in the case of cooked foods.
For stealing flowers, greens, shrubs, vines, creepers, or leaves, the fine is five <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>.
So too for vegetables, roots, and fruits.
A thief of jewels incurs the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine.
The thief of goods not specifically mentioned is fined an amount equal to their value.
Thieves must be made to pay the owner all that has been stolen.
After that, the stated punishment is to be imposed on them.

children.text: yeṣāṃ deyaḥ panthās teṣām apathadāyī kārṣāpaṇapañcaviṃśatiṃ daṇḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who does not give the road to those to whom the road should be given is to be fined twenty-five <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
So too one who does not give a seat to someone entitled to a seat.
And one who does not honor someone entitled to honor.
And in the case of transgressing the invitation due to neighboring Brahmins.
And in the case of those who invite someone but do not provide the meal.
An invited guest who says, 'So be it,' and then does not eat is fined one gold <s>māṣaka</s>.
And he must give the host twice the amount of food.
One who defiles a Brahmin with forbidden food is fined sixteen <s>suvarṇas</s>.
If he brings about loss of caste, the fine is one hundred.
If he does so with liquor, he is liable to death.
For defiling a Kṣatriya, the fine is half of that.
For defiling a Vaiśya, it is again half of that.
For defiling a Śūdra, the fine is the first <s>sāhasa</s>.

children.text: aspṛśyaḥ kāmakāreṇa spṛśan spṛśyaṃ traivarṇikaṃ vadhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: An untouchable person who intentionally touches a touchable member of the three higher varṇas is liable to death.
A menstruating woman should be struck with switches.
One who makes impurity near a road, a park, or water is fined one hundred <s>paṇas</s>.
And he must remove it.
One who breaks into a house, a plot, a wall, or the like incurs the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine.
And he must repair it.
One who throws a harmful substance into a house is fined one hundred <s>paṇas</s>.
So too one who denies common property.
And one who, when sent with something, does not deliver it.
And one who abandons a father, son, teacher, sacrificer, or officiating priest, though they have not fallen from status.
He must not abandon them.
So too those who feed Śūdra renunciants at rites for gods or ancestors.
And one who performs work for which he is not fit.
And one who breaks open a chest or a house.
And one who administers an oath without being appointed.
And one who injures the virility of animals.
In a dispute between father and son, the witnesses are fined ten <s>paṇas</s>.
Whoever comes between the two incurs the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine.
So too the maker of false scales and measures.
And one who alleges fraud in scales or measures when there is no fraud.
And the seller of counterfeit goods.
Merchants who combine together and hold back merchandise without setting a price are liable.
So too those who sell it individually.

children.text: gṛhītamūlyaṃ yaḥ paṇyaṃ kretur naiva dadyāt tasyāsau sodayaṃ dāpyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If someone has taken the price but does not give the merchandise to the buyer, he must be made to pay it with increase.
And he is to be fined one hundred <s>paṇas</s> by the king.

children.text: krītam akrīṇato yā hāniḥ sā kretur eva syāt ||
children.translated_text: Whatever loss results when a bought article is not accepted falls on the buyer alone.
For one who sells what the king has forbidden, there is confiscation of that article.

children.text: tarikaḥ sthalajaṃ śulkaṃ gṛhṇan daśapaṇān daṇḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A ferryman who takes a land toll is to be fined ten <s>paṇas</s>.
And a boatman or toll collector who takes a toll from students, forest-dwellers, mendicants, pregnant women, or pilgrims.
And he must give that toll back to them.
In gambling, those who play with false dice have their hands cut off.
Those who gamble by fraud have their pincers cut off.
So too knot-cutters.
And snatchers have their hands cut off.

children.text: divā paśūnāṃ vṛkādyupaghāte pāle tv anāyati pāladoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If cattle are injured by wolves or the like during the day, and the herdsman does not bring them in, the fault belongs to the herdsman.
He must also give the owner the value of the lost animal.
One who milks an animal without permission is fined twenty-five <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.

children.text: mahiṣī cet sasyanāśaṃ kuryāt tatpālas tv aṣṭau māṣān daṇḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If a buffalo damages crops, its herdsman is fined eight <s>māṣas</s>.
If it is without a herdsman, the owner is fined.
The same applies if it is a horse, a camel, or a donkey.
If it is a cow, the fine is half of that.
For goats and sheep it is half of that again.
If they have eaten and then lain down, the fine is doubled.
In every case, the value of the destroyed crop is to be paid to the owner.
There is no fault on a road, in a village, or at the edge of a pasture.
Nor in an unenclosed place.
Nor when the time is brief.
Nor in the case of released bulls and cows that have recently calved.

children.text: yas tūttamavarṇān dāsye niyojayet tasyottamasāhaso daṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If someone employs members of higher varṇas in slavery, his fine is the highest <s>sāhasa</s>.
One who has abandoned renunciation must perform slave-service for the king.

children.text: bhṛtakaś cāpūrṇe kāle bhṛtiṃ tyajan sakalam eva mūlyaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: A hired worker who abandons his hire before the term is complete must pay the entire value.
And he must give one hundred <s>paṇas</s> to the king.
Whatever is lost through his fault must be paid to the owner.
Except when the loss is caused by divine calamity.

children.text: svāmī cet bhṛtakam apūrṇe kāle jahyāt tasya sarvam eva mūlyaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If the master dismisses a hired worker before the term is complete, he must pay him the whole amount.
And he must pay one hundred <s>paṇas</s> to the king.
Except when there is fault on the hired worker's part.

children.text: yaḥ kanyāṃ pūrvadattām anyasmai dadyāt sa cauravac chāsyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who gives to another a girl previously given in marriage is to be punished like a thief.
Except when there is a defect in the bridegroom.
So too one who abandons a faultless woman.
And one who abandons a wife.

children.text: ajānānaḥ prakāśaṃ yaḥ paradravyaṃ krīṇīyāt tatra tasya na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, not knowing, someone buys another's property openly, in that case there is no fault for him.
The owner should obtain the property.

children.text: yady aprakāśaṃ hīnamūlyaṃ ca krīṇīyāt tadā kretā vikretā ca cauravac chāsyau ||
children.translated_text: But if he buys it secretly and at a deficient price, then the buyer and the seller are both to be punished like thieves.
One who carries off the property of a corporate group is to be banished.
And so is one who violates its agreement.
One who has carried off a deposit is to be made to pay the owner the money together with the increase of its value.
And he is to be punished by the king like a thief.
And so is one who says of what was not deposited, 'It was deposited.'

children.text: sīmābhettāram uttamasāhasaṃ daṇḍayitvā punaḥ sīmāṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: After fining a boundary-breaker with the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine, the king should have the boundary made again.
One who eats forbidden food that causes loss of caste is to be banished.
A seller of what is forbidden and not to be sold, and a breaker of an image of a deity, are to be fined the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine.
A physician acting falsely in the case of persons of the highest rank is liable to the highest fine.
In the case of persons of the middle rank, to the middle fine.
In the case of animals, to the first fine.
One who does not give what he has promised is to be made to give it, and is to be fined the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.
False witnesses should have all their property confiscated.
And so should assessors who live on bribes.

children.text: gocarmamātrādhikāṃ bhuvam anyasyādhīkṛtāṃ tasmād anirmocyānyasya yaḥ prayacchet sa vadhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who gives to another land exceeding the measure of a <s>gocarma</s>, which has been pledged to someone else, without redeeming it from that person, is liable to death.
But if it is less, he is to be fined sixteen <s>suvarṇas</s>.

children.text: eko 'śnīyād yad utpannaṃ naraḥ saṃvatsaraṃ phalam
children.translated_text: The land from which one man alone would eat the produce that arises for a year

children.text: gocarmamātrā sā kṣoṇī stokā vā yadi vā bahu ||
children.translated_text: is that measure called a <s>gocarma</s>, whether it is small or large.

children.text: yayor nikṣipta ādhis tau vivadetāṃ yadā narau
children.translated_text: When two men dispute over a pledge deposited between them,

children.text: yasya bhuktiḥ phalaṃ tasya balāt kāraṃ vinā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the fruit belongs to the one whose enjoyment of it was made without force.

children.text: sāgamena tu bhogena bhuktaṃ samyag yadā tu yat
children.translated_text: But when something has been properly enjoyed through possession accompanied by title,

children.text: āhartā labhate tatra nāpahāryaṃ tu tat kvacit ||
children.translated_text: the taker obtains it in that case, and it is never to be taken away.

children.text: pitrā bhuktaṃ tu yad dravyaṃ bhuktyācāreṇa dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: But property that was enjoyed by the father according to lawful usage through possession

children.text: tasmin prete na vācyo 'sau bhuktyā prāptaṃ hi tasya tat ||
children.translated_text: is not to be challenged after his death; for it has come to him by possession.

children.text: tribhir eva tu yā bhuktā puruṣair bhūr yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Land that has been enjoyed according to rule by three generations
is obtained there by the fourth, even in the absence of a written document.
In the killing of creatures with claws, with horns, and with fangs, of assailants,

children.text: hastyaśvānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ vadhe hantā na doṣabhāk ||
children.translated_text: and likewise of elephants, horses, and others, the killer is not guilty.

children.text: guruṃ vā bālavṛddhau vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā bahuśrutam
children.translated_text: Whether it is a teacher, a child or an old man, or a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
if he comes as an assailant, one should kill him without hesitation.
There is no fault at all for the killer in killing an assailant,

children.text: prakāśaṃ vāprakāśaṃ vā manyus tanmanyum ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: whether openly or secretly; wrath meets that very wrath.
One with a raised sword, poison, or fire, and likewise one whose hand is raised to curse,
one who kills by <s>Atharvan</s> rites, and a slanderous informer before kings,
and one who transgresses with another's wife: these are to be known as the seven assailants.
Others who take away reputation and wealth are said to be takers of <s>dharma</s> and material welfare.

children.text: uddeśatas te kathito dhare daṇḍavidhir mayā
children.translated_text: I have told you, O <s>Dharā</s>, the rule of punishment in summary,
for the detailed account of all offenses is exceedingly extensive.

children.text: aparādheṣu cānyeṣu jñātvā jātiṃ dhanaṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: In other offenses also, after considering caste, wealth, and age,

children.text: daṇḍaṃ prakalpayed rājā saṃmantrya brāhmaṇaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: the king should determine the fine in consultation with <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text: daṇḍyaṃ pramocayan daṇḍyād dviguṇaṃ daṇḍam āvahet
children.translated_text: A base man who releases one who deserves punishment should incur a fine twice that of the punishable person,
and so also an appointed officer who inflicts punishment on those who should not be punished.

children.text: yasya cauraḥ pure nāsti nānyastrīgo na duṣṭavāk
children.translated_text: The king in whose city there is no thief, no man who goes to another's wife, no foul speaker,
and no violent offender or destroyer of punishment, shares in the world of <s>Śakra</s>.
Then the creditor should take from the debtor the property exactly as it was given.

children.text: dvikaṃ trikaṃ catuṣkaṃ pañcakaṃ ca śataṃ varṇānukrameṇa pratimāsam ||
children.translated_text: Two, three, four, and five per hundred, according to the order of the <s>varṇas</s>, is the monthly interest.

children.text: sarve varṇā vā svapratipannāṃ vṛddhiṃ dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or all <s>varṇas</s> should pay the interest to which they have agreed.
Even if it has not been agreed upon, after the passage of a year they should pay it as prescribed.
There is no interest when a pledge is being enjoyed.

children.text: daivarājopaghātād ṛte vinaṣṭam ādhim uttamarṇo dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Except in the case of damage by divine or royal action, the creditor should replace a pledge that has been lost.
Even when the interest has reached its limit.
An immovable pledge is not to be taken, except by express statement.

children.text: gṛhītadhanapraveśārtham eva yat sthāvaraṃ dattaṃ tat gṛhītadhanapraveśe dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Whatever immovable property was given only for the purpose of securing the entry of money received, he should give back when the received money is entered as paid.

children.text: dīyamānaṃ prayuktam artham uttamarṇasyāgṛhṇatas tataḥ paraṃ na vardhate ||
children.translated_text: When the money lent is being offered, if the creditor does not accept it, from then on it does not increase.
The highest increase of gold is double.
Of grain, triple.
Of cloth, fourfold.
Of liquids, eightfold.
For women and cattle, the increase is their offspring.
For yeast, cotton thread, leather, weapons, bricks, and charcoal, the increase is without limit.
For things not mentioned, it is double.

children.text: prayuktam arthaṃ yathā kathaṃcit sādhayan na rājño vācyaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: A man who recovers lent money by any means whatever should not be censured by the king.

children.text: sādhyamānaś ced rājānam abhigacchet tatsamaṃ daṇḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if one from whom it is being recovered goes to the king, he is to be fined an amount equal to it.

children.text: uttamarṇaś ced rājānam iyāt tadvibhāvito 'dhamarṇo rājñe dhanadaśabhāgasaṃmitaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If the creditor goes to the king, and the debtor is proved liable for it, the debtor should give the king a fine equal to a tenth part of the money.
And the creditor, once he has obtained the money, should give a twentieth part.
One who denies everything, even if proved liable for only one part, should pay everything.

children.text: tasya ca bhāvanās tisro bhavanti likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaḥ samayakriyā ca ||
children.translated_text: His proofs are three: a written document, witnesses, and a formal act of agreement.
What has been received with witnesses should be given back only with witnesses.
When the matter has been entered in writing, he should have the written document read aloud.
In the case of incomplete payment, and when the document is not present, the creditor should give a writing in his own hand.

children.text: dhanagrāhiṇi prete pravrajite dvidaśāḥ samāḥ pravasite vā tatputrapautrair dhanaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: When the receiver of money has died, become an ascetic, or gone abroad for twenty years, the money is to be paid by his sons and grandsons.
After that, it is not to be demanded from them if they are unwilling.

children.text: saputrasya vāpy aputrasya vā rikthagrāhī ṛṇaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Whether a man has sons or has no sons, the heir who takes the estate must pay the debt.
For a man without property, the man who takes his wife must pay it.
A wife is not liable for what was contracted by her husband or son.
Nor are a husband and sons liable for what was contracted by a wife.
Nor is a father liable for what was contracted by a son.

children.text: avibhaktaiḥ kṛtam ṛṇaṃ yas tiṣṭhet sa dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: A debt contracted by undivided family members must be paid by the one who remains.
The same applies to paternal debt among undivided brothers.
And if they have divided, each must pay a share according to his inheritance.
The husband must pay for women who are cowherds, distillers, actors, washerwomen, or hunters.
What has been accepted by verbal promise is not non-payable for anyone.
And the same applies to what was contracted for the sake of the household.

children.text: yo gṛhītvā ṛṇaṃ sarvaṃ śvo dāsyāmīti sāmakam
children.translated_text: If a man, after taking a debt with interest, says, 'I will pay tomorrow,'

children.text: na dadyāllobhataḥ paścāt tathā vṛddhim avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and later, from greed, does not pay it, he incurs the interest accordingly.
Suretyship is prescribed for appearance, for assurance, and for payment.

children.text: ādyau tu vitathe dāpyāvitarasya sutā api ||
children.translated_text: If the first two fail, the sureties are to be made to pay; in the case of the other, even the sons are liable.

children.text: bahavaś cet pratibhuvo dadyus te 'rthaṃ yathākṛtam
children.translated_text: If there are many sureties, they should pay the sum according to what was agreed.
But when the sum has not been specified among them, the proceeding follows the creditor's choice.
Whatever amount a surety pays, being pressed by the creditor,

children.text: ṛṇikas taṃ pratibhuve dviguṇaṃ dātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: the debtor ought to pay that amount twofold to the surety.
Now a document is of three kinds.
It may be witnessed by the king, witnessed by ordinary witnesses, or unwitnessed.
A document made in the royal court by the appointed scribe and marked by the hand of its superintendent is witnessed by the king.

children.text: yatra kvacana yena kenacillikhitaṃ sākṣibhiḥ svahastacihnitaṃ sasākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: One written anywhere by anyone, and marked by the witnesses' own hands, is witnessed by ordinary witnesses.
One written in one's own hand is unwitnessed.
A document made by force is not valid evidence.
Nor are any documents made by fraud.
Nor is one valid, even if witnessed, when it is marked by witnesses corrupt in conduct and testimony.
Nor one written by a scribe of that kind.
Nor one made by a woman, a child, a dependent person, a drunkard, a madman, a frightened person, or one who has been beaten.
A document that is not contrary to local custom, whose authorized marks are clear, and whose sequence and letters are not effaced is valid evidence.

children.text: varṇaiś ca tatkṛtaiś cihnaiḥ patrair eva ca yuktibhiḥ
children.translated_text: A doubtful document should be established by its letters, by marks made by those persons, by other documents, and by reasoned indications,
when these are made to correspond with its evidentiary grounds.

children.text: yatrarṇī dhaniko vāpi sākṣī vā lekhako 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Where the debtor, the creditor, a witness, or even the scribe
has died, there the document should be established by their own handwriting.
Now, those who are not witnesses:

A king, a learned Vedic scholar, an ascetic, a gambler, a thief, a dependent person, a woman, a child, a violent man, a very old man, a drunkard, a madman, one accused of grave sin, a fallen man, one afflicted by hunger or thirst, one in distress, one impassioned, and a blind man are not witnesses.
Nor are enemies, friends, interested parties, relatives, those seen to have faults through forbidden acts, or accomplices.

children.text: anirdiṣṭas tu sākṣitve yaś copetya brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor one who has not been appointed as a witness, or one who comes forward and speaks on his own.
And a single person alone is not a witness.
In cases of theft, violence, verbal penalty, abuse, and seizure of a woman, witnesses are not to be examined for eligibility.
Now, witnesses:

children.text: kulajā vṛttavittasampannā yajvānas tapasvinaḥ putriṇo dharmajñā adhīyānāḥ satyavantas traividyavṛddhāś ca ||
children.translated_text: They should be well-born, endowed with conduct and property, performers of sacrifice, ascetics, men with sons, knowers of <s>dharma</s>, students, truthful men, and elders learned in the three Vedas.
Even one witness is sufficient if he possesses the qualities stated and is accepted by both parties.

children.text: dvayor vivadamānayor yasya pūrvavādas tasya sākṣiṇaḥ praṣṭavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of two litigants, the witnesses of the one whose statement came first should be questioned.

children.text: ādharyaṃ kāryavaśād yatra pūrvapakṣasya bhavet tatra prativādino 'pi ||
children.translated_text: But where, because of the matter at issue, dependence falls on the plaintiff's side, those of the defendant may also be questioned.

children.text: uddiṣṭasākṣiṇi mṛte deśāntaragate ca tadabhihitaśrotāraḥ pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: If an appointed witness has died or gone to another country, those who heard what he said are valid evidence.
A witness is such through seeing directly or through hearing.
Witnesses are purified by truth.
But where the killing of persons of the social orders would result, they are purified by untruth.
For purification from that, a twice-born man should offer ghee into the fire with the <s>Kūśmāṇḍī</s> verses.
A <s>Śūdra</s> should give one day's fodder for ten cows.
One should recognize a false witness from a change in his natural bearing, loss of facial color, and incoherent prattle.
Having summoned the witnesses at sunrise and made them take oaths, he should question them.
He should ask a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, 'Speak.'
He should ask a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, 'Speak the truth.'
He should question a <s>Vaiśya</s> by cows, seed, and gold.
But a <s>Śūdra</s> by all the great sins.
And he should make the witnesses hear this:

children.text: ye mahāpātakināṃ lokā ye copapātakināṃ te kūṭasākṣiṇām api ||
children.translated_text: The worlds that belong to those who commit great sins, and those that belong to those who commit lesser sins, also belong to false witnesses.
And there is the loss of merit accumulated between birth and death.
By truth the sun gives heat.
By truth the moon shines.
By truth the wind blows.
By truth the earth supports.
By truth the waters stand firm.
By truth there is fire.
And by truth there is space.
By truth there are gods.
By truth there are sacrifices.

children.text: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifices and truth, placed on a balance,
indeed truth is superior to a thousand <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifices.

children.text: jānanto 'pi hi ye sākṣye tūṣṇīṃbhūtā udāsate
children.translated_text: Those who know the matter in a testimony but remain silent and indifferent

children.text: te kūṭasākṣiṇāṃ pāpais tulyā daṇḍena cāpy atha
children.translated_text: are equal in sin to false witnesses, and also equal in punishment.

children.text: evaṃ hi sākṣiṇaḥ pṛcched varṇānukramato nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the king should question the witnesses in the order of the social classes.

children.text: yasyocuḥ sākṣiṇaḥ satyāṃ pratijñāṃ sa jayī bhavet
children.translated_text: The man whose true claim the witnesses declare becomes the victor.

children.text: anyathā vādino yasya dhruvas tasya parājayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, defeat is certain for the litigant whose claim is contrary.
When witnesses are divided, the ruler of men should accept the majority.
When they are equal, he should accept those superior in qualities; when qualities are divided equally, the best of the twice-born.

children.text: yasmin yasmin vivāde tu kūṭasākṣyanṛtaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: But in whatever dispute a false witness speaks an untruth...
That particular action should cease, and even what has been done should become as though not done.
Now, the procedure of ordeals agreed upon by stipulation.
In cases of treason against the king and violent assault, it is according to discretion.
In cases concerning deposits and thefts, it is according to the measure of the property.
For all classes of property, one should reckon the value in gold.
There, when it is less than one <s>kṛṣṇala</s>, he should make a <s>śūdra</s> swear with <s>dūrvā</s> grass in his hand.
When it is less than two <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>, with sesame in his hand.
When it is less than three <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>, with silver in his hand.
When it is less than four <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>, with gold in his hand.
When it is less than five <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>, with earth lifted from a furrow in his hand.
When it is less than half a <s>suvarṇa</s>, the <s>kośa</s> ordeal is to be assigned to a <s>śūdra</s>.
Beyond that, according to fitness, one of the ordeals by balance, fire, water, or poison is to be assigned.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, when the property is double, the ordeals agreed upon are as stated.
For a <s>rājanya</s>, when it is triple.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, except for the <s>kośa</s>, when it is quadruple.
One should not assign the <s>kośa</s> ordeal to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
Except in the case of an ordeal bound by an agreement concerning a future time.
In place of the <s>kośa</s>, he should make a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> swear only with earth lifted from a furrow in his hand.

children.text: prāgdṛṣṭadoṣe svalpe 'pyarthe divyānām anyatamam eva kārayet ||
children.translated_text: For one whose fault has been seen before, even in a small matter, he should make him undergo one of the divine ordeals.
For one among good people, known for good conduct, not even in a great matter.
The accuser should stake his head.
And the accused should perform the ordeal.
In cases of treason against the king and violent assault, even without the staking of the head.
For women, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the maimed, the incapable, and the sick, the balance is to be assigned.
And that is when the wind is not blowing.
Fire is not to be assigned to lepers, the incapable, or metalworkers.
Nor in autumn and summer.
Poison is not to be assigned to lepers, those of bilious constitution, or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Nor in the rainy season.

children.text: na śleṣmavyādhyarditānāṃ bhīrūṇāṃ śvāsakāsinām ambujīvināṃ codakam ||
children.translated_text: Water is not to be assigned to those afflicted by phlegmatic disease, the timid, those with asthma or cough, or those who live by water.
Nor in winter and the cold season.
The <s>kośa</s> ordeal is not to be assigned to atheists.
Nor in a country afflicted by disease, epidemic, or disorder.
Having summoned him at sunrise, bathed with his clothes on and fasting,
he should cause all ordeals to be performed in the presence of gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Now, the balance.
It should be four hastas high and two hastas long.
There the balance, made from sound wood and five hastas long, should have slings on both sides.
And either a goldsmith or a bronze-worker should hold it.

children.text: tatra caikasmin śikye puruṣaṃ divyakāriṇam āropayet dvitīye pratimānaṃ śilādi ||
children.translated_text: There, on one sling he should place the man undergoing the ordeal, and on the second a counterweight, such as a stone.

children.text: pratimānapuruṣau samadhṛtau sucihnitau kṛtvā puruṣam avatārayet ||
children.translated_text: After making the counterweight and the man equally balanced and well marked, he should make the man descend.
And he should take hold of the balance according to the stipulation.
And also the holder of the balance.

children.text: brahmaghnāṃ ye smṛtā lokā ye lokāḥ kūṭasākṣiṇām
children.translated_text: The worlds that are remembered as belonging to killers of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and the worlds belonging to false witnesses,

children.text: tulādhārasya te lokās tulāṃ dhārayato mṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: those are the worlds of the balance-holder who holds the balance falsely.
By words synonymous with <s>dharma</s> you are called <s>dhaṭa</s>,

children.text: tvam eva dhaṭa jānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you alone, O <s>dhaṭa</s>, know what human beings do not know.
This man, accused in a lawsuit, is weighed upon you;

children.text: tad enaṃ saṃśayād asmād dharmatas trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore you ought, in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, to save him from this doubt.

children.text: tatas tvāropayecchikye bhūya evātha taṃ naram
children.translated_text: Then he should place that man again on the sling,

children.text: tulito yadi vardheta tataḥ śuddhaḥ sa dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and if, when weighed, he rises, then he is pure according to <s>dharma</s>.
If the sling breaks or the axle breaks, he should place the man on it again,

children.text: evaṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ jñānaṃ yato bhavati nirṇayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for in this way certain knowledge arises, from which there is a decision.
Now, fire.
He should make seven circles with an interval of sixteen fingers between them.

children.text: tataḥ prāṅmukhasya prasāritabhujadvayasya saptāśvatthapatrāṇi karayor dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, for him as he faces east with both arms extended, he should place seven <s>aśvattha</s> leaves on his hands.
And he should wrap them, together with both hands, with a thread.

children.text: tatas tatrāgnivarṇaṃ lohapiṇḍaṃ pañcāśatpalikaṃ samaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Then he should place there a red-hot iron ball, even and weighing fifty <s>palas</s>.

children.text: tam ādāya nātidrutaṃ nātivilambitaṃ maṇḍaleṣu pādanyāsaṃ kurvan vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Taking it, he should go, placing his feet in the circles, neither too quickly nor too slowly.

children.text: tataḥ saptamaṃ maṇḍalam atītya bhūmau lohapiṇḍaṃ jahyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, after passing beyond the seventh circle, he should drop the iron ball on the ground.

children.text: yo hastayoḥ kvacid dagdhas tam aśuddhaṃ vinirdiśet
children.translated_text: If he is burned anywhere on his hands, one should declare him impure;

children.text: na dagdhaḥ sarvathā yas tu sa viśuddho bhaven naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the man who is not burned in any way becomes pure.

children.text: bhayād vā pātayed yas tu dagdho vā na vibhāvyate
children.translated_text: But if he drops it out of fear, or if it cannot be determined whether he has been burned,
he should make him carry the iron again, because the ordeal has not been cleared.
At the very beginning he should inspect his hands after they have been rubbed with rice grains.
After consecrating his hands with mantra, he should then place the iron ball in them.

children.text: tvam agne sarvabhūtānām antaś carasi sākṣivat
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, you move within all beings like a witness;

children.text: tvam evāgne vijānīṣe na vidur yāni mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you alone, O <s>Agni</s>, know what human beings do not know.
This man, accused in a lawsuit, desires purification;

children.text: tad enaṃ saṃśayād asmād dharmatas trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore you ought, in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, to save him from this doubt.
Now, water.
It should be in water free from mud, moss, dangerous aquatic creatures, fish, leeches, and the like.

children.text: tatrānābhimagnasyārogadveṣiṇaḥ puruṣasyānyasya jānunī gṛhītvābhimantritam ambhaḥ praviśet ||
children.translated_text: There, having taken the knees of another man who is immersed up to the navel, healthy, and not hostile, he should enter the consecrated water.

children.text: tatsamakālaṃ ca nātikrūramṛdunā dhanuṣā puruṣo 'paraḥ śarakṣepaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: At that same time another man should shoot an arrow with a bow that is neither too strong nor too weak.

children.text: taṃ cāparaḥ puruṣo javena śaram ānayet ||
children.translated_text: And another man should bring back that arrow swiftly.

children.text: tanmadhye yo na dṛśyeta sa śuddhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: The one who is not seen during that interval is declared pure;
otherwise he is impure, if even a single limb is seen.
O water, you move within all beings like a witness;

children.text: tvam evāmbho vijānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you alone, O water, know what human beings do not know.
This man, accused in a lawsuit, sinks in you.

children.text: tad enaṃ saṃśayād asmād dharmatas trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you ought, in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, to save him from this doubt.
Now, the poison ordeal.
No poisons at all are to be given,
except the <s>śārṅga</s> poison that originates in <s>Himācala</s>.

children.text: tasya ca yavasaptakaṃ ghṛtaplutam abhiśastāya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Seven barley-grains of it, soaked in ghee, should be given to the accused man.
If the poison is easily digested, without violent distress or exhaustion,

children.text: viśuddhaṃ tam iti jñātvā divasānte visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: then, knowing him to be purified, one should release him at the end of the day.
Because you are poison and because you are dangerous, you are cruel to all embodied beings;

children.text: tvam eva viṣa jānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you alone, O poison, know the things that human beings do not know.
This man, accused in a lawsuit, seeks purification;

children.text: tad enaṃ saṃśayād asmād dharmatas trātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: therefore you ought, in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, to save him from this doubt.
Now, the <s>kośa</s> ordeal.

children.text: ugrān devān samabhyarcya tatsnānodakāt prasṛtitrayaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped fierce deities, he should drink three handfuls from the water in which they have been bathed.

children.text: idaṃ mayā na kṛtam iti vadan sthāpitadevatābhimukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should say, 'This was not done by me,' while facing the installed deity.

children.text: yasya paśyed dvisaptāhāt trisaptāhād athāpi vā
children.translated_text: If, within two weeks or even within three weeks, one should see in him
disease, fire, the death of a relative, or even alarm from the king,

children.text: tam aśuddhaṃ vijānīyāt tathā śuddhaṃ viparyaye
children.translated_text: one should know him to be impure; in the opposite case, one should know him to be pure.

children.text: divye ca śuddhaṃ puruṣaṃ satkuryād dhārmiko nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in a divine ordeal, a righteous king should honor the man who is pure.
Now, there are twelve kinds of sons.

children.text: svakṣetre saṃskṛtāyām utpāditaḥ svayam aurasaḥ prathamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first is the <s>aurasa</s>, personally begotten in one's own field, on a wife who has been ritually married.
The second is the <s>kṣetraja</s>, begotten on an appointed wife by a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> kinsman or by a man of higher varṇa.
The third is the son of an appointed daughter, the <s>putrikāputra</s>.

children.text: yas tv asyāḥ putraḥ sa me putro bhaved iti yā pitrā dattā sā putrikā ||
children.translated_text: A daughter given by her father with the intention, 'The son she bears shall be my son,' is a <s>putrikā</s>.
Even without the formal rule for a <s>putrikā</s>, a daughter who has been assigned and has no brother is herself a <s>putrikā</s>.
The fourth is the <s>paunarbhava</s>, the son of a remarried woman.
A woman who, while still untouched, is ritually married again is a <s>punarbhū</s>.
Still more so is one who, even without a new rite, formerly belonged to another man.
The fifth is the <s>kānīna</s>.
He is begotten in his father's house by an unmarried woman.
And he belongs to the man who takes her hand in marriage.
One secretly born in the house is the sixth.
He belongs to the man in whose bed he is born.
The seventh is the <s>sahoḍha</s>.
He is the son of a woman who is ritually married while pregnant.
And he belongs to the man who takes her hand in marriage.
The eighth is the <s>dattaka</s>, the given son.
He is the one given by his mother and father to someone.
The ninth is the bought son.
He belongs to the man by whom he is bought.
The tenth is the self-offered son.
He belongs to the man whom he approaches.
The eleventh, however, is the cast-off son.
He has been abandoned by his father and mother.
And he belongs to the man by whom he is taken in.
The twelfth is one begotten anywhere at all.
Of these, each earlier one is superior to each later one.
He alone is the taker of the inheritance.
And he should support the others.
For those who are unmarried, he should perform the rites according to his own wealth.
Those who are fallen, impotent, afflicted by incurable disease, or disabled do not take shares.
They must be supported by those who receive the estate.
And their <s>aurasa</s> sons do take shares.
But not the son of one who is fallen.
When an act causing fall has been committed, those born afterward are excluded.
And those born from women in inverse-varṇa unions do not receive shares.
Their sons do not share even in the paternal grandfather's property.
They are to be maintained by those who receive shares.
The one who takes the property is the one who gives the <s>piṇḍa</s> offering.

children.text: ekoḍhānām apyekasyāḥ putraḥ sarvāsāṃ putra eva ||
children.translated_text: Even among women married to one man, the son of one is the son of them all.
And the same holds among brothers of the same birth.
A son should give the <s>piṇḍa</s> offering even if he does not obtain his father's wealth.

children.text: punnāmno narakād yasmāt pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Because a son saves his father from the hell named <s>Puṃ</s>,

children.text: tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ svayam eva svayaṃbhuvā ||
children.translated_text: therefore he is called <s>putra</s>, as <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> himself has declared.

children.text: ṛṇam asmin saṃnayaty amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati
children.translated_text: A father places his debt in him and attains immortality,
if, while living, he sees the face of his son once born.
Through a son he conquers the worlds; through a grandson he obtains endlessness;
and through the son's grandson he reaches the realm of the sun.
In this world no distinction is established between a son's son and a daughter's son;
for a daughter's son also carries across a sonless man, just like a son's son.
Sons born from women of the same varṇa are of the same varṇa.
In regular anuloma unions, they have the mother's varṇa.
In inverse pratiloma unions, they are condemned by the Āryas.
There, the son of a <s>Vaiśyā</s> woman by a <s>Śūdra</s> man is an <s>Āyogava</s>.
The <s>Pulkasa</s> and the <s>Māgadha</s> are sons of <s>Kṣatriyā</s> women by <s>Vaiśya</s> and <s>Śūdra</s> men respectively.
And <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, <s>Vaidehaka</s>, and <s>Sūta</s> are sons of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> woman by <s>Śūdra</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Kṣatriya</s> men respectively.
Mixtures of mixtures are innumerable.
Going on stage is the occupation of the <s>Āyogavas</s>.
Hunting is the occupation of the <s>Pulkasas</s>.
The work of praise is the occupation of the <s>Māgadhas</s>.
Being executioners is the occupation of the <s>Caṇḍālas</s>.
Guarding women and living from that is the occupation of the <s>Vaidehakas</s>.
Driving horses and chariots is the occupation of the <s>Sūtas</s>.

children.text: caṇḍālānāṃ bahir grāmanivasanaṃ mṛtacailadhāraṇam iti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, the special rule is living outside the village and wearing the clothes of the dead.
And for all of them, marriage is with people of the same caste.
And they inherit the wealth of their own fathers.
These castes, born from mixture, are indicated through father and mother;

children.text: pracchannā vā prakāśā vā veditavyāḥ svakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether hidden or manifest, they should be recognized by their own occupations.
For the sake of a brahmin or a cow, giving up the body without rites,
and in rescuing women, children, and the like, is a cause of attainment for outsiders.

children.text: pitā cet putrān vibhajet tasya svecchā svayam upārjite 'rthe ||
children.translated_text: If a father divides his sons, his choice prevails regarding wealth acquired by himself.
But in ancestral wealth, father and sons have equal ownership.
Sons divided by their father should give a share to one born after the division.
The wealth of a sonless man goes to his wife.
In its absence, it goes to the daughter.
In her absence, it goes to the father.
In his absence, it goes to the mother.
In her absence, it goes to the brother.
In his absence, it goes to the brother's son.
In his absence, it goes to a kinsman.
In his absence, it goes to one of the same family line.
In his absence, it goes to a fellow student.
In his absence, it goes to the king, except for the wealth of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s property belongs to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
The teacher should take the wealth of a forest-dweller.
Or the pupil may take it.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭinas tu saṃsṛṣṭī sodarasya tu sodaraḥ
children.translated_text: But for one who has reunited, a reunited relative, and for a full brother, a full brother,

children.text: dadyād apahareccāṃśaṃ jātasya ca mṛtasya ca ||
children.translated_text: should assign and take the share, whether of one born or of one who has died.

children.text: pitṛmātṛsutabhrātṛdattam adhyagnyupāgatam ādhivedanikaṃ bandhudattaṃ śulkam anvādheyakam iti strīdhanam ||
children.translated_text: What is given by father, mother, son, or brother, what is received before the nuptial fire, the <s>ādhivedanika</s> gift, what is given by relatives, the bride-price, and the <s>anvādheyaka</s> gift: this is <s>strīdhana</s> (a woman's property).
In the four forms of marriage beginning with <s>Brāhma</s>, when a childless woman has died, it belongs to her husband.
But in the remaining forms, the father should take it.

children.text: sarveṣv eva prasūtāyāṃ yaddhanaṃ tat duhitṛgāmi ||
children.translated_text: In every form, when she has borne a child, whatever wealth there is goes to the daughter.

children.text: patyau jīvati yaḥ strībhir alaṃkāro dhṛto bhavet
children.translated_text: An ornament that has been worn by women while the husband is alive

children.text: na taṃ bhajeran dāyādā bhajamānāḥ patanti te ||
children.translated_text: the heirs should not divide; if they divide it, they fall.
For those who have different fathers, the apportionment of shares is according to the father.

children.text: yasya yat paitṛkaṃ rikthaṃ sa tad gṛhṇīta netaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever paternal inheritance belongs to each one, he should take that and not another's.

children.text: brāhmaṇasya caturṣu varṇeṣu cet putrā bhaveyuḥ te paitṛkaṃ rikthaṃ daśadhā vibhajeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has sons among the four <s>varṇas</s>, they should divide the paternal inheritance into ten parts.
There the son of the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> should take four shares.
The son of the <s>kṣatriyā</s> takes three.
The son of the <s>vaiśyā</s> takes two shares.
But the son of the <s>śūdrā</s> takes one.

children.text: atha cet śūdravarjaṃ brāhmaṇasya putratrayaṃ bhavet tadā taddhanaṃ navadhā vibhajeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has three sons excluding the <s>śūdra</s> son, then they should divide that wealth into nine parts.
In the order of the <s>varṇas</s>, they should take shares apportioned as four, three, and two.

children.text: vaiśyavarjam aṣṭadhā kṛtaṃ caturas trīn ekaṃ cādadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>vaiśya</s> son is absent, the wealth is made into eight parts, and they should take four, three, and one.

children.text: kṣatriyavarjam saptadhā kṛtaṃ caturo dvāvekaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>kṣatriya</s> son is absent, the wealth is made into seven parts, and they should take four, two, and one.

children.text: brāhmaṇavarjaṃ ṣaḍdhā kṛtaṃ trīn dvāvekaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> son is absent, the wealth is made into six parts, and they should take three, two, and one.
For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, when there are sons by <s>kṣatriyā</s>, <s>vaiśyā</s>, and <s>śūdrā</s> women, this same division applies.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇakṣatriyau putrau syātāṃ tadā saptadhā kṛtād dhanād brāhmaṇaścaturo 'ṃśān ādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> son and a <s>kṣatriya</s> son, then from wealth divided into seven parts the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should take four shares.
The <s>rājanya</s> should take three.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇavaiśyau tadā ṣaḍdhā vibhaktasya caturo 'ṃśān brāhmaṇas tvādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> son and a <s>vaiśya</s> son, then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should take four shares of the wealth divided into six parts.
The <s>vaiśya</s> takes two shares.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇaśūdrau putrau syātāṃ tadā taddhanam pañcadhā vibhajeyātām ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> son and a <s>śūdra</s> son, then the two should divide that wealth into five parts.
The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should take four shares.
The <s>śūdra</s> takes one.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya vā kṣatriyavaiśyau putrau syātāṃ tadā taddhanaṃ pañcadhā vibhajeyātām ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or a <s>kṣatriya</s> has a <s>kṣatriya</s> son and a <s>vaiśya</s> son, then the two should divide that wealth into five parts.
The <s>kṣatriya</s> should take three shares.
The <s>vaiśya</s> takes two shares.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya vā kṣatriyaśūdrau putrau syātāṃ tadā taddhanaṃ caturdhā vibhajeyātām ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or a <s>kṣatriya</s> has a <s>kṣatriya</s> son and a <s>śūdra</s> son, then the two should divide that wealth into four parts.
The <s>kṣatriya</s> should take three shares.
The <s>śūdra</s> takes one.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya vaiśyasya vā vaiśyaśūdrau putrau syātāṃ tadā taddhanaṃ tridhā vibhajeyātām ||
children.translated_text: Now, if a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, or a <s>vaiśya</s> has a <s>vaiśya</s> son and a <s>śūdra</s> son, then the two should divide that wealth into three parts.
The <s>vaiśya</s> should take two shares.
The <s>śūdra</s> takes one.
Now, when they are sole sons, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, and <s>vaiśya</s> sons of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> take the whole estate.
For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, the <s>rājanya</s> and <s>vaiśya</s> sons do so.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, the <s>vaiśya</s> son does so.
For a <s>śūdra</s>, the <s>śūdra</s> son does so.
But for twice-born men, a single <s>śūdra</s> son takes half.
The rule that applies to the estate of a sonless man applies here to the other half.
Mothers take shares in accordance with their sons' shares.
And so do unmarried daughters.
Sons of the same <s>varṇa</s> should take equal shares.
They should give the eldest the best portion as an extra allotment.

children.text: yadi dvau brāhmaṇīputrau syātām ekaḥ śūdrāputraḥ tadā navadhā vibhaktasyārthasya brāhmaṇīputrāv aṣṭau bhāgān ādadyātām ekaṃ śūdrāputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: If there are two sons of a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> and one son of a <s>śūdrā</s>, then, of the property divided into nine parts, the two <s>brāhmaṇī</s> sons should take eight shares and the <s>śūdrā</s> son one.

children.text: atha śūdrāputrāvubhau syātām eko brāhmaṇīputraḥ tadā ṣaḍdhā vibhaktasyārthasya caturo 'ṃśān brāhmaṇas tvādadyāt dvāvaṃśau śūdrāputrau ||
children.translated_text: Now, if both are sons of a <s>śūdrā</s> and one is the son of a <s>brāhmaṇī</s>, then, of the property divided into six parts, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should take four shares and the two <s>śūdra</s> sons two shares.
By this rule, the apportionment of shares also takes place in other cases.

children.text: vibhaktāḥ saha jīvanto vibhajeran punar yadi
