children.translated_text: Those who, after having divided, live together and then divide again,

children.text: samas tatra vibhāgaḥ syājjyaiṣṭhyaṃ tatra na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: in their case the division should be equal; seniority has no place there.
Whatever one acquires by labor without diminishing the father's property,

children.text: svayam īhitalabdhaṃ tan nākāmo dātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: that, being obtained by his own effort, he need not give if he does not wish to.

children.text: paitṛkaṃ tu yadā dravyam anavāptaṃ yad āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: But when he obtains ancestral property that had not previously been recovered,

children.text: na tat putrair bhajet sārdham akāmaḥ svayam arjitam ||
children.translated_text: he need not share it with his sons if unwilling, since it was acquired by himself.

children.text: vastraṃ patram alaṃkāraḥ kṛtānnam udakaṃ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Clothing, vessels, ornaments, prepared food, water, and women,

children.text: yogakṣemaṃ pracāraś ca na vibhājyaṃ ca pustakam ||
children.translated_text: means of support, instruments of movement, and a book are not to be divided.
A dead twice-born man should not be carried out by a <s>śūdra</s>.
Nor should a <s>śūdra</s> be carried out by a twice-born man.
Sons should carry out their father and mother.
<s>Śūdras</s> should not carry out a twice-born man, even if he is their father.

children.text: brāhmaṇam anāthaṃ ye brāhmaṇā nirharanti te svargalokabhājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who carry out an orphaned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> share in the world of heaven.

children.text: nirhṛtya ca bāndhavaṃ pretaṃ saṃṣkṛtyāpradakṣiṇena citām abhigamyāpsu savāsaso nimajjanaṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after carrying out the dead kinsman and performing the funeral rites, they should approach the pyre in a counterclockwise direction and immerse themselves in water with their clothes on.
After making the water-offering for the dead, they should place one <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral rice-ball) on kuśa grass.

children.text: parivartitavāsasaś ca nimbapatrāṇi vidaśya dvāryaśmani padanyāsaṃ kṛtvā gṛhaṃ praviśeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having changed their garments, bitten neem leaves, and set foot on a stone at the doorway, they should enter the house.
And they should throw unbroken grains into the fire.
On the fourth day they should gather the bones.
Those bones should be cast into the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: yāvatsaṃkhyam asthi puruṣasya gaṅgāmbhasi tiṣṭhati tāvad varṣasahasrāṇi svargalokam adhitiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: For as many bones of a man as remain in the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, for that many thousands of years he dwells in the heavenly world.

children.text: yāvad āśaucaṃ tāvat pretasyodakaṃ piṇḍam ekaṃ ca dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the impurity lasts, they should give water and one <s>piṇḍa</s> for the dead.
They should live on food obtained by purchase.
And they should eat no meat.
They should sleep on the bare ground.
And they should sleep separately.

children.text: grāmānniṣkramyāśaucānte kṛtaśmaśrukarmāṇas tilakalkaiḥ sarṣapakalkair vā snātāḥ parivartitavāsaso gṛhaṃ praviśeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the impurity, having gone out of the village, had their beards and hair attended to, bathed with paste of sesame or paste of mustard, and changed their garments, they should enter the house.

children.text: tatra śāntiṃ kṛtvā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca pūjanaṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, after performing a rite of appeasement, they should honor the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
The gods are invisible deities; the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are visible deities.
The worlds are upheld by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
By the favor of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the deities remain in heaven.

children.text: brāhmaṇābhihitaṃ vākyaṃ na mithyā jāyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: A statement uttered by <s>brāhmaṇas</s> never becomes false at any time.

children.text: yad brāhmaṇās tuṣṭatamā vadanti tad devatāḥ pratyabhinandayanti
children.translated_text: What the most satisfied <s>brāhmaṇas</s> say, that the deities gladly approve.

children.text: tuṣṭeṣu tuṣṭāḥ satataṃ bhavanti pratyakṣadeveṣu parokṣadevāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the visible deities are satisfied, the invisible deities are always satisfied.
Those of undepressed spirit should console people afflicted with grief for dead relatives,

children.text: vākyais tu yair bhūmi tavābhidhāsye vākyānyahaṃ tāni mano'bhirāme ||
children.translated_text: with those words, O lovely-minded one, with which, O Earth, I shall speak to you; those words I shall tell.
What is the northern course of the sun is the day of the gods.
The southern course is their night.
A year is their day and night.
By thirty of these, months are formed.
Twelve months make a year.
Twelve hundred divine years make the <s>Kaliyuga</s>.
The <s>Dvāpara</s> is twice that.
The <s>Tretā</s> is three times that.
The <s>Kṛtayuga</s> is four times that.
Twelve thousand divine years make a <s>caturyuga</s> (cycle of four ages).
Seventy-one <s>caturyugas</s> make a <s>manvantara</s>.
And a thousand <s>caturyugas</s> make a <s>kalpa</s>.
That is a day of <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
And his night is of the same length.

children.text: evaṃvidhenāhorātreṇa māsavarṣagaṇanayā sarvasyaiva brahmaṇo varṣaśatam āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By such a day and night, and by the reckoning of months and years, the whole lifetime of <s>Brahmā</s> is one hundred years.
And by the lifetime of <s>Brahmā</s> a day of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is bounded.
At its end comes a great <s>kalpa</s>.
His night is just as long.
There is no number at all of the days and nights of the <s>Puruṣa</s> that have passed.
Nor is there any number of those that will be in the future.
For time has neither beginning nor end.
Thus, in this unsupported time, which moves on continually,

children.text: na tadbhūtaṃ prapaśyāmi sthitir yasya bhaved dhruvā ||
children.translated_text: I do not see any being whose stability could be fixed.

children.text: gaṅgāyāḥ sikatā dhārās tathā varṣati vāsave
children.translated_text: The sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and the streams that <s>Vāsava</s> rains down,

children.text: śakyā gaṇayituṃ loke na vyatītāḥ pitāmahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: may be counted in the world, but the past <s>Pitāmahas</s> cannot be counted.
In each <s>kalpa</s>, fourteen lords of the gods perish,
and also the fourteen <s>Manus</s>, chiefs of all the worlds.
Many thousands of <s>Indras</s> and tens of thousands of chiefs of the demons
have been destroyed here by time; what then is to be said of human beings?

children.text: rājarṣayaś ca bahavaḥ sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: And many royal seers, endowed together with every virtue,

children.text: devā brahmarṣayaś caiva kālena nidhanaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as gods and brahmanical seers, have gone to their end through time.
Those who are capable in this world of causing creation and destruction

children.text: te 'pi kālena nīyante kālo hi duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are themselves led away by time; for time is hard to overcome.

children.text: ākramya sarvaḥ kālena paralokaṃ ca nīyate
children.translated_text: Everyone is overtaken by time and is led to the next world.
A creature is under the power of the bond of <s>karma</s>; what room is there for lamentation there?

children.text: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca
children.translated_text: For one who is born, death is certain; and for one who has died, birth is certain.
In this matter, hard to avoid, there is no help in the world.
Since people who grieve do not help the dead person here,

children.text: ato na roditavyaṃ hi kriyā kāryā svaśaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore one should not weep; the rite should be performed according to one's ability.

children.text: sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cobhau sahāyau yasya gacchataḥ
children.translated_text: Merit and demerit are the two companions that go with a person.

children.text: bāndhavais tasya kiṃ kāryaṃ śocadbhir atha vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: What use are grieving relatives to him, whether they grieve or not?

children.text: bāndhavānām aśauce tu sthitiṃ preto na vindati
children.translated_text: During the impurity of his relatives the dead person does not find a resting-place.
Therefore he comes precisely to those who give him <s>piṇḍa</s> and water.

children.text: arvāk sapiṇdīkaraṇāt preto bhavati yo mṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Before the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> (joining with the ancestors), the person who has died is a <s>preta</s>.
To the one who has gone to the <s>pretaloka</s>, give food together with a water-pot.
And when he has gone to the <s>pitṛloka</s>, he eats, in the <s>śrāddha</s>, food equal to <s>svadhā</s>.
Therefore give <s>śrāddha</s> for this one who has gone to the <s>pitṛloka</s>.
Whether in divine state, in a place of torment, or likewise in an animal womb,

children.text: mānuṣye ca tathāpnoti śrāddhaṃ dattaṃ svabāndhavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise in human birth, he receives the <s>śrāddha</s> given by his own relatives.

children.text: pretasya śrāddhakartuś ca puṣṭiḥ śrāddhe kṛte dhruvam
children.translated_text: For the dead person and for the performer of the <s>śrāddha</s>, nourishment is certain when <s>śrāddha</s> has been performed.

children.text: tasmācchrāddhaṃ sadā kāryaṃ śokaṃ tyaktvā nirarthakam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>śrāddha</s> should always be performed, after abandoning useless grief.

children.text: etāvad eva kartavyaṃ sadā pretasya bandhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: This alone is always to be done by the relatives for the dead person:

children.text: nopakuryān naraḥ śocan pretasyātmana eva ca ||
children.translated_text: a man who grieves does not help either the dead person or himself.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokam anākrandaṃ mriyamāṇāṃś ca bāndhavān
children.translated_text: Seeing that the world is without one to cry out for help, and seeing relatives dying,

children.text: dharmam ekaṃ sahāyārthaṃ varayadhvaṃ sadā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: always choose <s>dharma</s> alone, O people, as your companion.

children.text: mṛto 'pi bāndhavaḥ śakto nānugantuṃ naraṃ mṛtam
children.translated_text: Even a dead relative, though willing, is not able to follow a man who has died.

children.text: jāyāvarjaṃ hi sarvasya yāmyaḥ panthā virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: For everyone, except one's wife, the path belonging to <s>Yama</s> is obstructed.
<s>Dharma</s> alone follows this person wherever he may go.
In this human world there is no waiting for a proper occasion; perform <s>dharma</s> without delay.

children.text: śvaḥ kāryam adya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇikam
children.translated_text: What is to be done tomorrow one should do today, and what is for the afternoon in the forenoon.

children.text: na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ vāsya na vākṛtam ||
children.translated_text: For death does not wait, whether this person's work has been done or has not been done.
Death finds a person attached to fields, shops, and houses, whose mind has gone elsewhere,
and carries him off, like a she-wolf coming upon a sheep.

children.text: na kālasya priyaḥ kaścid dveṣyaś cāsya na vidyate
children.translated_text: No one is dear to Time, and no one is hated by it.

children.text: āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe prasahya harate janam ||
children.translated_text: When life-span and karma have run out, it seizes a person by force.
One whose time has not arrived does not die, even when pierced by a hundred arrows.
One whose time has arrived does not live, even when merely touched by the tip of <s>kuśa</s> grass.

children.text: nauṣadhāni na mantrāś ca na homā na punar japāḥ
children.translated_text: Medicines do not save him, nor mantras, nor oblations, nor again recitations,
a human being who has been reached by death or by old age.
Even with hundreds of precautions one is unable to ward off a coming misfortune.

children.text: na nivārayituṃ śaktas tatra kā paridevanā ||
children.translated_text: What room is there, then, for lamentation?
As a calf finds its mother among thousands of cows,

children.text: tathā pūrvakṛtaṃ karma kartāraṃ vindate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: so a deed done before surely finds its doer.
Beings have unmanifest beginnings, and then a manifest middle,
and indeed unmanifest endings; what room is there for lamentation in that?

children.text: dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā
children.translated_text: Just as, in this body, the embodied one has childhood, youth, and old age,

children.text: tathā dehāntaraprāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati ||
children.translated_text: so there is the attainment of another body; the wise person is not bewildered by that.

children.text: gṛhṇātīha yathā vastraṃ tyaktvā pūrvadhṛtaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a man here takes up a garment after casting off one worn before,
so the embodied one takes up a new body, bound by karma.

children.text: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: Weapons do not cut this one, and fire does not burn this one.

children.text: na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Waters do not moisten this one, and wind does not dry this one.
This one cannot be cut; this one cannot be burned; this one cannot be moistened or dried.
This one is eternal, always-going, firm, unmoving, and ancient.
This one is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchangeable.
Therefore, knowing this one in this way, you should not lament.

children.text: athāśaucavyapagame susnātaḥ suprakṣālitapāṇipādaḥ svācāntas tvevaṃvidhān eva brāhmaṇān yathāśakti udaṅmukhān gandhamālyavastrālaṃkārādibhiḥ pūjitān bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, when impurity has passed away, having bathed well, washed his hands and feet well, and properly sipped water, he should feed such <s>brāhmaṇas</s> as he can, facing north and honored with perfumes, garlands, garments, ornaments, and the like.
At an <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite he should adapt the mantras as referring to one person.
Near the leftovers he should offer just one <s>piṇḍa</s>, with that person's name and <s>gotra</s>.

children.text: bhuktavatsu brāhmaṇeṣu dakṣiṇayābhipūjiteṣu pretanāmagotrābhyāṃ dattākṣayyodakaḥ caturaṅgulapṛthvīḥ tāvadantarāḥ tāvadadhaḥkhātāḥ vitastyāyatāḥ tisraḥ karṣūḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> have eaten and have been honored with a fee, after giving imperishable water with the deceased person's name and <s>gotra</s>, he should make three trenches four fingers wide, separated by the same distance, dug down by the same measure, and a span long.

children.text: karṣūsamīpe cāgnitrayam upasamādhāya paristīrya tatraikaikasmin āhutitrayaṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Near the trenches he should establish the three fires, strew the sacred grass, and offer three oblations in each of them.
Homage with <s>svadhā</s> to <s>Soma</s> possessed of the ancestors.
Homage with <s>svadhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>, carrier of the ancestral offering.
Homage with <s>svadhā</s> to <s>Yama Āṅgirasa</s>.
And in the three places he should perform the placing of <s>piṇḍas</s> as before.

children.text: annadadhighṛtamadhumāṃsaiḥ karṣūtrayaṃ pūrayitvā etat ta iti japet ||
children.translated_text: After filling the three trenches with food, curds, ghee, honey, and meat, he should murmur, "This is for you."
In this way he should perform the rite every month on the day of death.

children.text: saṃvatsarānte pretāya tatpitre tatpitāmahāya tatprapitāmahāya ca brāhmaṇān devapūrvān bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: At the end of a year he should feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with the gods first, for the deceased, for his father, for his grandfather, and for his great-grandfather.
In this rite he should perform the offering in the fire, the invocation, and the water for the feet.

children.text: saṃsṛjatu tvā pṛthivī samānī ca iti ca pretapādyapātre pitṛpādyapātratraye yojayet ||
children.translated_text: With the words, "May the common earth unite you," he should join the vessel of foot-water for the deceased with the three vessels of foot-water for the ancestors.
Near the leftovers he should make four <s>piṇḍas</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇāṃś ca svācāntān dattadakṣiṇāṃś cānuvrajya visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: After the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> have sipped water and received their fees, he should accompany them and dismiss them.
Then he should place the deceased person's <s>piṇḍa</s> into the three <s>piṇḍas</s>, just as with the water from the vessels for the feet.
Even when the three trenches are close together, the procedure is exactly the same.

children.text: sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ māsikārthavat dvādaśāhaṃ śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā trayodaśe 'hni vā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should perform the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> after carrying out a twelve-day <s>śrāddha</s> in the manner of a monthly rite, or on the thirteenth day.
For <s>śūdras</s>, however, it is on the twelfth day and without mantras.

children.text: saṃvatsarābhyantare yadyadhimāso bhavet tadā māsikārthe dinam ekaṃ vardhayet ||
children.translated_text: If an intercalary month occurs within the year, then he should add one day for the monthly rite.

children.text: sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ strīṇāṃ kāryam evaṃ tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: The <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> of women should likewise be performed in this same way,
and he should perform the <s>śrāddha</s> every year for as long as he lives.
For one whose <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> has been performed before the end of a year,
for him too he should give food together with a water-pot to a twice-born man for a year.
For the <s>sapiṇḍas</s> of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, impurity at birth and death lasts ten days.
For a <s>rājanya</s>, it lasts twelve days.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, it lasts fifteen days.
For a <s>śūdra</s>, it lasts a month.
And <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relationship ceases with the seventh man.
During impurity, fire-offering, giving, receiving, and Vedic recitation cease.
During impurity one should not eat anyone's food.

children.text: brāhmaṇādīnām aśauce yaḥ sakṛd evānnam atti tasya tāvad āśaucaṃ yāvat teṣām ||
children.translated_text: If, during the impurity of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, someone eats their food even once, his impurity lasts as long as theirs.
When impurity has passed away, he should perform an expiation.

children.text: savarṇasyāśauce dvijo bhuktvā sravantīm āsādya tannimagnas triraghamarṣaṇaṃ japtvottīrya gāyatryaṣṭasahasraṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten during the impurity of one of the same class, a twice-born man should approach flowing water, immerse himself in it, recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times, come out, and recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> eight thousand times.

children.text: kṣatriyāśauce brāhmaṇas tvetad evopoṣitaḥ kṛtvā śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: During the impurity of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> becomes pure by doing this same rite after fasting.
And a <s>rājanya</s> becomes pure in the same way during the impurity of a <s>vaiśya</s>.
During the impurity of a <s>vaiśya</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> becomes pure after fasting for three nights.

children.text: brāhmaṇāśauce rājanyaḥ kṣatriyāśauce vaiśyaśca sravantīm āsādya gāyatrīśatapañcakaṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: A <s>rājanya</s> in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s impurity, and a <s>vaiśya</s> in a <s>kṣatriya</s>'s impurity, should go to running water and recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> five hundred times.
And a <s>vaiśya</s> in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s impurity should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> eight hundred times.
A twice-born man who has eaten during a <s>śūdra</s>'s impurity should perform the <s>prājāpatya</s> penance.
And a <s>śūdra</s>, in the impurity of twice-born men, should bathe.
A <s>śūdra</s>, after bathing during a <s>śūdra</s>'s impurity, should drink <s>pañcagavya</s>.

children.text: patnīnāṃ dāsānām ānulomyena svāminas tulyam āśaucam ||
children.translated_text: For wives and servants, the impurity is equal to that of the master, according to the regular order.
When the master has died, their own impurity applies.
For people of lower varṇa in relation to higher-varṇa <s>sapiṇḍas</s>, purification comes when that impurity has passed away.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in relation to <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s> <s>sapiṇḍas</s>, purification is after six nights, three nights, and one night respectively.
For a <s>kṣatriya</s> in relation to <s>vaiśya</s> and <s>śūdra</s> <s>sapiṇḍas</s>, it is after six nights and three nights respectively.
For a <s>vaiśya</s> in relation to <s>śūdras</s>, it is after six nights.
In a miscarriage, the days and nights are equal to the months of pregnancy.

children.text: jātamṛte mṛtajāte vā kulasya sadyaḥ śaucam ||
children.translated_text: When a child is born dead or dies at birth, the family's purification is immediate.
When a child who has not yet cut teeth dies, purification is immediate on that very day.
There is no fire-rite for him and no water-offering rite.
But for a child who has cut teeth and has not yet had the <s>cūḍā</s> performed, purification is after one day and night.
For one whose <s>cūḍā</s> has been performed but who has not yet been initiated, it is after three nights.
After that, it is according to the period already stated.
For women, marriage is the sacrament.
For women who have been consecrated by marriage, there is no impurity on the father's side.

children.text: tatprasavamaraṇe cet pitṛgṛhe syātāṃ tadā ekarātraṃ trirātraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: But if her childbirth or death should occur in her father's house, then there is one night for childbirth and three nights for death.

children.text: jananāśaucamadhye yady aparaṃ jananāśaucaṃ syāt tadā pūrvāśaucavyapagame śuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, in the middle of birth impurity, another birth impurity occurs, purification comes when the earlier impurity has passed away.
If it occurs in the remainder of the night, purification is after two days.
If it occurs at dawn, purification is after three days.
Likewise, when the death of a kinsman occurs in the middle of death impurity.
A person staying in another country, on hearing of a birth or death, becomes pure after the remaining portion of the impurity.
If the impurity has passed, but the news is within a year, purification is by one night.
After that, it is by bathing.
In the case of an <s>ācārya</s> or maternal grandfather, if the impurity has passed, purification is after three nights.

children.text: anauraseṣu putreṣu jāteṣu ca mṛteṣu ca
children.translated_text: For sons not born from oneself, when they are born or when they die,
and for wives who previously belonged to another man, when they give birth or when they die,
and when an <s>ācārya</s>'s wife or son, an <s>upādhyāya</s>, maternal uncle, father-in-law, mother-in-law, fellow student, or pupil has died, purification is after one night.
And the same applies for the king of one's own country.
And when a non-<s>sapiṇḍa</s> dies in one's own house.
There is no impurity for those killed by a precipice, fire, fasting to death, water, battle, lightning, or the king.
Nor is there impurity for kings engaged in royal business.
Nor for those under a vow while they are observing the vow.
Nor for participants in a <s>sattra</s> while they are in the <s>sattra</s>.
Nor for artisans while they are doing artisan work.
Nor for those carrying out a royal command, when acting by the king's wish.
Nor during a deity installation or a marriage, when preparations have already been gathered.
Nor when the country is in disorder.
And not even in a severe calamity.
Those who kill themselves and fallen persons do not receive impurity observance or water rites.

children.text: patitasya dāsī mṛte 'hni padā apāṃ ghaṭam apavarjayet ||
children.translated_text: When a fallen man has died, on the day of death a slave woman should overturn a pot of water with her foot.

children.text: udbandhanamṛtasya yaḥ pāśaṃ chindyāt sa taptakṛcchreṇa śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: The person who cuts the noose of one who has died by hanging is purified by the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> penance.
So too the one who performs the funeral rites for those who kill themselves.
And the one who sheds tears for such a person.

children.text: sarvasyaiva pretasya bāndhavaiḥ sahāśrupātaṃ kṛtvā snānena ||
children.translated_text: For every dead person, after shedding tears together with the relatives, purification is by bathing.
If the collection of bones has not been performed, purification is by bathing with one's clothes on.

children.text: dvijaḥ śūdrapretānugamanaṃ kṛtvā sravantīm āsādya tannimagnaḥ triraghamarṣaṇaṃ japtvottīrya gāyatryaṣṭasahasraṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: A twice-born man who has followed a <s>śūdra</s> corpse should go to running water, immerse himself in it, recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times, come out, and recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> eight thousand times.
For a twice-born corpse, the recitation is eight hundred times.
A <s>śūdra</s>, after following a corpse, should bathe.
On exposure to the smoke of a funeral pyre, all varṇas should bathe.
The same applies after sexual intercourse, a bad dream, when blood has reached the throat, and after vomiting or purging.
And after shaving has been done.
And after touching one who has touched a corpse, and after touching menstruating women, <s>caṇḍālas</s>, and sacrificial posts.
And after touching the carcass of a five-clawed animal, except those fit to be eaten, and its bones or fat.

children.text: sarveṣv eteṣu snāneṣu vastraṃ nāprakṣālitaṃ bibhṛyāt ||
children.translated_text: In all these baths, one should not wear a garment that has not been washed.
A menstruating woman becomes pure by bathing on the fourth day.

children.text: rajasvalā hīnavarṇāṃ rajasvalāṃ spṛṣṭvā na tāvad aśnīyāt yāvan na śuddhā ||
children.translated_text: A menstruating woman, after touching a menstruating woman of lower varṇa, should not eat until that woman is pure.

children.text: savarṇām adhikavarṇāṃ vā spṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ snātvā śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: After touching one of the same varṇa or of a higher varṇa, she becomes pure by bathing immediately.

children.text: kṣutvā suptvā bhuktvā bhojanādhyayanepsuḥ pītvā snātvā niṣṭhīvya vāsaḥ paridhāya rathyām ākramya mūtrapurīṣaṃ kṛtvā pañcanakhāsthyasnehaṃ spṛṣṭvā cācamet ||
children.translated_text: After sneezing, sleeping, eating, when wishing to eat or study, after drinking, bathing, spitting, putting on a garment, stepping onto a road, urinating or defecating, and touching a five-clawed animal, bone, or fat, one should sip water.
And also after conversation with a <s>caṇḍāla</s> or a <s>mleccha</s>.

children.text: nābher adhastāt prabāhuṣu ca kāyikair malaiḥ surābhir madyaiś copahato mṛttoyais tadaṅgaṃ prakṣālya śudhyet ||
children.translated_text: If one is affected below the navel or on the forearms by bodily impurities, by <s>surā</s>, or by other liquors, one is purified by washing that limb with earth and water.
If one is affected elsewhere, one should wash that limb with earth and water and then bathe.
But if the mouth is affected, one should fast, bathe, and be purified with <s>pañcagavya</s>.
The same applies if the lips are affected.

children.text: vasā śukram asṛṅ majjā mūtraṃ viṭ karṇaviṇnakhāḥ
children.translated_text: Fat, semen, blood, marrow, urine, feces, ear-wax, and nails,

children.text: śleṣmāśru dūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: phlegm, tears, eye-discharge, and sweat: these twelve are the impurities of human beings.

children.text: gauḍī mādhvī ca paiṣṭī ca vijñeyā trividhā surā
children.translated_text: <s>Surā</s> is to be known as threefold: <s>gauḍī</s>, <s>mādhvī</s>, and <s>paiṣṭī</s>.

children.text: yathaivaikā tathā sarvā na pātavyā dvijātibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as one is forbidden, so are all; they must not be drunk by twice-born men.
Liquors made from <s>madhūka</s>, sugarcane, <s>ṭāṅka</s>, <s>kola</s>, date, and jackfruit,
from grape juice and honey, <s>maireya</s>, and that made from coconut,
these ten alcoholic drinks too are impure for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: rājanyaś caiva vaiśyaś ca spṛṣṭvaitāni na duṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And a <s>rājanya</s> and a <s>vaiśya</s> are not defiled by touching these.

children.text: guroḥ pretasya śiṣyas tu pitṛmedhaṃ samācaran
children.translated_text: But a pupil who performs the <s>pitṛmedha</s> rite for his deceased <s>guru</s>
is purified there in ten nights, together with those who eat the food for the dead.

children.text: ācāryaṃ svam upādhyāyaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum
children.translated_text: A man under a vow, after carrying out his own <s>ācārya</s>, <s>upādhyāya</s>, father, mother, or <s>guru</s> when dead,

children.text: nirhṛtya tu vratī pretān na vratena viyujyate ||
children.translated_text: is not separated from his vow.

children.text: ādiṣṭī nodakaṃ kuryād ā vratasya samāpanāt
children.translated_text: One who has been enjoined should not offer water until the completion of the vow.
But when it is completed, after offering water, he is purified in just three nights.
Knowledge, austerity, fire, food, earth, mind, water, anointing,
wind, action, the sun, and time are agents of purification for embodied beings.

children.text: sarveṣām eva śaucānām annaśaucaṃ paraṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Among all forms of purity, purity in food is remembered as supreme.

children.text: yo 'nne śuciḥ sa hi śucir na mṛdvāriśuciḥ śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who is pure with respect to food is truly pure; one pure merely by earth and water is not pure.
The learned are purified by forbearance, those who have done what should not be done by giving,
hidden sinners by recitation, and the best knowers of the <s>Veda</s> by austerity.

children.text: mṛttoyaiḥ śudhyate śodhyaṃ nadī vegena śudhyati
children.translated_text: What is to be cleansed is purified with earth and water; a river is purified by its current.
A woman is purified by menstruation, and the best of twice-born men whose minds are tainted are purified by renunciation.

children.text: adbhir gātrāṇi śudhyanti manaḥ satyena śudhyati
children.translated_text: The limbs are purified by water; the mind is purified by truth.
The inner self of beings is purified by knowledge and austerity; the intellect is purified by knowledge.

children.text: eṣa śaucasya te proktaḥ śārīrasya vinirṇayaḥ
children.translated_text: This determination concerning bodily purity has been declared to you.
Hear now the determination concerning the purity of various kinds of substances.

children.text: śārīrair malaiḥ surābhir madyair vā yad upahataṃ tad atyantopahatam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has been affected by bodily impurities, by liquor, or by intoxicating drinks is utterly defiled.

children.text: atyantopahataṃ sarvaṃ lohabhāṇḍam agnau prakṣiptaṃ śudhyet ||
children.translated_text: Every metal vessel that is utterly defiled should become pure when placed in fire.

children.text: maṇimayam aśmamayam abjaṃ ca saptarātraṃ mahīnikhananena ||
children.translated_text: An article made of gems, stone, or shell is purified by being buried in the earth for seven nights.
An article made of horn, tooth, or bone is purified by scraping.
An article made of wood or clay should be discarded.

children.text: atyantopahatasya vastrasya yat prakṣālitaṃ sad virajyate tacchindyāt ||
children.translated_text: Of a cloth that is utterly defiled, whatever part, after being washed, becomes discolored should be cut away.
Objects made of gold, silver, shell, or gems, if not smeared, are purified with water.
So too objects made of stone, cups, and <s>graha</s> vessels.
<s>Caru</s> vessels, <s>sruk</s> ladles, and <s>sruva</s> ladles are purified with hot water.
In a sacrificial rite, sacrificial vessels are purified by wiping them with the hand.
<s>Sphya</s> blades, winnowing baskets, carts, pestles, and mortars are purified by sprinkling.
So too beds, vehicles, and seats.
And many items as well.
So too grains, skins, ropes, woven materials, bamboo articles, thread, and cotton garments.
So too vegetables, roots, fruits, and flowers.
So too grass, wood, and dry leaves.
These are purified by washing.
Small quantities too are purified in this way.
Silk and wool are purified with alkaline substances.
Coarse woolen cloths are purified with <s>ariṣṭaka</s> nuts.
Fine cloths are purified with <s>śrīphala</s> fruits.
Linen garments are purified with white mustard.
So too articles made of horn, bone, and tooth.
Deer-hair fabrics are purified with lotus seeds.
Objects made of copper, brass, tin, and lead are purified with sour water.
Bronze and iron are purified with ashes.
Wooden objects are purified by planing.
Objects produced from fruit are purified with cow-hair brushes.
Things joined together in a mass are purified by sprinkling.
Liquids are purified by straining.
Jaggery and other products of sugarcane, when abundant or stored in a house, are purified by applying water and fire.
And so are all salts.
Earthen objects are purified by firing them again.
Images of deities, once purified like other substances, are purified further by re-consecration.

children.text: asiddhasyānnasya yanmātram upahataṃ tanmātraṃ parityajya śeṣasya kaṇḍanaprakṣālane kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Of uncooked food, one should discard only the amount that has been defiled and then pound and wash the remainder.

children.text: droṇābhyadhikam siddham annam upahataṃ na duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Cooked food in excess of a <s>droṇa</s>, when defiled, is not polluted.

children.text: tasyopahatamātram apāsya gāyatryābhimantritaṃ suvarṇāmbhaḥ prakṣipet bastasya ca pradarśayed agneś ca ||
children.translated_text: After removing only the defiled portion, one should sprinkle in gold-water consecrated with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and show it to a goat and to fire.
What has been eaten by birds, smelled by a cow, shaken off, or sneezed upon,
and what has been contaminated by hair or insects, is purified by sprinkling earth on it.

children.text: yāvan nāpaityamedhyāktād gandho lepaś ca tatkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as the smell and the smear caused by contact with an impure thing do not depart,

children.text: tāvan mṛdvāri deyaṃ syāt sarvāsu dravyaśuddhiṣu ||
children.translated_text: so long earth and water should be applied in all purifications of substances.

children.text: ajāśvaṃ mukhato medhyaṃ na gaur na narajā malāḥ
children.translated_text: The goat and the horse are pure at the mouth; not so the cow, nor are impurities produced from human beings pure.
Roads are purified by the rays of the moon and sun and by the wind.
Road mud and road water touched by outcastes, dogs, or crows
are purified by wind alone, as are structures laid with baked bricks.

children.text: prāṇinām atha sarveṣāṃ mṛdbhir adbhiś ca kārayet
children.translated_text: For all living beings, one should perform purification with earths and waters,
always and without negligence, when they are utterly defiled.

children.text: bhūmiṣṭham udakaṃ puṇyaṃ vaitṛṣṇyaṃ yatra gor bhavet
children.translated_text: Water standing on the ground is pure where a cow can quench its thirst,

children.text: avyāptaṃ ced amedhyena tadvad eva śilāgatam ||
children.translated_text: provided it is not pervaded by an impure thing; the same applies to water resting on stone.
From a well containing a dead five-nailed animal, or one that is utterly defiled,

children.text: apaḥ samuddharet sarvāḥ śeṣaṃ vastreṇa śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: one should draw out all the water and cleanse what remains with a cloth.
In a well lined with baked bricks, one should kindle a fire.
Afterward, when new water has appeared, one should place <s>pañcagavya</s> in it.
In small, stagnant reservoirs of water, O earth,

children.text: kūpavat kathitā śuddhir mahatsu ca na dūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: purification is said to be as for a well; in large ones there is no pollution.
The gods ordained three purities for <s>brāhmaṇas</s>:

children.text: adṛṣṭam adbhir nirṇiktaṃ yacca vācā praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: what has not been seen to be impure, what has been rinsed with water, and what is commended by speech.

children.text: nityaṃ śuddhaḥ kāruhastaḥ paṇyaṃ yacca prasāritam
children.translated_text: The hand of an artisan is always pure, as is merchandise displayed for sale,

children.text: brāhmaṇāntaritaṃ bhaikṣyam ākarāḥ sarva eva ca ||
children.translated_text: alms separated by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and all mines and sources of ore.

children.text: nityam āsyaṃ śuci strīṇāṃ śakuniḥ phalapātane
children.translated_text: The mouth of women is always pure; a bird is pure when it causes fruit to fall.

children.text: prasrave ca śucir vatsaḥ śvā mṛgagrahaṇe śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: A calf is pure at the flow of milk, and a dog is pure in seizing game.

children.text: śvabhir hatasya yan māṃsaṃ śuci tat parikīrtitam
children.translated_text: The flesh of an animal killed by dogs is declared to be pure.

children.text: kravyādbhiś ca hatasyānyaiś caṇḍālādyaiś ca dasyubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too is that of one killed by other flesh-eaters, by <s>caṇḍālas</s> and the like, or by robbers.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ nābher yāni khāni tāni medhyāni nirdiśet
children.translated_text: The openings above the navel one should declare pure.
Those below it are impure, as are impurities fallen from the body.
A fly, drops, a shadow, a cow, an elephant, a horse, and rays of light,

children.text: rajo bhūr vāyur agniś ca mārjāraś ca sadā śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: dust, earth, wind, fire, and a cat are always pure.

children.text: nocchiṣṭaṃ kurvate mukhyā vipruṣo 'ṅge na yānti yāḥ
children.translated_text: Drops that do not fall upon the body do not make something <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (left over or ritually polluted).

children.text: na śmaśrūṇi gatāny āsyaṃ na dantāntaraveṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: Nor do hairs of the beard that have entered the mouth, nor what is lodged between the teeth.

children.text: spṛśanti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān
children.translated_text: Drops may touch the feet of others from a person who is sipping water for purification.

children.text: bhaumikais te samā jñeyā na tair aprayato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: They should be understood as equivalent to water on the ground; one does not become impure by them.
If a person holding an object in his hand is somehow touched by <s>ucchiṣṭa</s>,

children.text: anidhāyaiva tad dravyam ācāntaḥ śucitām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: without setting that object down, he attains purity after sipping water.
A house is purified by sweeping and smearing, and a book by sprinkling.
By sweeping, smearing, watering, and scraping,

children.text: dāhena ca bhuvaḥ śuddhir vāsenāpyathavā gavām
children.translated_text: and also by burning, the ground is purified, or else by the dwelling of cows.
Cows are purifying and auspicious; the worlds are established in cows.
Cows extend the sacrifice; cows remove every sin.

children.text: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ sarpiḥ kṣīraṃ dadhi ca rocanā ||
children.translated_text: Cow urine, cow dung, ghee, milk, curds, and <s>rocanā</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgam etat paramaṃ maṅgalyaṃ paramaṃ gavām
children.translated_text: this sixfold set from cows is supreme and supremely auspicious.
Water from the horns of cows is holy and destroys all sin.
Rubbing or scratching cows destroys every stain.
By giving fodder to cows, one is honored in the world of heaven.

children.text: gavāṃ hi tīrthe vasatīha gaṅgā puṣṭis tathāsāṃ rajasi pravṛddhā
children.translated_text: Here <s>Gaṅgā</s> dwells in the sacred place of cows, and nourishment thrives in their dust.

children.text: lakṣmīḥ karīṣe praṇatau ca dharmas tāsāṃ praṇāmaṃ satataṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> is in their dung, and <s>dharma</s> in bowing to them; therefore one should constantly bow to them.

children.text: atha brāhmaṇasya varṇānukrameṇa catasro bhāryā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Now, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> may have four wives in the order of the <s>varṇas</s>.
A <s>kṣatriya</s> may have three.
A <s>vaiśya</s> may have two.
A <s>śūdra</s> may have one.
Among these, when marrying a woman of the same <s>varṇa</s>, her hand is to be grasped.
When marrying outside one's <s>varṇa</s>, an arrow is grasped with a <s>kṣatriya</s> maiden.
A goad is grasped with a <s>vaiśya</s> maiden.
The end of a garment is grasped with a <s>śūdra</s> maiden.

children.text: na sagotrāṃ na samānārṣapravarāṃ bhāryāṃ vindeta ||
children.translated_text: One should not take as wife a woman of the same <s>gotra</s> or the same ancestral <s>ṛṣi-pravara</s>.

children.text: mātṛtas tv ā pañcamāt puruṣāt pitṛtaś cā saptamāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor one related up to the fifth generation on the mother's side or up to the seventh on the father's side.
Nor one from a bad family.
Nor one who is diseased.
Nor one with extra limbs.
Nor one deficient in limbs.
Nor one who is excessively tawny.
Nor one who is talkative.
Now there are eight forms of marriage.

children.text: brāhmo daiva ārṣaḥ prājāpatyo gāndharva āsuro rākṣasaḥ paiśācaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: They are <s>brāhma</s>, <s>daiva</s>, <s>ārṣa</s>, <s>prājāpatya</s>, <s>gāndharva</s>, <s>āsura</s>, <s>rākṣasa</s>, and <s>paiśāca</s>.
The gift of a maiden to a worthy man after inviting him is <s>brāhma</s>.
Giving her to an officiating priest at a sacrifice is <s>daiva</s>.
Giving her after receiving a pair of cows is <s>ārṣa</s>.
Giving her to one who has requested her is <s>prājāpatya</s>.
The union of two mutually desirous people, without the parents, is <s>gāndharva</s>.
Marriage by purchase is <s>āsura</s>.
Seizure in battle is <s>rākṣasa</s>.
Intercourse with a sleeping or intoxicated woman is <s>paiśāca</s>.
Of these, the first four are lawful.
The <s>gāndharva</s> form is also lawful for <s>rājanyas</s>.
A son of a <s>brāhma</s> marriage purifies twenty-one men.
A son of a <s>daiva</s> marriage purifies fourteen.
A son of an <s>ārṣa</s> marriage purifies seven.
A son of a <s>prājāpatya</s> marriage purifies four.

children.text: brāhmeṇa vivāhena kanyāṃ dadat brahmalokaṃ gamayati ||
children.translated_text: By giving a maiden in a <s>brāhma</s> marriage, one causes her to go to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By a <s>daiva</s> marriage, to heaven.
By an <s>ārṣa</s> marriage, to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By a <s>prājāpatya</s> marriage, to the world of the gods.
By a <s>gāndharva</s> marriage, one goes to the world of the <s>gandharvas</s>.

children.text: pitā pitāmaho bhrātā sakulyo mātāmaho mātā ceti kanyāpradāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The father, paternal grandfather, brother, kinsman, maternal grandfather, and mother are givers of the maiden.
In the absence of the preceding one, the next, if in sound condition, is the giver, each in order.
After waiting through three menstrual seasons, a maiden should make her own choice.
When three seasons have passed, she always has authority over herself.
A maiden who sees her menses in her father's house while still unconsecrated,

children.text: sā kanyā vṛṣalī jñeyā haraṃs tāṃ na viduṣyati ||
children.translated_text: that maiden should be known as a <s>vṛṣalī</s>; one who takes her does not incur fault.
Now, the duties of women.
She should have vows and conduct equal to her husband's.
She should honor her mother-in-law, father-in-law, teacher, deities, and guests.
She should keep the household implements well prepared.
She should not be free-handed in spending.
She should keep vessels and goods well guarded.
She should not delight in rites involving roots and charms.
She should be devoted to auspicious conduct.
When her husband is abroad, she should not perform acts of adornment.
She should not go to other people's houses.
She should not stand at doorways or windows.
She should not be independent in any actions.
Even in childhood, youth, and old age, she is dependent on father, husband, and sons.
When her husband has died, she should practice celibacy or follow him by ascending after him.

children.text: nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthagyajño na vrataṃ nāpyupoṣitam
children.translated_text: Women have no separate sacrifice, no vow, and no fasting observance.

children.text: patiṃ śuśrūṣate yat tu tena svarge mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: But by serving her husband she is honored in heaven.

children.text: patyau jīvati yā yoṣid upavāsavrataṃ caret
children.translated_text: A woman who observes a fasting vow while her husband is alive

children.text: āyuḥ sā harate bhartur narakaṃ caiva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: takes away her husband's lifespan and goes to hell.

children.text: mṛte bhartari sādhvī strī brahmacarye vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: A virtuous woman whose husband has died, remaining steadfast in celibacy,
goes to heaven even if sonless, just like those who are <s>brahmacārins</s>.

children.text: savarṇāsu bahubhāryāsu vidyamānāsu jyeṣṭhayā saha dharmakāryaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When there are many wives of the same <s>varṇa</s>, he should perform religious rites with the eldest, if she is present.
Among mixed wives, he may do so even with the youngest, if she is of the same <s>varṇa</s>.
If there is no wife of the same <s>varṇa</s>, then with the one immediately next, and in distress.
But a twice-born man should never perform them with a <s>śūdrā</s>.

children.text: dvijasya bhāryā śūdrā tu dharmārthaṃ na kvacid bhavet
children.translated_text: A <s>śūdrā</s> wife of a twice-born man should never serve any religious purpose.

children.text: ratyartham eva sā tasya rāgāndhasya prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: For that man blinded by passion, she is declared to be only for the sake of pleasure.
Twice-born men who, out of delusion, marry a woman of lower caste
quickly bring their families, together with their descendants, down to the condition of <s>śūdras</s>.
But for the man whose rites to the gods, ancestors, and guests have her as their chief support,

children.text: nāśnanti pitṛdevāstu na ca svargaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: the ancestors and gods do not eat, and he does not go to heaven.
When the embryo is clearly known, there is the <s>niṣeka</s> rite.
Before movement in the womb, there is <s>puṃsavana</s>.
In the sixth or eighth month there is <s>sīmantonnayana</s>.
And when the child is born, there is <s>jātakarma</s>.
When the impurity has passed, there is name-giving.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the name should be auspicious.
For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, it should express strength.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, it should be connected with wealth.
For a <s>śūdra</s>, it should be contemptible.
In the fourth month there is the showing of the sun.
In the sixth month there is the first feeding with rice.
In the third year there is the tonsure.
These same rites for women are performed without mantras.
For them, marriage is performed with mantras.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, initiation is in the eighth year from conception.
For a king, it is in the eleventh year from conception.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, it is in the twelfth year from conception.
For them, the girdles are made respectively of <s>muñja</s> grass, bowstring, and <s>balbaja</s> grass.
Their sacred threads and garments are of cotton, hemp, and wool.
Their skins are those of the black antelope, tiger, and goat.
Their staffs are of <s>palāśa</s>, <s>khadira</s>, and <s>udumbara</s> wood.
They should be equal in length to the region of the hairline, the forehead, and the nose.
Or all of them may be the same.
They should be unbent and with their bark intact.
Begging for alms is done with the word <s>bhavat</s> at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>Sāvitrī</s> does not lapse until the sixteenth year,

children.text: ā dvāviṃśāt kṣatrabandhor ā caturviṃśater viśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a kinsman of the <s>kṣatriyas</s> until the twenty-second, and for a <s>vaiśya</s> until the twenty-fourth.
After that, all three, not consecrated at the proper time,
become fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>vrātyas</s>, censured by the noble.

children.text: yadyasya vihitaṃ carma yat sūtraṃ yā ca mekhalā
children.translated_text: Whatever skin is prescribed for one, whatever thread, and whatever girdle,

children.text: yo daṇḍo yacca vasanaṃ tat tad asya vrateṣvapi ||
children.translated_text: whatever staff and whatever garment, that very equipment is used also in his vows.
If the girdle, antelope skin, staff, sacred thread, or water-pot
has been lost, he should cast it into water and take others with mantra.
Next, for brahmacārins there is residence in the teacher's household.
There is worship at the two twilights.

children.text: pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japet tiṣṭhan paścimām āsīnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should recite at the earlier twilight while standing, and at the later one while seated.
At both times he should perform bathing and the fire rite.
He should immerse himself in the water straight like a staff.
He should study when summoned.
He should do what is pleasing and beneficial to the teacher.
He should wear the girdle, staff, antelope skin, and sacred thread.
Except in the teacher's household, he should beg for alms among virtuous people.
With the teacher's permission he should eat the alms.
He should avoid food prepared for a <s>śrāddha</s>, salt, sour food, stale food, dancing, singing, women, honey, meat, collyrium, leftovers, injury to living beings, and obscene speech.
His bed should be low.
He should rise before the teacher and go to rest last.
After performing twilight worship, he should salute the teacher.
And with his hands arranged appropriately, he should touch the teacher's feet.
He should touch the right foot with the right hand, and the other with the other hand.
At the end of the salutation he should state his own name to him, ending with the word <s>bhoḥ</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhann āsīnaḥ śayāno bhuñjānaḥ parāṅmukhaś ca nāsyābhibhāṣaṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not address him while standing, sitting, lying down, eating, or facing away.
If the teacher is seated, he should address him while standing; if the teacher is going, while approaching him;

children.text: āgacchataḥ pratyudgamya paścād dhāvaṃs tu dhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: if he is coming, by going to meet him; and if he is running, by running after him.
If the teacher faces away, he should face him.
If the teacher is at a distance, he should go near him.
If the teacher is lying down, he should bow down.

children.text: tasya ca cakṣurviṣaye na yatheṣṭāsanaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: And within his sight he should not sit as he pleases.
Nor should he utter his bare name alone.
He should not imitate his gait, gestures, speech, and the like.

children.text: yatrāsya nindāparivādau syātāṃ na tatra tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: Where there is censure or slander of him, he should not remain there.
He should not share one seat with him.
Except on stones, slabs, boats, and vehicles.
When the teacher's teacher is present, he should behave toward him as toward the teacher.

children.text: anirdiṣṭaś ca guruṇā svān gurūn nābhivādayet ||
children.translated_text: And unless instructed by the teacher, he should not salute his own elders.

children.text: bāle samānavayasi vādhyāpake guruputre guruvad varteta ||
children.translated_text: Toward the teacher's son, whether a child, of the same age, or an instructor, he should behave as toward the teacher.
But he should not wash his feet.
Nor should he eat his leftovers.

children.text: evaṃ vedaṃ vedau vedān vā svīkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In this way he should learn one Veda, two Vedas, or all the Vedas.
After that, he should learn the auxiliary sciences of the Veda.

children.text: yas tvanadhītavedo 'nyatra śramaṃ kuryād asau sasaṃtānaḥ śūdratvam eti ||
children.translated_text: But one who has not studied the Veda and makes effort elsewhere goes, together with his descendants, to the state of a <s>śūdra</s>.
The first birth is from the mother; the second is the tying of the <s>muñja</s> girdle.

children.text: tatrāsya mātā sāvitrī bhavati pitā tvācāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There his mother is the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, but his father is the <s>ācārya</s>.
By this alone comes their twice-born status.
Before the tying of the <s>muñja</s> girdle, a twice-born man is equal to a <s>śūdra</s>.
A brahmacārin should be either shaven-headed or wear matted hair.

children.text: vedasvīkaraṇād ūrdhvaṃ gurvanujñātas tasmai varaṃ dattvā snāyāt ||
children.translated_text: After learning the Veda, with the teacher's permission and after giving him the chosen fee, he should take the ceremonial bath.

children.text: tato gurukula eva vā janmanaḥ śeṣaṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: Or else he may spend the remainder of his life in the teacher's household itself.
There, when the <s>ācārya</s> has died, he should behave toward the teacher's son as toward the teacher.
Or toward the teacher's wives who are of the same varṇa.
In their absence, he should tend the sacred fire and be a lifelong brahmacārin.

children.text: evaṃ carati yo vipro brahmacaryam atandritaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>vipra</s> who thus practices brahmacarya without negligence

children.text: sa gacchatyuttamaṃ sthānaṃ na cehājāyate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes to the highest place and is not born again here.
For a twice-born man under a vow, an intentional emission of semen
is called a breach of the vow by brahmacārins who know <s>dharma</s>.
When this sin has occurred, after wearing a donkey skin...
He should go for alms at seven houses, declaring his own deed.
Living on the alms obtained from them, eating only once a day,
and sipping water at the three daily times, he is purified in a year.

children.text: svapne siktvā brahmacārī dvijaḥ śukram akāmataḥ
children.translated_text: If a twice-born brahmacarin emits semen unwillingly in a dream,

children.text: snātvārkam arcayitvā triḥ punar mām ityṛcaṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: he should bathe, worship the Sun three times, and recite the verse beginning <s>punar mām</s>.
Without going for alms and without kindling the sacred fire,
if he is not ill, he should observe the <s>avakīrṇin-vrata</s> for seven nights.

children.text: taṃ ced abhyudiyāt sūryaḥ śayānaṃ kāmakārataḥ
children.translated_text: If the sun rises over him while he is lying down intentionally,
or sets over him through lack of awareness, he should fast for the day while reciting.

children.text: yastūpanīya vratādeśaṃ kṛtvā vedam adhyāpayet tam ācāryaṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should know as an <s>ācārya</s> the man who, after initiating a student and prescribing the vow, teaches him the Veda.

children.text: yastvenaṃ mūlyenādhyāpayet tam upādhyāyam ekadeśaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: But one should know as an <s>upādhyāya</s> the man who teaches him for a fee, or who teaches him a section.

children.text: yo yasya yajñakarmāṇi kuryāt tam ṛtvijaṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should know as an <s>ṛtvij</s> the man who performs another's sacrificial rites.
One should not appoint someone who has not been examined.
One should not teach him.
One should not initiate him.

children.text: adharmeṇa ca yaḥ prāha yaścādharmeṇa pṛcchati
children.translated_text: The one who expounds wrongly, against <s>dharma</s>, and the one who asks wrongly, against <s>dharma</s>:
one of those two dies, or incurs hostility.

children.text: dharmārthau yatra na syātāṃ śuśrūṣā vāpi tadvidhā
children.translated_text: Where <s>dharma</s> and benefit are not present, nor service of the proper kind,

children.text: tatra vidyā na vaktavyā śubhaṃ bījam ivoṣare ||
children.translated_text: knowledge should not be spoken there, like good seed on barren soil.

children.text: vidyā ha vai brahmāṇam ājagāma gopāya mā śevadhiṣṭe 'ham asti
children.translated_text: Knowledge indeed came to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: "Protect me; I am your treasure.

children.text: asūyakāyānṛjave 'yatāya na māṃ brūyā avīryavatī tathā syām ||
children.translated_text: Do not speak me to one who is envious, crooked, or uncontrolled, lest I become powerless."

children.text: yam eva vidyāḥ śucim apramattaṃ medhāvinaṃ brahmacaryopapannam
children.translated_text: "Speak me only to a man who is pure, vigilant, intelligent, and endowed with brahmacarya,

children.text: yaste na druhyet katamacca nāha tasmai māṃ brūyā nidhipāya brahman ||
children.translated_text: who does not harm you in any way; speak me, O <s>Brahman</s>, to him as to the keeper of a treasure."

children.text: śrāvaṇyāṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ vā chandāṃsy upākṛtyārdhapañcamān māsān adhīyīta ||
children.translated_text: On the <s>Śrāvaṇī</s> or the <s>Prauṣṭhapadī</s>, after beginning the Vedas, he should study for four and a half months.
After that he should perform their <s>utsarga</s> outside.
Between the <s>utsarjana</s> and the <s>upākarma</s>, he should study the Vedāṅgas.
He should not study for a day and night on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days.
Nor during a change of season, an eclipse, or birth-and-death impurity.
Nor during <s>Indra</s>'s procession.
Nor when a violent wind is blowing.
Nor when there is untimely rain, lightning, or thunder.
Nor during earthquakes, meteor falls, or burning of the quarters.
Nor in a village where there is a corpse.
Nor when weapons clash.
Nor when dogs, jackals, or donkeys are howling.
Nor at the sound of musical instruments.
Nor near a <s>śūdra</s> or a fallen man.
Nor in a temple, cremation ground, crossroads, or road.
Nor at the water's edge.
Nor with his feet placed on a stool.
Nor in conveyances such as an elephant, horse, camel, boat, or ox-cart.
Nor after vomiting.
Nor after purging.
Nor while suffering from indigestion.
Nor when a five-clawed animal passes between.
Nor when there is calamity involving a king, a learned Vedic scholar, a cow, or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Nor at the <s>upākarma</s>.
Nor at the <s>utsarga</s>.
Nor should the Ṛg or Yajur Veda be studied while a Sāman is being chanted.
After studying in the latter part of the night, he should not lie down to sleep.
Even if pressed, he should avoid study on days of suspended study.
For what is studied on a day of suspended study bears fruit neither here nor in the next world.
By that study, the life span of both teacher and pupil is diminished.

children.text: tasmād anadhyāyavarjaṃ guruṇā brahmalokakāmena vidyā satśiṣyakṣetreṣu vaptavyā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, avoiding days of suspended study, a teacher who desires the world of <s>Brahman</s> should sow knowledge in the fields of good pupils.
At the beginning and end of Vedic recitation, the pupil should clasp the teacher's feet.
And the <s>praṇava</s> should be uttered.

children.text: tatra ca yad ṛco 'dhīte tenāsyājyena pitṝṇāṃ tṛptir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: There, whatever Ṛg verses he studies, by that his ancestors are satisfied with ghee.
Whatever Yajus formulas he studies, by that they are satisfied with honey.
Whatever Sāman chants he studies, by that they are satisfied with milk.
Whatever Atharvan material he studies, by that they are satisfied with meat.
Whatever Purāṇa, Itihāsa, Vedāṅga, or Dharmaśāstra texts he studies, by that they are satisfied with food.

children.text: yaś ca vidyām āsādyāsmin loke tayā jīvet na sā tasya paraloke phalapradā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: A man who, after acquiring knowledge, lives by it in this world: that knowledge will not bear fruit for him in the next world.

children.text: yaś ca vidyayā yaśaḥ pareṣāṃ hanti ||
children.translated_text: The same applies to one who uses knowledge to destroy the reputation of others.
Without permission, one should not take knowledge from another person who is reciting.
That taking of it is theft of sacred knowledge for him, leading to hell.

children.text: laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vāpi tathādhyātmikam eva vā
children.translated_text: Whether knowledge is worldly, Vedic,

children.text: ādadīta yato jñānaṃ na taṃ druhyet kadācana ||
children.translated_text: or spiritual, from whomever one receives knowledge, one should never harm him.
Of the begetting father and the giver of sacred knowledge, the father who gives sacred knowledge is weightier.

children.text: brahmajanma hi viprasya pretya ceha ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: For the sacred birth of a <s>vipra</s> is eternal both after death and here.

children.text: kāmān mātā pitā cainaṃ yad utpādayato mithaḥ
children.translated_text: Mother and father produce him mutually out of desire;

children.text: saṃbhūtiṃ tasya tāṃ vidyād yad yonāviha jāyate ||
children.translated_text: one should know that production as the one by which he is born here from the womb.

children.text: ācāryas tvasya yāṃ jātiṃ vidhivad vedapāragaḥ
children.translated_text: But the birth that the <s>ācārya</s>, duly and as one who has mastered the Veda,
produces for him through the <s>Sāvitrī</s>: that is true, undecaying, and immortal.

children.text: ya āvṛṇotyavitathena karṇāvaduḥkhaṃ kurvann amṛtaṃ samprayacchan
children.translated_text: The one who fills his ears with what is not false, making him free from pain and bestowing immortality,

children.text: taṃ manyeta pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca tasmai na druhyet kṛtam asya jānan ||
children.translated_text: one should regard him as father and mother, and, knowing what he has done, one should not harm him.
Three persons are supremely venerable for a man:
mother, father, and <s>ācārya</s>.
One should always be obedient in service to them.
Whatever they tell him, he should do.
He should act in ways pleasing and beneficial to them.

children.text: na tair ananujñātaḥ kiṃcid api kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Without their permission, he should not do anything at all.

children.text: eta eva trayo vedā eta eva trayaḥ surāḥ
children.translated_text: These very three are the three Vedas; these very three are the three gods.

children.text: eta eva trayo lokā eta eva trayo 'gnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These very three are the three worlds; these very three are the three fires.

children.text: pitā gārhapatyo 'gniḥ dakṣiṇāgnir mātā gurur āhavanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The father is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire; the mother is the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>; the teacher is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.

children.text: sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: All the <s>dharmas</s> are honored for the man by whom these three are honored.

children.text: anādṛtās tu yasyaite sarvās tasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for the man by whom these three are not honored, all his rites are fruitless.

children.text: imaṃ lokaṃ mātṛbhaktyā pitṛbhaktyā tu madhyamam
children.translated_text: By devotion to one's mother one attains this world, and by devotion to one's father the middle world;
but by service to the teacher alone one attains the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

The king, the officiating priest, the learned <s>śrotriya</s>, the restrainer from <s>adharma</s>, the <s>upādhyāya</s>, the paternal uncle, the maternal grandfather, the maternal uncle, the father-in-law, the elder brother, and kinsmen are to be treated like an <s>ācārya</s>.
So too are the wives of these men, if they are of the same varṇa.
So too the mother's sister, the father's sister, and the elder sister.
Toward a younger father-in-law, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, or officiating priest, rising in respect itself is the salutation.

children.text: hīnavarṇānāṃ gurupatnīnāṃ dūrād abhivādanaṃ na pādopasparśanam ||
children.translated_text: For teachers' wives of lower varṇa there should be salutation from a distance, not touching of the feet.
For teachers' wives one should not perform such services as removing hair from the body, applying collyrium, arranging the hair, or washing the feet.

children.text: asaṃstutāpi parapatnī bhaginīti vācyā putrīti māteti vā ||
children.translated_text: Even another man's wife, though not previously acquainted, should be addressed as 'sister,' or as 'daughter,' or as 'mother.'

children.text: na ca gurūṇāṃ tvam iti brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: And one should not address elders with the familiar 'you.'
If one transgresses this, one should fast and, at the end of the day, eat after appeasing him.

children.text: na ca guruṇā saha vigṛhya kathāḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: And one should not converse with a teacher after quarreling with him.
Nor should one speak slander of him.
Nor should one say what is displeasing to him.
But a teacher's wife who is young should not here be saluted at the feet
by a man who has completed twenty years and knows what is proper and improper.

children.text: kāmaṃ tu gurupatnīnāṃ yuvatīnāṃ yuvā bhuvi
children.translated_text: Yet a young man on earth may certainly perform the prescribed salutation

children.text: vidhivad vandanaṃ kuryād asāvaham iti bruvan ||
children.translated_text: to young teachers' wives, saying, 'It is I, sir.'
After returning from abroad, and each day, one should touch the feet and offer salutation
to teachers' wives, remembering the <s>dharma</s> of good people.

children.text: vittaṃ bandhur vayaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī
children.translated_text: Wealth, kinship, age, action, and knowledge as the fifth

children.text: etāni mānasthānāni garīyo yad yad uttaram ||
children.translated_text: are grounds of honor; each succeeding one is weightier than the one before.

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ daśavarṣaṃ ca śatavarṣaṃ ca bhūmipam
children.translated_text: A ten-year-old <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and a hundred-year-old king

children.text: pitāputrau vijānīyād brāhmaṇas tu tayoḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: should be regarded as father and son; of the two, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is the father.

children.text: viprāṇāṃ jñānato jyaiṣṭhyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu vīryataḥ
children.translated_text: Among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, seniority is by knowledge; among <s>kṣatriyas</s>, by valor;
among <s>vaiśyas</s>, by grain and wealth; among <s>śūdras</s>, by birth alone.

children.text: atha puruṣasya kāmakrodhalobhākhyaṃ riputrayaṃ sughoraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Now there is, for a person, a terribly fearsome threefold enemy called desire, anger, and greed.
It exists especially for a householder, because of attachment to possessions.
Overcome by that, he engages in exceedingly grave sins, great sins, secondary great sins, and minor sins;
in acts that cause loss of caste, in acts that produce mixture, and in acts that make one unfit to receive gifts;
and in acts that bring defilement and in miscellaneous offenses.
This is the threefold gate of hell, destructive of the self:

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: desire, anger, and greed; therefore one should abandon this triad.
Intercourse with one's mother, intercourse with one's daughter, and intercourse with one's daughter-in-law: these are exceedingly grave sins.
These perpetrators of exceedingly grave sins should enter fire;

children.text: na hyanyā niṣkṛtis teṣāṃ vidyate hi kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: for there is no other expiation for them in any way.

children.text: brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ brāhmaṇasuvarṇaharaṇaṃ gurudāragamanam iti mahāpātakāni ||
children.translated_text: Killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, drinking liquor, stealing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s gold, and intercourse with the teacher's wife: these are the great sins.
And association with such offenders is also one.
One falls within a year by associating with a fallen man:
by sharing the same vehicle, food, seat, and bed.
But through sexual connection, Vedic-teaching connection, and chief forms of connection, one falls immediately.
These perpetrators of great sins may be purified by a horse sacrifice
and also by visiting all the sacred fords on earth.

children.text: yāgasthasya kṣatriyasya vaiśyasya ca rajasvalāyāś cāntarvatnyāś cātrigotrāyāś cāvijñātasya garbhasya śaraṇāgatasya ca ghātanaṃ brahmahatyāsamānīti ||
children.translated_text: The killing of a <s>kṣatriya</s> or a <s>vaiśya</s> engaged in sacrifice, of a menstruating woman, of a pregnant woman, of a woman of the <s>Atri</s> lineage, of a fetus whose sex is unknown, or of one who has sought refuge is equal to killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
False testimony and the killing of a friend: these two are equal to drinking liquor.
The seizure of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s land and the seizure of a deposit are equal to stealing gold.
Intercourse with the wife of a paternal uncle, maternal grandfather, maternal uncle, father-in-law, or king is equal to intercourse with the teacher's wife.
So too intercourse with one's father's sister, mother's sister, or sister.
And intercourse with the wife of a learned <s>śrotriya</s>, officiating priest, <s>upādhyāya</s>, or friend.

children.text: svasuḥ sakhyāḥ sagotrāyā uttamavarṇāyāḥ kumāryā antyajāyā rajasvalāyāḥ śaraṇāgatāyāḥ pravrajitāyā nikṣiptāyāś ca ||
children.translated_text: So too with one's sister, a female friend, a woman of the same lineage, a maiden of a higher varṇa, an outcaste woman, a menstruating woman, a woman who has sought refuge, a renunciant woman, or a woman entrusted to one's care.
These perpetrators of secondary great sins, like perpetrators of great sins,
are purified by a horse sacrifice or by visiting sacred fords.
Speaking falsely for self-exaltation;
slander that reaches the king;
and the obstinate assertion of a falsehood against one's teacher;
reviling the Veda;
and abandonment of what has been studied;
and abandonment of fire, father, mother, son, and wife;
eating forbidden food or food not fit to be eaten;
taking another's property;
intercourse with another's wife;
officiating at a sacrifice for one for whom one should not officiate;
living by improper work;
and accepting gifts from unworthy persons;
killing a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>, a <s>śūdra</s>, or a cow;
selling what must not be sold;
for a younger brother who has married before the elder brother, the elder brother's
marriage after him;
and giving a daughter to that man;
and officiating for him;
becoming a <s>vrātya</s> (one outside Vedic discipline);
teaching for hire;
and taking instruction from a paid teacher;
supervision over all mines;
setting great machines in motion;
injury to trees, shrubs, creepers, vines, and medicinal plants;
living by means of a woman;
and engaging in rites of sorcery and destructive magic;
beginning a rite for one's own sake;
not maintaining the sacred fires;
failure to discharge the debts owed to gods, seers, and ancestors;
resorting to false scriptures;
atheism;
being an actor or dancer;
association with drinkers of liquor and with women;
these are minor sins.
Men who have committed these minor sins should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> penance;

children.text: parākaṃ ca tathā kuryur yajeyur gosavena vā ||
children.translated_text: they should likewise perform the <s>parāka</s>, or sacrifice with the <s>gosava</s>.
Causing bodily pain to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;
Smelling what should not be smelled, and smelling liquor.
Crookedness.
Engaging in sexual intercourse among animals.
And with a male.
These are acts that cause <s>jātibhraṃśa</s> (fall from caste).
Having intentionally committed any one act that causes <s>jātibhraṃśa</s>,
one should perform the <s>sāṃtapana kṛcchra</s>; if unintentionally, the <s>prājāpatya</s>.
Injury to domestic and wild animals is <s>saṃkarīkaraṇa</s> (causing mixture).
Having committed <s>saṃkarīkaraṇa</s>, one should eat barley-gruel for a month,
or else one should undertake the <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> as the expiation.

children.text: ninditebhyo dhanādānaṃ vāṇijyaṃ kusīdajīvanam asatyabhāṣaṇaṃ śūdrasevanam ityapātrīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Taking wealth from blameworthy persons, trade, living by usury, speaking falsehood, and serving a <s>śūdra</s>: this is <s>apātrīkaraṇa</s> (making oneself unworthy).
Having committed <s>apātrīkaraṇa</s>, one is purified by the <s>taptakṛcchra</s>,
or again by the <s>śītakṛcchra</s>, or by the <s>mahāsāṃtapana</s>.
Killing birds, aquatic creatures, and water-born beings,
and worms and insects,
and eating what has followed after liquor:
these are acts that bring impurity.
For acts that cause pollution, the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> is the purification,
or else the <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> is the purifying expiation.
What has not been stated is miscellaneous.
In the case of a miscellaneous sin, after considering its heaviness and lightness,
a wise person should perform an expiation as approved by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Now, the hells.
<s>Tāmisra</s>.
<s>Andhatāmisra</s>.
<s>Raurava</s>.
<s>Mahāraurava</s>.
<s>Kālasūtra</s>.
<s>Mahānaraka</s>.
<s>Saṃjīvana</s>.
<s>Avīci</s>.
<s>Tapana</s>.
<s>Saṃpratāpana</s>.
<s>Saṃghātaka</s>.
<s>Kākola</s>.
<s>Kuḍmala</s>.
<s>Pūtimṛttika</s>.
<s>Lohaśaṅku</s>.
<s>Ṛbīsa</s>.
<s>Viṣamapanthā</s>.
<s>Kaṇṭakaśālmali</s>.
<s>Dīpanadī</s>.
<s>Asipatravana</s>.
And <s>Lohacāraka</s>.

children.text: eteṣv akṛtaprāyaścittā atipātakinaḥ paryāyeṇa kalpaṃ pacyante ||
children.translated_text: In these, those guilty of the gravest sins who have not performed expiation are cooked in turn for a <s>kalpa</s>.
Those guilty of great sins are cooked for a <s>manvantara</s>.
And those guilty of secondary great sins as well.
Those guilty of lesser sins are cooked for a four-age cycle.
And those who have committed <s>saṃkarīkaraṇa</s> for a thousand years.
And those who have committed acts causing <s>jātibhraṃśa</s> likewise.
And those who have committed <s>apātrīkaraṇa</s> likewise.
And those who have committed acts causing pollution likewise.
And those guilty of miscellaneous sins for many heaps of years.
Wicked people who have committed sins, immediately after giving up their life,

children.text: yāmyaṃ panthānam āsādya duḥkham aśnanti dāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: reach the path of <s>Yama</s> and undergo dreadful suffering.

children.text: yamasya puruṣair ghoraiḥ kṛṣyamāṇā yatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Dragged this way and that by the terrible servants of <s>Yama</s>,
they are led along in great distress and pain.
By dogs, jackals, flesh-eaters, crows, vultures, herons, and the like,
by fire-mouthed beings, by snakes, and also by scorpions, they are devoured.

children.text: agninā dahyamānāś ca tudyamānāś ca kaṇṭakaiḥ
children.translated_text: They are burned by fire and pierced by thorns,

children.text: krakacaiḥ pāṭyamānāś ca pīḍyamānāś ca tṛṣṇayā ||
children.translated_text: sawn apart by saws and tormented by thirst.

children.text: kṣudhayā vyathamānāś ca ghorair vyāghragaṇais tathā
children.translated_text: They are afflicted by hunger and by terrible packs of tigers,
and they faint at every step from the smell of pus and blood.
Longing for another's food and drink, they are beaten by attendants
whose faces resemble those of fearsome crows, vultures, herons, and the like.

children.text: kvacit tailena kvāthyante tāḍyante musalaiḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: In one place they are boiled in oil; in another they are beaten with pestles.

children.text: āyasīṣu ca vaṭyante śilāsu ca tathā kvacit ||
children.translated_text: And in another place they are rolled on iron surfaces, and likewise on stones.

children.text: kvacid vāntam athāśnanti kvacit pūyam asṛk kvacit
children.translated_text: In one place they eat vomit; in another, pus; in another, blood.

children.text: kvacid viṣṭhāṃ kvacin māṃsaṃ pūyagandhi sudāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: In one place they eat feces; in another, flesh, terribly foul with the smell of pus.
In some places they remain in dreadful darkness,
and they are devoured by worms and by very terrible fire-mouthed beings.
In one place they are oppressed by cold; in another they stand amid filth.
In one place, the dreadful ghosts eat one another.

children.text: kvacid bhūtena tāḍyante lambamānās tathā kvacit
children.translated_text: In one place they are beaten by a spirit; in another, they hang suspended.

children.text: kvacit kṣipyanti bāṇaughair utkṛtyante tathā kvacit ||
children.translated_text: In one place they are struck by showers of arrows, and in another they are cut to pieces.
Their feet are placed on thorns, and they are encircled by the coils of snakes.

children.text: pīḍyamānās tathā yantraiḥ kṛṣyamāṇāś ca jānubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are tormented by machines and dragged by their knees.
Their backs, heads, and necks are broken; their throats are needle-like and very terrible.
Their bodies are as large as mansions and capable of enduring torment.
Thus sinners, after experiencing their sin and being deeply miserable,
enter animal wombs and many kinds of suffering.
Now, for those of sinful self who have experienced suffering in the hells, there are animal wombs.
For those guilty of the gravest sins, there are in turn all stationary wombs.
And for those guilty of great sins, worm wombs.
For those guilty of secondary great sins, bird wombs.
For those guilty of lesser sins, water-born wombs.
For those who have committed acts causing <s>jātibhraṃśa</s>, aquatic wombs.
For those who have committed acts of <s>saṃkarīkaraṇa</s>, deer wombs.
For those who have committed acts of <s>apātrīkaraṇa</s>, domestic-animal wombs.
For those who have committed acts causing pollution, untouchable wombs among human beings.
In the miscellaneous cases, they become miscellaneous violent flesh-eaters.
One who eats food that should not be eaten, and what is forbidden as food, becomes a worm.
A thief becomes a hawk.
One who steals from a principal road becomes a burrow-dweller.
A grain-stealer becomes a mouse.
A stealer of bronze becomes a goose.
A water-stealer becomes a water-plunging creature.
A stealer of honey becomes a biting insect.
A stealer of milk becomes a crow.
A stealer of juice becomes a dog.
A stealer of ghee becomes a mongoose.
A stealer of meat becomes a vulture.
A stealer of fat becomes a cormorant.
A stealer of oil becomes an oil-drinker.
A stealer of salt becomes a <s>cīvivāka</s> bird.
A stealer of curds becomes a crane.
Having stolen silk, one becomes a partridge.
A stealer of linen becomes a frog.
A stealer of cotton cloth becomes a <s>krauñca</s> bird.
A stealer of a cow becomes a monitor lizard.
A stealer of molasses becomes a <s>vālguda</s> creature.
A stealer of perfumes becomes a musk-rat.
A stealer of leafy vegetables becomes a peacock.
A stealer of prepared food becomes a <s>sedhā</s> creature.
A stealer of uncooked food becomes a porcupine.
A stealer of fire becomes a heron.
A stealer of household equipment becomes a house-haunting creature.
A stealer of red garments becomes a <s>jīvajīvaka</s> bird.
A stealer of an elephant becomes a tortoise.
A stealer of a horse becomes a tiger.
A stealer of fruit or flowers becomes a monkey.
A stealer of a woman becomes a bear.
A stealer of a vehicle becomes a camel.
A stealer of livestock becomes a vulture.

children.text: yad vā tad vā paradravyam apahṛtya balān naraḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever property of another a man forcibly takes away,

children.text: avaśyam yāti tiryaktvaṃ jagdhvā caivāhutaṃ haviḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also after eating sacrificial oblation that has not been offered, he necessarily goes to animal existence.
Women too, by this same rule, incur fault after stealing,

children.text: eteṣām eva jantūnāṃ bhāryātvam upayānti tāḥ ||
