children.translated_text: and they become wives of those very creatures.

children.text: narakābhibhūtaduḥkhānāṃ tiryaktvam uttīrṇānāṃ mānuṣyeṣu lakṣaṇāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For those whose sufferings in hell have overwhelmed them and who have passed through animal existence, there are bodily marks among human beings.
One guilty of an extreme sin is leprous.
A killer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is consumptive.
A drinker of liquor has darkened teeth.
A stealer of gold has bad nails.
One who violates his teacher's bed has diseased skin.
A slanderer has a foul nose.
An informer has a foul mouth.
A grain-thief is missing a limb.
A thief of mixed goods has an extra limb.
A stealer of food is sickly.
A stealer of speech is mute.
A stealer of cloth has white leprosy.
A horse-thief is lame.
One who reviles gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is mute.
A poisoner has a lolling tongue.
An incendiary is insane.
One who acts against his teacher is epileptic.
A cow-killer is blind,
and so is a stealer of a lamp.
A lamp-extinguisher is one-eyed.
A seller of tin, chowries, and lead becomes a washerman.
A seller of one-hoofed animals becomes a hunter.
One who eats from a <s>kuṇḍa</s> has a vulva-like mouth.
A thief becomes a bell-ringer.
A usurer suffers from vertigo.
One who eats delicacies alone has a wind-swelling.
A breaker of agreements is bald.
A violator of chastity has elephantiasis.
One who destroys another's livelihood is poor.
One who causes pain to others has a long illness.
Thus, according to the particular action, people are born bearing marks,
afflicted with diseases, and also blind, hunchbacked, lame, or one-eyed.

children.text: vāmanā badhirā mūkā durbalāś ca tathāpare
children.translated_text: Others are dwarfish, deaf, mute, and weak;
therefore one should perform expiation with every effort.
Now there are the <s>kṛcchra</s> penances.
For three days one should not eat.
And each day one should perform bathing at the three libation-times.
At each bath there is immersion in the waters three times.
While immersed, one should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times.
By day, while standing, one should remain standing.
At night, one should remain seated.
At the end of the rite one should give a milch cow.
This is the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> penance.

children.text: tryahaṃ sāyaṃ tryahaṃ prātas tryaham ayācitam aśnīyāt
children.translated_text: For three days one should eat in the evening, for three days in the morning, and for three days what is obtained unasked;
this is the <s>Prājāpatya</s> penance.

children.text: tryaham uṣṇāḥ pibed apas tryaham uṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ tryaham uṣṇaṃ payas tryahaṃ ca nāśnīyād eṣa taptakṛcchraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three days one should drink hot water, for three days hot ghee, for three days hot milk, and for three days one should not eat; this is the <s>taptakṛcchra</s>.
With these same items cold, it is the <s>śītakṛcchra</s>.
The <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> is passing twenty-one days on milk.
The <s>udakakṛcchra</s> is the eating of water and barley-meal for a month.
The <s>mūlakṛcchra</s> is the eating of lotus-fibres.
The <s>śrīphalakṛcchra</s> is the eating of bilva fruits.
Or it may be done with lotus seeds.
For one who takes no food for twelve days, it is the <s>parāka</s> penance.

children.text: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakāny ekadivasam aśnīyāt
children.translated_text: One should consume cow urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, and water infused with <s>kuśa</s> grass for one day;
on the second day one should fast.
This is the <s>sāṃtapana</s> penance.
The <s>mahāsāṃtapana</s> is performed by repeating cow urine and the rest each day.
And the <s>atisāṃtapana</s> is performed by repeating them for three days.
The <s>tulāpuruṣa</s> consists of eating oil-cake, rice-water, buttermilk, water, and barley-meal, with fasts in between.

The <s>parṇakṛcchra</s> consists of drinking, one by one, water boiled with leaves of <s>kuśa</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, lotus, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, banyan, <s>brāhmī</s>, and <s>suvarcalā</s>.
One should perform all these <s>kṛcchra</s> penances after having shaved,
constantly bathing at the three libation-times, sleeping on the ground, and controlling the senses.
One should avoid excessive conversation with women, <s>śūdras</s>, and the fallen,

children.text: pavitrāṇi japen nityaṃ juhuyāc caiva śaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and should recite purificatory texts constantly and make oblations according to one's ability.
Now, the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> penance.
One should eat fixed mouthfuls of food.

children.text: tāṃś candrakalābhivṛddhau vardhayet hānau hrāsayet amāvāsyāyāṃ nāśnīyāt
children.translated_text: One should increase them as the lunar digits wax and decrease them as they wane; on the new-moon day one should not eat.
This is the barley-middle <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
Or it is the ant-middle form.
The one in which the new moon falls in the middle is the ant-middle form.
The one in which the full moon falls there is the barley-middle form.

children.text: aṣṭau grāsān pratidivasaṃ māsam aśnīyāt sa yaticāndrāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If one eats eight mouthfuls each day for a month, that is the ascetic's <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātaś caturaś caturaḥ sa śiśucāndrāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Four in the evening and four in the morning is the child's <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: yathā kathaṃcit ṣaṣṭyonāṃ triśatīṃ māsenāśnīyāt sa sāmānyacāndrāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, in whatever way, one eats two hundred and forty mouthfuls in a month, that is the ordinary <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: vratam etat purā bhūmiṃ kṛtvā saptarṣayo 'malāḥ
children.translated_text: Having performed this vow on earth in ancient times, the stainless <s>Saptarṣis</s>

children.text: prāptavantaḥ paraṃ sthānaṃ brahmā rudras tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: attained the highest station, and so too did <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: atha karmabhir ātmakṛtair gurum ātmānaṃ manyetātmārthe prasṛtiyāvakaṃ śrapayet ||
children.translated_text: Now, because of actions done by oneself, one should regard oneself as burdened; for one's own sake one should cook a handful of barley-gruel.
One should not then offer it in the fire.
Nor is there a <s>bali</s> offering here.
One should consecrate with mantras what is uncooked, what is being cooked, and what is cooked.
While it is being cooked, one should protect it.

children.text: brahmā devānāṃ padavīḥ kavīnām ṛṣir viprāṇāṃ mahiṣo mṛgāṇām
children.translated_text: The <s>brahmā</s> priest is the guide of the gods, the seer of poets, the sage of the inspired, the buffalo among beasts...

children.text: śyeno gṛdhrāṇāṃ svadhitir vanānāṃ somaḥ pavitram atyeti rebhan ||
children.translated_text: The hawk among vultures, the axe among forests, Soma, roaring, passes through the purifier.
With this, he binds the darbha grasses.

children.text: śṛtaṃ ca tam aśnīyāt pātre niṣicya ||
children.translated_text: And he should eat that cooked thing, after pouring it into a vessel.

children.text: ye devā manojātā manojuṣaḥ sudakṣā dakṣapitaras te naḥ pāntu te no 'vantu tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhety ātmani juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: With the formula, 'May the gods born of mind, delighting in mind, very skillful, whose father is Skill, protect us; may they guard us. Homage to them; svāhā to them,' he should make an oblation into himself.
Then, having sipped water, he should touch his navel.

children.text: snātāḥ pītā bhavata yūyam āpo 'smākam udare yavāḥ tā asmabhyam anamīvā ayakṣmā anāgasaḥ santu devīr amṛtā ṛtāvṛdha iti ||
children.translated_text: With the formula, 'You waters, be bathed and drunk; barley-grains are in our belly. May those divine, immortal, truth-increasing waters be for us free from sickness, free from wasting disease, and free from guilt.'
One who seeks intelligence should do this for three nights.
One who has committed sin should do it for six nights.
Having drunk it for seven nights, it purifies one who is any one of the great sinners.
By twelve nights it burns away even sin committed by one's ancestors.
Having drunk it for a month, it burns away all sins.
And for barley-grains taken from cow excrement, the period is twenty-one nights.
You are barley; you are the king of grains, belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s>, mixed with honey.
You are the expeller of all sins, a purifier upheld by the seers.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ yavā madhu yavā āpo vā amṛtaṃ yavāḥ
children.translated_text: Ghee is barley; honey is barley; the waters are barley; barley is immortality.

children.text: sarve punīta me pāpaṃ yan me kiṃcana duṣkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: All of you purify my sin, whatever evil deed of mine there is.
What was done by speech, what was done by action, what was badly conceived by the mind,

children.text: alakṣmīṃ kālakarṇīṃ ca nāśayadhvaṃ yavā mama ||
children.translated_text: and misfortune and <s>Kālakarṇī</s>: destroy them for me, O barley-grains.
What has been licked by a dog or pig, and what has been spoiled by leftovers,

children.text: mātāpitror aśuśrūṣāṃ tat punīdhvaṃ yavā mama ||
children.translated_text: and failure to serve my mother and father: purify that for me, O barley-grains.
Food of a group, food of a courtesan, food of a <s>Śūdra</s>, impurity connected with <s>śrāddha</s>,

children.text: caurasyānnaṃ navaśrāddhaṃ punīdhvaṃ ca yavā mama ||
children.translated_text: a thief's food and a new <s>śrāddha</s>: purify these for me, O barley-grains.

children.text: bāladhūrtam adharmaṃ ca rājadvārakṛtaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Childish deceit, <s>adharma</s>, and whatever was done at the king's gate,
stealing gold, breach of the vow, and officiating at the sacrifice of one for whom one should not sacrifice,

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ parīvādaṃ punīdhvaṃ ca yavā mama ||
children.translated_text: and slander of Brahmins: purify these for me, O barley-grains.

children.text: mārgaśīrṣaśuklaikādaśyām upoṣito dvādaśyāṃ bhagavantaṃ śrīvāsudevam arcayet ||
children.translated_text: On the bright eleventh day of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, after fasting, on the twelfth day he should worship the blessed <s>Śrīvāsudeva</s>.
He should do so with flowers, incense, anointments, lamps, and food-offerings, and with offerings to fire and the satisfying of Brahmins.

children.text: vratam etat saṃvatsaraṃ kṛtvā pāpebhyaḥ pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having performed this vow for a year, he becomes purified from sins.
Having performed it for as long as he lives, he reaches <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>.
In the same way, on the twelfth days of both fortnights, within a year he reaches the heavenly world.
Having performed it for as long as he lives, he reaches <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>.
Exactly so also on the fifteenth lunar days.
On the new-moon day, as one become <s>Brahman</s>, and likewise on the full-moon day,
serving <s>Keśava</s> as one become joined in yoga, he attains the great goal.
On the day on which the moon and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> are seen together in the sky,

children.text: paurṇamāsī tu mahatī proktā saṃvatsare tu sā ||
children.translated_text: that full-moon day in the year is declared to be great.
On that day, giving, fasting, and the like are proclaimed inexhaustible,
and likewise the bright twelfth day that is joined with <s>Śravaṇa</s>.
Having made a leaf-hut in the forest, he should dwell there.
He should bathe three times a day.

children.text: svakarma cācakṣāṇo grāme grāme bhaikṣyam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: And, declaring his own deed, he should go for alms in village after village.
He should sleep on grass.
This is the <s>mahāvrata</s> (great vow).
Having killed a Brahmin, he should perform it for twelve years.
Or after killing a <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s> engaged in sacrifice.
Or after killing a pregnant woman or a menstruating woman.
Or a woman of the <s>Atri</s> lineage.
Or a friend.
For the killing of a king, he should perform that same <s>mahāvrata</s> doubled.
For the killing of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, three quarters of it should be performed.
For the killing of a <s>Vaiśya</s>, half.
For the killing of a <s>Śūdra</s>, half of that.
In all these cases, he should carry the head of the corpse as his banner.

children.text: māsam ekaṃ kṛtavāpano gavām anugamanaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: For one month, with his hair shaved, he should follow cows.
When they sit, he should sit.
And when they stand, he should stand.
And he should lift up those that have fallen.
And he should protect them from dangers.
Without first providing protection from cold and the like for them, he should not provide it for himself.
He should bathe with cow urine.
And he should subsist on products of the cow.
He should perform this <s>govrata</s> (cow vow) for killing a cow.
Having killed an elephant, he should give five dark-blue bulls.
For a horse, he should give a garment.
For killing a donkey, he should give a one-year-old draught ox.
And the same for killing a sheep or a goat.
For killing a camel, he should give a <s>kṛṣṇala</s> of gold.
Having killed a dog, he should fast for three nights.

children.text: hatvā mūṣakamārjāranakulamaṇḍūkaḍuṇḍubhājagarāṇām anyatamam upoṣitaḥ kṛsaraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayitvā lohadaṇḍaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having killed any one of a mouse, cat, mongoose, frog, water-snake, or python, after fasting he should feed a Brahmin with <s>kṛsara</s> and give an iron staff as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.
For killing a monitor lizard, owl, crow, or fish, he should fast for three nights.
Having killed any one of a swan, crane, heron, cormorant, monkey, hawk, vulture, or cakravāka bird, he should give a cow to a Brahmin.
Having killed a snake, he should give a black-iron spade.
Having killed a eunuch, he should give a load of straw.
Having killed a boar, he should give a jar of ghee.
For a partridge, he should give a <s>droṇa</s> of sesame.
For a parrot, he should give a two-year-old calf.
For a krauñca bird, he should give a three-year-old animal.
For killing a carnivorous wild animal, he should give a milch cow.
For killing a non-carnivorous wild animal, he should give a young heifer.
For killing an unmentioned wild animal, he should subsist on milk for three nights.
For killing a bird, he should eat only at night.
Or he should give a <s>māṣa</s> of silver.
Having killed an aquatic creature, he should fast.
But in the destruction of a thousand boneless living beings,

children.text: pūrṇe cānasy anasthnāṃ tu śūdrahatyāvrataṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: and when a full cart-load of boneless beings has been killed, he should perform the vow for killing a <s>Śūdra</s>.

children.text: kiṃcid eva tu viprāya dadyād asthimatāṃ vadhe
children.translated_text: In the killing of creatures with bones, he should give at least something to a Brahmin,
and for injury to boneless creatures he is purified by breath-control.

children.text: phaladānāṃ tu vṛkṣāṇāṃ chedane japyam ṛkśatam
children.translated_text: For cutting fruit-bearing trees, one should recite one hundred Ṛg verses as <s>japa</s>.
The same applies for shrubs, creepers, vines, flowering plants, and herbs.
For living beings born from food, and for all those born from sap,
and for those arising from fruit and flowers, sipping ghee is the purification.

children.text: kṛṣṭajānām oṣadhīnāṃ jātānāṃ ca svayaṃ vane
children.translated_text: For cultivated herbs and those that grow by themselves in the forest,
if one has taken them uselessly, one should follow a cow for one day, observing a milk-vow.
A drinker of <s>surā</s> (liquor), excluded from all rites, should eat coarse grains for a year.

children.text: malānāṃ madyānāṃ cānyatamasya prāśane cāndrāyaṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: On drinking any one of the impure kinds of liquor or other intoxicants, one should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).
The same applies on eating garlic, onion, leeks, things with such a smell, excrement, pork, village fowl, monkey meat, or beef.

children.text: sarveṣv eteṣu dvijānāṃ prāyaścittānte bhūyaḥ saṃskāraṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In all these cases, for twice-born men, after the expiation is complete, the consecration should be performed again.
In the rite of re-consecration, shaving, the girdle, the staff, the practice of begging, and the vows are to be omitted.
For eating the flesh of five-nailed animals, except hare, porcupine, iguana, rhinoceros, and tortoise, one should fast for seven nights.
Having eaten the food of a corporate group, a courtesan, a thief, or a singer, one should subsist on milk for seven nights.
The same applies to the food of a carpenter and of a leather-worker.
And to that of a usurer, a miser, an initiated sacrificer, one bound in fetters, one accused of grave sin, and a eunuch.
And to that of an unchaste woman, a hypocrite, a physician, a hunter, a cruel man, a fierce man, and eaters of leftovers.
And to that of a woman without a male protector, a goldsmith, a rival, and fallen persons.
And to that of slanderers, liars, those whose religious conduct is damaged, and sellers of liquids or essences.
And to that of actors, weavers, ingrates, and washermen.
And to that of artisans, Niṣādas, stage performers, lute-players, and sellers of weapons.
And to that of those who live by dogs, distillers, oilmen, and washers of clothes.
And to that from the houses of menstruating women and women living with a paramour.

children.text: bhrūṇaghnāvekṣitam udakyāsaṃspṛṣṭaṃ patatriṇāvalīḍhaṃ śunā saṃspṛṣṭaṃ gavāghrātaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The same applies to food looked at by an embryo-killer, touched by a menstruating woman, licked by a bird, touched by a dog, or smelled by a cow.
And to food deliberately touched by the foot or sneezed upon.
And to the food of the intoxicated, the angry, and the sick.
And to food not respectfully offered, and to meat killed in vain.
For eating the flesh of any fish except pāṭhīna, rohita, rājīva, siṃhatuṇḍa, and śakula, one should fast for three nights.
The same applies to eating the flesh of any aquatic creature.

children.text: āpaḥ surābhāṇḍasthāḥ pītvā saptarātraṃ śaṅkhapuṣpīśṛtaṃ payaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Having drunk water kept in a vessel for <s>surā</s>, one should drink milk boiled with śaṅkhapuṣpī for seven nights.
And for water kept in a vessel for other liquor, for five nights.

children.text: somapaḥ surāpasyāghrāya gandham udakamagnas trir aghamarṣaṇaṃ japtvā ghṛtaprāśanam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: A Soma-drinker who has smelled the odor of a <s>surā</s>-drinker should plunge into water, recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times, and perform the sipping of ghee.
For eating the flesh of a donkey, camel, or crow, one should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
The same applies after eating unknown food, food from a slaughterhouse, or dried meat.
For eating the flesh of carnivorous beasts or birds, one should perform the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated difficult penance).
For eating kalaviṅka, plavaka, cakravāka, haṃsa, rajjudāla, sārasa, dātyūha, parrot, myna, crane, heron, cuckoo, or khañjarīṭa, one should fast for three nights.
The same applies to eating animals with a single hoof or with teeth in both jaws.
For eating the flesh of any bird except partridge, kapiñjala, quail, varttikā, and peacock, one should fast for a day and night.
For eating insects, one should drink <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s> for one day.
The same applies to eating dog flesh.
For eating chattrāka and kavaka mushrooms, one should perform the <s>sāṃtapana</s> penance.

children.text: yavagodhūmapayovikāraṃ snehāktaṃ śuktaṃ khāṇḍavaṃ ca varjayitvā yat paryuṣitaṃ tat prāśyopavaset ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten any stale food, except barley, wheat, milk-products, fat-smeared preparations, sour gruel, and <s>khāṇḍava</s>, one should fast.
The same applies to red exudations of trees arising from cutting or from impure causes.
And to śālūka roots, improperly prepared kṛsara, saṃyāva, milk-rice, cakes, śaṣkulī cakes, food for deities, and oblations.
And to all milks except those of the cow, goat, and buffalo.
Even those milks are forbidden when ten days have not yet passed after birth.
And the milk of a syandinī, a saṃdhinī, or a cow whose calf is absent.
And milk from animals that eat impure things.
And sour preparations taken by themselves, except for curds.
A student in the <s>brahmacarya</s> stage who eats at a <s>śrāddha</s> meal should fast for three nights.
And for one day he should remain in water.
For eating honey and meat, the <s>prājāpatya</s> penance is prescribed.
On eating leftovers from a cat, crow, mongoose, or mouse, one should drink <s>brahmasuvarcalā</s>.

children.text: śvocchiṣṭāśane dinam ekam upoṣitaḥ pañcagavyaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: On eating leftovers from a dog, after fasting for one day, one should drink <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow).
For eating the excrement or urine of five-nailed animals, one should fast for seven nights.
On eating an uncooked <s>śrāddha</s> offering, one should subsist on milk for three nights.
A Brāhmaṇa who eats leftovers from a Śūdra should fast for seven nights.
On eating leftovers from a Vaiśya, he should fast for five nights.
On eating leftovers from a Kṣatriya, he should fast for three nights.
But on eating leftovers from a Brāhmaṇa, he should fast for one day.
A Kṣatriya who eats leftovers from a Śūdra should fast for five nights.
If he eats leftovers from a Vaiśya, he should fast for three nights.
A Vaiśya who eats leftovers from a Śūdra should do the same.
Having eaten food from a Caṇḍāla, one should fast for three nights.
Having eaten cooked food from him, the <s>parāka</s> penance is prescribed.

children.text: asaṃskṛtān paśūn mantrair nādyād vipraḥ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: A Brāhmaṇa should never eat animals that have not been consecrated with mantras,

children.text: mantrais tu saṃskṛtān adyācchāśvataṃ vidhim āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but, adhering to the eternal rule, he may eat those consecrated with mantras.
As many hairs as there are on the animal, so many acts of killing here

children.text: vṛthā paśughnaḥ prāpnoti pretya ceha ca niṣkṛtim ||
children.translated_text: does the needless killer of an animal incur, both after death and in this world, as requital.

children.text: yajñārthaṃ paśavaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayam eva svayaṃbhuvā
children.translated_text: Animals were created for sacrifice by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> himself.

children.text: yajño hi bhūtyai sarvasya tasmād yajñe vadho 'vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For sacrifice is for the welfare of all; therefore killing in sacrifice is non-killing.

children.text: na tādṛśaṃ bhavaty eno mṛgahantur dhanārthinaḥ
children.translated_text: Such guilt does not arise for a hunter seeking wealth

children.text: yādṛśaṃ bhavati pretya vṛthā māṃsāni khādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as arises after death for one who eats meat needlessly.

children.text: oṣadhyaḥ paśavo vṛkṣās tiryañcaḥ pakṣiṇas tathā
children.translated_text: Herbs, animals, trees, beasts, and likewise birds

children.text: yajñārthaṃ nidhanam prāptāḥ prāpnuvanty ucchritīḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who meet death for the sake of sacrifice attain exalted states again.
At a <s>madhuparka</s> (honorific honey-mixture offering), at a sacrifice, and in rites for ancestors and deities,
animals may be killed only there, and never anywhere else under any circumstances.
A twice-born man who knows the true meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, when killing animals for sacrificial purposes,

children.text: ātmānaṃ ca paśūṃś caiva gamayatyuttamāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: causes both himself and the animals to go to the highest state.

children.text: gṛhe gurāvaraṇye vā nivasann ātmavān dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether living in the house of his guru or in the forest, a self-controlled twice-born man
must not practice violence not enjoined by the <s>Veda</s>, even in distress.
That violence which is enjoined by the <s>Veda</s>, fixed in this world of moving and unmoving beings,

children.text: ahiṃsām eva tāṃ vidyād vedād dharmo hi nirbabhau ||
children.translated_text: one should know to be non-violence itself, for <s>dharma</s> has arisen from the <s>Veda</s>.
One who harms harmless beings out of a desire for his own pleasure

children.text: sa jīvaṃś ca mṛtaś caiva na kvacit sukham edhate ||
children.translated_text: does not prosper in happiness anywhere, either living or dead.
One who does not wish to cause bondage, killing, and pain to living beings,

children.text: sa sarvasya hitaprepsuḥ sukham atyantam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: seeking the welfare of all, enjoys endless happiness.

children.text: yad dhyāyati yat kurute ratiṃ badhnāti yatra ca
children.translated_text: Whatever one thinks of, whatever one does, and whatever one fixes his delight upon,

children.text: tad evāpnoty ayatnena yo hinasti na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: that very thing he obtains without effort, if he does not harm anything.

children.text: nākṛtvā prāṇināṃ hiṃsāṃ māṃsam utpadyate kvacit
children.translated_text: Meat never comes into being without violence toward living beings,

children.text: na ca prāṇivadhaḥ svargyas tasmān māṃsaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: and killing living beings does not lead to heaven; therefore one should avoid meat.

children.text: samutpattiṃ ca māṃsasya vadhabandhau ca dehinām
children.translated_text: Having fully considered the origin of meat and the slaughter and bondage of embodied beings,
one should turn away from eating every kind of meat.

children.text: na bhakṣayati yo māṃsaṃ vidhiṃ hitvā piśācavat
children.translated_text: One who does not eat meat, abandoning the practice as one would a demonic act,

children.text: sa loke priyatāṃ yāti vyādhibhiś ca na pīḍyate ||
children.translated_text: becomes beloved in the world and is not afflicted by diseases.
The approver, the cutter, the killer, the buyer and seller,

children.text: saṃskartā copahartā ca khādakaś ceti ghātakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the preparer, the server, and the eater: these are all killers.
There is no greater wrongdoer than one who wishes to increase his own flesh by another's flesh
without first honoring the ancestors and gods.

children.text: varṣe varṣe 'śvamedhena yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ
children.translated_text: One man may sacrifice every year with the <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) for a hundred years,

children.text: māṃsāni ca na khāded yas tayoḥ puṇyaphalaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: and another may not eat meats; the meritorious fruit of the two is equal.
With divine foods of fruits and roots and with the foods eaten by sages,

children.text: na tat phalam avāpnoti yan māṃsaparivarjanāt ||
children.translated_text: one does not obtain that fruit which comes from abstaining from meat.

children.text: māṃ sa bhakṣayitāmutra yasya māṃsam ihādmyaham
children.translated_text: 'He will eat me there whose meat I eat here':
the wise declare this to be the meat-ness of meat.
One who has stolen gold should declare the act to the king and hand over a pestle.
He becomes purified either by being killed or by renunciation.
Or he should perform the <s>mahāvrata</s> (great vow) for twelve years.
The same applies to one who steals a deposit.
One who steals grain or money should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> (austerity) for a year.
For stealing a human being, a woman, a well, a field, or a reservoir, the penance is <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
For objects of little value, the penance is <s>sāṃtapana</s>.
For stealing things to be eaten, prepared food, vehicles, beds, seats, flowers, roots, or fruits, one should drink the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five products of the cow).
For stealing grass, wood, trees, dry grain, jaggery, cloth, leather, or meat, one should fast for three nights.
For stealing jewels, pearls, coral, copper, silver, iron, or bronze, one should eat broken grains for twelve days.
For stealing cotton, silk, wool, and the like, one should subsist on milk for three nights.
For stealing two-hoofed or one-hoofed animals, one should fast for two nights.
For stealing birds, perfumes, medicinal herbs, ropes, or wicker articles, one should fast for a day.
After giving back the stolen property itself, by some means, even to the creditor or owner,
one should then perform penance for the removal of the stain.

children.text: yad yat parebhyas tv ādadyāt puruṣas tu niraṅkuśaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever a lawless man takes from others,

children.text: tena tena vihīnaḥ syād yatra yatrābhijāyate ||
children.translated_text: of that very thing he will be deprived wherever he is born.

children.text: jīvitaṃ dharmakāmau ca dhane yasmāt pratiṣṭhitau
children.translated_text: Since life, <s>dharma</s>, and desire are founded upon wealth,
therefore one should by every effort avoid injury to another's wealth.
But one who is intent on injuring living beings, and likewise one who is intent on injuring wealth,
among the two, the one intent on injuring wealth obtains great suffering.

children.text: athāgamyāgamane mahāvratavidhānenābdaṃ cīravāsā vane prājāpatyaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the case of intercourse with a forbidden woman, he should live in the forest wearing bark garments and perform the <s>prājāpatya</s> penance for a year according to the rule of the <s>mahāvrata</s>.
The same applies in the case of intercourse with another man's wife.
For intercourse with a cow, the <s>govrata</s> (cow vow) is prescribed.

children.text: puṃsy ayonāv ākāśe 'psu divā goyāne ca savāsāḥ snānam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: For intercourse with a male, in a non-vaginal place, in the open air, in water, by day, or in a cow-cart, he should bathe with his clothes on.
By intercourse with a <s>caṇḍālī</s>, he becomes equal to her.
If it was done unknowingly, he should perform two <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> penances.
For intercourse with an animal or a prostitute, the penance is <s>prājāpatya</s>.

children.text: sakṛd duṣṭā ca strī yat puruṣasya paradāre tadvrataṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: And a woman once defiled should perform the same vow that is prescribed for a man in the case of another man's wife.
Whatever sin a twice-born man commits in one night through intercourse with a <s>vṛṣalī</s>,

children.text: tad bhaikṣyabhug japan nityaṃ tribhir varṣair vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: he removes in three years by eating alms and constantly reciting sacred formulas.

children.text: yaḥ pāpātmā yena saha saṃyujyate sa tasyaiva prāyaścittaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Whatever sinner one joins with, one should perform that person's very penance.

children.text: mṛtapañcanakhāt kūpād atyantopahatāccodakaṃ pītvā brāhmaṇas trirātram upavaset ||
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who drinks water from a well containing a dead five-nailed animal or one utterly polluted should fast for three nights.
A <s>rājanya</s> should fast for two days.
A <s>vaiśya</s> should fast for one day.
A <s>śūdra</s> should eat only at night.
And all of them, at the end of the vow, should drink <s>pañcagavya</s>.

children.text: pañcagavyaṃ pibecchūdro brāhmaṇas tu surāṃ pibet
children.translated_text: If a <s>śūdra</s> drinks <s>pañcagavya</s>, while a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> drinks liquor,
both go to the hell called <s>Mahāraurava</s>.

children.text: parvānārogyavarjam ṛtāv avagacchan patnīṃ trirātram upavaset ||
children.translated_text: Except on lunar days and in illness, if he approaches his wife in her season, he should fast for three nights.
A false witness should observe the vow for killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
If one urinates or defecates without water, one should bathe with one's clothes on and offer an oblation with the great utterances.
One who is released after sunrise should bathe with his clothes on and recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> eight hundred times.

children.text: śvasṛgālaviḍvarāhakharavānaravāyasapuṃścalībhir daṣṭaḥ sravantīm āsādya ṣoḍaśa prāṇāyāmān kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If one has been bitten by a dog, jackal, village pig, donkey, monkey, crow, or promiscuous woman, he should go to flowing water and perform sixteen <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls).
One who has ruined the Veda and the sacred fires should bathe at the three daily savanas, sleep on the ground, and live for a year on alms taken once a day.

children.text: samutkarṣānṛte guroścālīkanirbandhe tadākṣepaṇe ca māsaṃ payasā varteta ||
children.translated_text: For a false claim of superiority, for obstinate falsehood toward one's teacher, and for reviling him, one should live on milk for a month.

children.text: nāstiko nāstikavṛttiḥ kṛtaghnaḥ kūṭavyavahārī brāhmaṇavṛttighnaścaite saṃvatsaraṃ bhaikṣyeṇa varteran ||
children.translated_text: An unbeliever, one who lives by unbelieving conduct, an ingrate, a fraudulent dealer, and one who destroys a brāhmaṇa's livelihood should live on alms for a year.

children.text: parivittiḥ parivettā ca yayā ca parividyate dātā yājakaśca cāndrāyaṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The passed-over elder brother, the younger brother who marries before him, the woman through whom he is passed over, the giver of the bride, and the officiating priest should perform a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).
A seller of living beings, land, merit, or soma should perform the <s>taptakṛcchra</s> (heated difficult penance).

A seller of fresh herbs, perfumes, flowers, fruits, roots, hides, canes, split bamboo, husks, potsherds, hair, ashes, bones, cow-products, oil-cake, or sesame oil should perform the <s>prājāpatya</s> penance.
A seller of resin, lac, honey, beeswax, conch, shell, tin, lead, black iron, fig-wood articles, swords, or vessels should perform a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
A seller of red cloth, dye, jewels, perfumes, molasses, sweet juice, or wool should fast for three nights.
A seller of meat, salt, lac, or milk should perform a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
And one should initiate him again.

children.text: uṣṭreṇa khareṇa vā gatvā nagnaḥ snātvā suptvā bhuktvā prāṇāyāmatrayam kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: After going by camel or donkey, or after bathing, sleeping, or eating naked, one should perform three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.
Having recited three thousand repetitions of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, composed in mind,
and having drunk milk in a cow-pen for a month, one is released from accepting an improper gift.
Having officiated at a sacrifice for one for whom one should not officiate, and having performed another's final rite,

children.text: abhicāram ahīnaṃ ca tribhiḥ kṛcchrair vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: and also a complete act of hostile magic, one removes it by three <s>kṛcchras</s> (difficult penances).
Those twice-born men whose <s>Sāvitrī</s> has not been taught according to rule,
one should make them perform three <s>kṛcchras</s> and then initiate them according to rule.

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ cikīrṣanti vikarmasthās tu ye dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Those twice-born men who, though established in forbidden action, wish to undertake expiation,
and who have been excluded from brāhmaṇa status: this same prescription should be laid down also for them.
Whatever wealth brāhmaṇas acquire by a censured action,
they are purified by giving it up, and likewise by recitation and austerity.
When the obligatory rites taught in the Veda are neglected,
and when the vow of a <s>snātaka</s> is broken, the expiation is abstaining from food.
After threatening a brāhmaṇa one should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s>; after striking him down, an <s>atikṛcchra</s>;
and if one causes a brāhmaṇa's blood to flow, one should perform a <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s>.
One should have no dealings at all with sinners who have not been cleansed.
But a knower of <s>dharma</s> should not despise those who have completed this cleansing.
Even when they have been purified according to <s>dharma</s>, one should not live together with killers of children, ingrates,
killers of those who sought refuge, or killers of women.

children.text: aśītir yasya varṣāṇi bālo vāpy ūnaṣoḍaśaḥ
children.translated_text: A person who is eighty years old, or a child under sixteen,

children.text: prāyaścittārdham arhanti striyo rogiṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: as well as women and the sick, are entitled to half the expiation.
For the removal of sins for which no expiation has been stated,

children.text: śaktiṃ cāvekṣya pāpaṃ ca prāyaścittaṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: one should prescribe an expiation after considering both the person's capacity and the sin.
Now there are the secret expiations.

children.text: sravantīm āsādya snātaḥ pratyahaṃ ṣoḍaśa prāṇāyāmān salakṣaṇān kṛtvaikakālaṃ haviṣyāśī māsena brahmahā pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to flowing water and bathed, performing daily sixteen properly characterized <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>, and eating sacrificial food once a day, a killer of a brāhmaṇa becomes purified in a month.
At the end of the rite he should give a milk-giving cow.
A drinker of liquor becomes purified by the vow and by the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> hymn.
One who has stolen gold is purified by ten thousand recitations of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
One who has violated his teacher's bed is purified, after fasting for three nights, by recitation and oblation of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>.
Just as the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, king of sacrifices, removes all sins,
so the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> hymn removes all sins.
A twice-born man should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> for the removal of all sins;
for all the sins of a twice-born man are burned away by <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.
When, with breath extended, he recites three times the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, together with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, the <s>praṇava</s>, and the head-formula,

children.text: triḥ paṭhed āyataprāṇaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: akāraṃ cāpyukāraṃ ca makāraṃ ca prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> milked forth the syllable a, the syllable u, and the syllable m

children.text: vedatrayānniraduhad bhūr bhuvaḥ svar itīti ca ||
children.translated_text: from the three Vedas, and likewise the utterances <s>bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>svar</s>.

children.text: tribhya eva tu vedebhyaḥ pādaṃ pādam adūduhat
children.translated_text: From the three Vedas alone <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>

children.text: tad ity ṛco 'syāḥ sāvitryāḥ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: milked one foot from each, forming this <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse.

children.text: etad akṣaram etāṃ ca japan vyāhṛtipūrvikām
children.translated_text: A Veda-knowing brāhmaṇa who recites this syllable and this verse, prefaced by the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>,
at the two twilights is joined with the merit of the Veda.

children.text: sahasrakṛtvas tvabhyasya bahir etat trikaṃ dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: A twice-born man who repeats this triad a thousand times outside the settlement
is freed within a month from even a great sin, like a snake from its skin.
A man of the brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, or vaiśya class who is separated from this triad
and from his own rite at the proper time incurs blame among good people.
The three imperishable great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, preceded by <s>oṃ</s>,

children.text: tripadā caiva gāyatrī vijñeyā brāhmaṇo mukham ||
children.translated_text: and the three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> should be known as the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>.
Whoever studies this day after day for three years, untiring,

children.text: sa brahma param abhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān ||
children.translated_text: approaches the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, becoming wind-like and having space as his form.

children.text: ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmāḥ paraṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: The single syllable is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> are the supreme austerity.

children.text: sāvitryās tu paraṃ nānyan maunāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing higher than the <s>Sāvitrī</s>; truth is superior to silence.
All Vedic acts, the rites expressed by 'he offers' and 'he sacrifices,' pass away;

children.text: akṣaraṃ tvakṣaraṃ jñeyaṃ brahmā caiva prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the syllable should be known as imperishable, and as <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> himself.
The sacrifice of recitation is superior to the sacrifice prescribed by rule by ten times;
recitation in a low voice is said to be a hundred times superior, and mental recitation a thousand times.
Those four cooked sacrifices, even when accompanied by the prescribed sacrifices,

children.text: te sarve japayajñasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: all of them are not worth a sixteenth part of the sacrifice of recitation.

children.text: japyenaiva tu saṃsidhyed brāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is perfected by recitation alone; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: kuryād anyanna vā kuryān maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Whether he performs anything else or does not perform it, he is called a friendly <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
Now, therefore, there are purifications belonging to all the Vedas.

children.text: yeṣāṃ japyaiśca homaiśca dvijātayaḥ pāpebhyaḥ pūyante ||
children.translated_text: By reciting and offering oblations with them, twice-born men are purified from sins.
The <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>.
The <s>Devakṛta</s>.
The <s>Śuddhavatī</s> verses.
The <s>Taratsamandīya</s>.
The <s>Kūśmāṇḍī</s> verses.
The <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses.
The <s>Durgā-Sāvitrī</s>.
The <s>Atīṣaṅga</s> verses.
The <s>Padastoma</s> chants.
The <s>Sāmans</s> and the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>.
The <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s> verses.
The <s>Candrasāman</s>.
The two <s>Sāmans</s> in the <s>Puruṣavrata</s>.
The <s>Abliṅga</s> hymn.
The <s>Bārhaspatya</s>.
The hymn to cows.
The hymn to horses.
And the two <s>Sāmans</s> in the lunar hymns.
The <s>Śatarudriya</s>.
The <s>Atharvaśiras</s>.
The <s>Trisuparṇa</s>.
The <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
The <s>Nārāyaṇīya</s>.
And the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>.

children.text: trīṇyājyadohāni rathaṃtaraṃ ca agnivrataṃ vāmadevyaṃ bṛhacca
children.translated_text: The three <s>Ājyadoha</s> chants, the <s>Rathaṃtara</s>, the <s>Agnivrata</s>, the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, and the <s>Bṛhat</s>:

children.text: etāni gītāni punanti jantūn jātismaratvaṃ labhate yadīcchet ||
children.translated_text: when these are sung, they purify beings; if one so desires, one obtains memory of former births.
Now, those to be avoided:
<s>Vrātyas</s>.
Fallen persons.
Those impure for three generations on the mother's and father's side.
All these are people whose food must not be eaten and from whom gifts must not be accepted.
And one should avoid the occasion of accepting gifts from those from whom gifts must not be accepted.
Through accepting gifts, the brahmanic splendor of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> perishes.

children.text: dravyāṇāṃ vāvijñāya pratigrahavidhiṃ yaḥ pratigrahaṃ kuryāt sa dātrā saha nimajjati ||
children.translated_text: One who accepts a gift without knowing the rule for accepting different objects sinks down together with the giver.

children.text: pratigrahasamarthaśca yaḥ pratigrahaṃ varjayet sa dātṛlokam avāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: But one who is capable of receiving a gift and yet avoids receiving it obtains the world of the giver.
One should not refuse, when they are offered unasked, fuel, water, roots, fruits, protection, meat, honey, a bed, a seat, a house, flowers, curds, and vegetables.
<s>Prajāpati</s> considered alms to be acceptable when they have been called for and offered,
placed before one without prior solicitation, even from a man of bad deeds.

children.text: nāśnanti pitaras tasya daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca
children.translated_text: The ancestors of one who disdains such alms do not eat for fifteen years,

children.text: na ca havyaṃ vahatyagnir yas tām abhyavamanyate ||
children.translated_text: and the fire does not carry his oblation.
When wishing to support elders and servants and to honor the ancestors and gods,

children.text: sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān na tu tṛpyet svayaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one may accept gifts from everywhere, but one should not satisfy oneself from them.

children.text: eteṣv api ca kāryeṣu samarthas tatpratigrahe
children.translated_text: Even in these matters, if one is capable of receiving those gifts,
one should not take from an adulteress, a heretic, a fallen man, or an enemy.

children.text: guruṣu tvabhyatīteṣu vinā vā tair gṛhe vasan
children.translated_text: But when the elders have passed away, or when living at home without them,

children.text: ātmano vṛttim anvicchan gṛhṇīyāt sādhutaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: one who seeks his own livelihood should always accept from a good man.
A sharecropper, a family friend, slaves, a cowherd, and a barber:
among <s>śūdras</s>, these are persons whose food may be eaten, as is one who offers himself in service.
Now the wealth of a householder is of three kinds.
It is white, mixed, and black.

children.text: śuklenārthena yad aurdhvadehikaṃ karoti tenāsya devatvam āsādayati ||
children.translated_text: Whatever rite for the next world he performs with white wealth, by that it causes him to attain the state of a god.
Whatever he performs with mixed wealth, that leads to human birth.
Whatever he performs with black wealth, that leads to animal birth.
For all, wealth acquired by one's own occupation is white.
What is obtained by a closely related occupation is mixed.
And what is obtained by an entirely different occupation is black.

children.text: kramāgataṃ prītidāyaṃ prāptaṃ ca saha bhāryayā
children.translated_text: Inherited wealth, a gift given with affection, and what is obtained together with one's wife,
are declared, without distinction, to be white wealth for all.
What is obtained through bribes and fees, through selling what should not be sold,
and what is received from a favor done is declared to be mixed.
What is obtained by cheating, gambling, theft, counterfeit dealings, and violence,
and whatever is acquired by deceit, that is declared to be black.

children.text: yathāvidhena dravyeṇa yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever a man does with wealth of a given kind, according to its rule,

children.text: tathāvidham avāpnoti sa phalaṃ pretya ceha ca ||
children.translated_text: he obtains fruit of that same kind both after death and here in this world.
A householder should perform the cooked sacrifices in the nuptial fire.
He should perform the <s>agnihotra</s> in the evening and in the morning.
He should offer oblations to the deities.
At the conjunction and opposition of the moon and sun he should sacrifice with the new-moon and full-moon rites.
At each half-yearly turn, he should sacrifice with an animal.
And in autumn and summer, with the first-fruits offering.
Or when rice and barley ripen.
He should have grain enough for more than three years.
Every year he should sacrifice with soma.
When wealth is lacking, with a <s>Vaiśvānara</s> oblation.
He should avoid food from a <s>śūdra</s> in sacrifice.

children.text: yajñārthaṃ bhikṣitam avāptam arthaṃ sakalam eva vitaret ||
children.translated_text: He should distribute completely all the wealth obtained by begging for the sake of sacrifice.
Evening and morning he should offer the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
And he should give alms to a mendicant.
By giving honored alms he obtains the fruit of gifting a cow.
If there is no mendicant, he should give a mouthful to the cows.
Or he should throw it into the fire.
Even after he has eaten, if food is available, he should not turn away a beggar.

children.text: kaṇḍanī peṣaṇī cullī udakumbha upaskara iti pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya ||
children.translated_text: The pounding stone, the grinding stone, the hearth, the water jar, and the broom: these are the five slaughter-places of a householder.
For expiation of them he should perform the sacrifices to <s>Brahman</s>, the gods, beings, the ancestors, and men.
Vedic study is the sacrifice to <s>Brahman</s>.
The oblation is the divine sacrifice.
Offering water to the ancestors is the ancestral sacrifice.
The food offering is the sacrifice to beings.
And the sacrifice to men is the honoring of a guest.
For the deities, the guest, the servants, the ancestors, and oneself,

children.text: na nirvapati pañcānām ucchvasan na sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: one who does not set aside portions for these five does not truly live, even while breathing.
The student, the ascetic, and the mendicant live from the household stage.
Therefore a householder should not treat these arrivals with contempt.

children.text: gṛhastha eva yajate gṛhasthas tapyate tapaḥ
children.translated_text: The householder alone sacrifices; the householder practices austerity.
and the householder gives; therefore the householder's <s>āśrama</s> is the best.
Sages, ancestors, gods, beings, and guests as well
look expectantly to householders; therefore the householder's <s>āśrama</s> is the best.
By constantly pursuing the three aims, giving food, worshiping the gods, honoring brāhmaṇas,

children.text: svādhyāyasevāṃ pitṛtarpaṇaṃ ca kṛtvā gṛhī śakrapadaṃ prayāti ||
children.translated_text: attending to recitation, and offering satisfaction to the ancestors, the householder goes to the rank of <s>Śakra</s>.
Having risen in the <s>brāhma</s> muhūrta, one should void urine and feces.
At night one should face south, and by day and at the twilights one should face north.
Not on uncovered ground.
Not on land ploughed by a ploughshare.
Not in shade.
And not on saline soil.
Not on grassy ground.
Not where there are living beings.
Not in a pit.
Not on an anthill.
Not on a path.
Not in a street.
Not in another unclean place.
Not in a garden.
Not in a garden or near water.
Not on ashes.
Not on coals.
Not on cow dung.
Not in a cattle enclosure.
Not in the open.
Not in water.
Not facing wind, fire, the moon, the sun, a woman, a teacher, or brāhmaṇas.
Nor with one's head uncovered.

children.text: loṣṭeṣṭakāparimṛṣṭagudo gṛhītaśiśnaś cotthāyādbhir mṛdbhiścoddhṛtābhir gandhalepakṣayakaraṃ śaucaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: After rising, with the anus wiped by clods and bricks and holding the penis, one should perform cleansing with water and with lifted earth, so as to remove smell and smear.

children.text: ekā liṅge gude tisras tathaikatra kare daśa
children.translated_text: One portion of earth should be applied to the organ, three to the anus, and ten likewise to one hand;

children.text: ubhayoḥ sapta dātavyā mṛdas tisras tu pādayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: seven should be applied to both hands, and three portions of earth to the feet.
This is the cleansing for householders; for brahmacārins it is doubled,

children.text: triguṇaṃ tu vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: for forest-dwellers it is tripled, and for ascetics it is quadrupled.
Next, one should not use a palāśa tooth-cleaning stick.
Nor one made from śleṣmātaka, ariṣṭa, vibhītaka, dhava, or dhanvana.
Nor one made from bandhūka, nirguṇḍī, śigru, tilvaka, or tinduka.
Nor one made from kovidāra, śamī, pīlu, pippala, iṅguda, or guggulu.
Nor one made from pāribhadraka, āmlikā, mocaka, śālmalī, or śaṇa.
Not one that is sweet.
Not one that is sour.
Not one that is dry at the top.
Not one that is hollow.
Not one that has a foul smell.
Not one that is slimy.
He should not face south or west.
He should use it facing north or east.
He should use any one of vaṭa, asana, arka, khadira, karañja, badara, sarja, nimba, āri, medā, apāmārga, mālatī, kakubha, or bilva.
It should be astringent, bitter, or pungent.
It should be as thick as the tip of the little finger, furnished with its brush, and twelve finger-breadths long.
In the morning, purified and restraining speech, he should chew the tooth-cleaning stick.
Having washed it and broken it, he should carefully discard it in a clean place.
On the new-moon day he should never eat a tooth-stick.

children.text: atha dvijātīnāṃ kanīnikāmūle prājāpatyaṃ nāma tīrtham ||
children.translated_text: Next, for the twice-born, at the root of the little finger is the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Prājāpatya</s>.
At the root of the thumb is the <s>Brāhma</s>.
At the tips of the fingers is the <s>Daiva</s>.
At the root of the forefinger is the <s>Pitrya</s>.

children.text: anagnyuṣṇābhir aphenilābhiḥ aśūdraikakarāvarjitābhir akṣārābhir adbhiḥ śucau deśe svāsīno 'ntarjānu prāṅmukhaścodaṅmukho vā tanmanāḥ sumanāścācāmet ||
children.translated_text: With waters not heated by fire, not foamy, not supplied by a śūdra or with one hand, and not alkaline, seated properly in a clean place, with the knees drawn in, facing east or north, attentive and well-disposed, he should sip water.
He should sip three times with the <s>Brāhma</s> <s>tīrtha</s>.
He should wipe twice.
With water he should touch the apertures, the head, and the heart.
Twice-born persons are purified, respectively, by water reaching the heart, throat, and palate;

children.text: śudhyeran strī ca śūdraśca sakṛt spṛṣṭābhir antataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a woman and a śūdra are purified at the end by water touched once.
Next, for the sake of security and welfare, one should approach the ruler.
One should not take to the road alone.
Not together with unrighteous people.
Not with base men.
Not with enemies.
Not too early in the morning.
Not too late in the evening.
Not at the twilights.
Not at midday.
Not where drinking water is close at hand.
Not too hastily.
Not continually with mounts or vehicles that are young, sick, or distressed.
Not with those whose limbs are deficient.
Not with wretched ones.
Not with cows.
Not with untamed ones.

children.text: yavasodake vāhanānām adattvā ātmanaḥ kṣuttṛṣṇāpanodanaṃ na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Without first giving barley and water to the mounts, he should not relieve his own hunger and thirst.
He should not stand at a crossroads.
Not at the root of a tree at night.
Not in an empty house.
Not on grass.
Not in an enclosure where animals are tied.
Not on hair, chaff, skulls, bones, ashes, or coals.
Not on cotton seed.
He should circumambulate a crossroads clockwise.
And likewise an image of a deity.
And trees that are recognized as sacred.
Having seen fire, a brāhmaṇa, a courtesan, a full water-pot, a mirror, a parasol, a banner, a flag, a śrīvṛkṣa, vardhamāna, and nandyāvarta,
and a palm-leaf fan, a fly-whisk, a horse, an elephant, a goat, a cow, curds, milk, honey, and white mustard,
and a vīṇā, sandalwood, a weapon, fresh cow dung, fruit, flowers, fresh greens, gorocanā, and sprouts of dūrvā grass,
and a turban, ornaments, jewels, gold, silver, garments, seats, vehicles, and meat,
and a water vessel, raised fertile earth, a single tethered animal, a maiden, and fish, he should proceed.
Next, having seen the drunk, the mad, and the deformed, he should turn back.
And those who have vomited or been purged, the shaven-headed, the matted-haired, and dwarfs.
And saffron-clad wanderers and dirty people.
And oil, molasses, dry cow dung, fuel, grass, leaves, ashes, and coals.
And salt, a eunuch, liquor, an impotent man, cotton, rope, fetters, and people with loose hair.
But at the time of departure he should greet a vīṇā, sandalwood, fresh greens, a turban, ornaments, and maidens.
He should not step on the shadows of gods, brāhmaṇas, teachers, tawny cows, or consecrated persons.
Nor on spit, vomit, blood, feces, urine, or bathing water.
He should not step over a calf's tether.
He should not run when it is raining.
He should not cross a river needlessly.
He should not do so without first giving water to the deities and the ancestors.
He should not do so by means of his arms.
He should not do so in a broken boat.
He should not stand on the bank.
He should not look down into a well.
He should not leap over it.
For the aged, burden-bearers, kings, bath-graduates, women, the sick, bridegrooms, and those in vehicles,

children.text: panthā deyā nṛpas tveṣāṃ mānyaḥ snātaśca bhūpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: a path should be given; but the king is to be honored by these, and the bath-graduate by the king.
He should not bathe in others' watering places.
In an emergency he may do so, after taking out five clods and some water.
He should not bathe when food is undigested.
Nor when he is ill.
Nor naked.
Nor at night.
Except at the sight of <s>Rāhu</s>.
Nor at the two twilights.
One whose habit is morning bathing should bathe after looking toward the east, red and copper-colored with dawn.
After bathing, he should not shake his head.
He should not shake water from his limbs.
He should not touch himself as one smeared with oil.
He should not wear a garment previously worn if it has not been washed.

children.text: snāta eva soṣṇīṣe dhaute vāsasī bibhṛyāt ||
children.translated_text: Only after bathing should he wear washed garments, along with a head-cloth.
He should not converse with <s>mlecchas</s>, outcastes, or fallen persons.
He should bathe in springs, temple tanks, excavated tanks, and lakes.

children.text: uddhṛtāt bhūmiṣṭham udakaṃ puṇyaṃ sthāvarāt prasravat tasmān nādeyaṃ tasmād api sādhuparigṛhītaṃ sarvata eva gāṅgam ||
children.translated_text: Water standing on the ground is more sacred than water drawn up; flowing water is more sacred than standing water; river water is more sacred than that; water used by good people is more sacred even than that; and <s>Gaṅgā</s> water is sacred in every case.

children.text: mṛttoyaiḥ kṛtamalāpakarṣo 'psu nimajjyopaviśyāpo hi ṣṭheti tisṛbhir hiraṇyavarṇeti catasṛbhir idam āpaḥ pravahateti ca tīrtham abhimantrayet ||
children.translated_text: Having removed dirt with earth and water, he should immerse himself in the waters, sit down, and consecrate the bathing place with the three verses beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā," the four beginning "hiraṇyavarṇāḥ," and also "idam āpaḥ pravahata."
Then, submerged in the waters, he should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times.
Or the verse beginning "tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam."
And the <s>Drupadā</s> and the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
Or the section beginning "yuñjate manaḥ."
Or the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>.
After bathing, while still in wet clothing, he should perform the water-offering to the gods and ancestors while remaining in the water.
But if he has changed his clothing, he should do so after coming up from the bathing place.
Without making the water-offering to the gods and ancestors, he should not wring out his bathing cloth.
After bathing and sipping water, he should ritually rinse himself according to rule.
With each verse of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, he should offer flowers to the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
And handfuls of water.

children.text: ādāv eva daivena tīrthena devānāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: At the very beginning, using the divine <s>tīrtha</s>, he should make the water-offering to the gods.
Immediately after that, using the ancestral <s>tīrtha</s>, to the ancestors.
There he should first make the water-offering for those of his own lineage.
Then for relatives and kinsmen.
Then for friends.
Thus he should be one who bathes daily.
And after bathing, he should recite purifying texts according to his ability.
Especially the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
And the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>.
There is nothing higher than these two.

children.text: snāto 'dhikārī bhavati daive pitrye ca karmaṇi
children.translated_text: One who has bathed becomes qualified for rites concerning the gods and the ancestors,

children.text: pavitrāṇāṃ tathā japye dāne ca vidhibodhite ||
children.translated_text: as well as for recitation of purifying texts and for giving gifts prescribed by rule.
Misfortune, ill omen, bad dreams, and evil thoughts
are believed to perish for one who has been sprinkled with even a mere measure of water.

children.text: yāmyaṃ hi yātanāduḥkhaṃ nityasnāyī na paśyati
children.translated_text: One who bathes daily does not see the torment and suffering belonging to <s>Yama</s>.
By daily bathing even men who have done evil are purified.

children.text: athātaḥ susnātaḥ suprakṣālitapāṇipādaḥ svācānto devatārcāyāṃ sthale vā bhagavantam anādinidhanaṃ vāsudevam abhyarcayet ||
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, well bathed, with hands and feet well washed, and having properly sipped water, he should worship the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, without beginning or end, at a place for deity worship or on a clean spot.

children.text: aśvinoḥ prāṇas tau ta iti jīvādānaṃ dattvā yuñjate mana ityanuvākenāvāhanaṃ kṛtvā jānubhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ śirasā ca namaskāraṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: After giving life-bestowal with the formula beginning "aśvinoḥ prāṇas tau te," and making the invocation with the section beginning "yuñjate manaḥ," he should make obeisance with his knees, hands, and head.

children.text: āpo hi ṣṭheti tisṛbhir arghyaṃ nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: With the three verses beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā," he should present the arghya offering.
With the four beginning "hiraṇyavarṇāḥ," the water for washing the feet.
With "śaṃ na āpo dhanvanyāḥ," the water for sipping.
With "idam āpaḥ pravahata," the bathing water.
With "rathe akṣeṣu vṛṣabhasya vāje," the unguent and ornaments.
With "yuvā suvāsāḥ," the garment.
With "puṣpāvatīḥ," the flowers.
With "dhūr asi dhūrva," the incense.
With "tejo 'si śukram," the lamp.
With "dadhikrāvṇaḥ," the honey-mixture.
With the eight verses beginning "hiraṇyagarbhaḥ," the food offering.

children.text: cāmaraṃ vyajanaṃ mātrāṃ chatraṃ yānāsane tathā
children.translated_text: The fly-whisk, fan, measure, umbrella, vehicle, and seat,
he should present all of that to the deity with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> alone.

children.text: evam abhyarcya tu japet sūktaṃ vai pauruṣaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having worshipped in this way, he should then recite the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> hymn.
With that very hymn he should offer ghee if he desires the eternal abode.
He should not perform rites for the gods and ancestors with water drawn at night.
He should not give an unguent except sandalwood, musk, aloe-wood, camphor, saffron, or nutmeg.
Nor a garment dyed blue or red.
Nor a counterfeit ornament of jewels or gold.
Nor anything with a harsh smell.
Nor anything without fragrance.
Nor anything produced from a thorny plant.

children.text: kaṇṭakijam api śuklaṃ sugandhikaṃ tu dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: But even what is produced from a thorny plant may be given if it is white and fragrant.

children.text: raktam api kuṅkumaṃ jalajaṃ ca dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Even a red thing may be given if it is saffron or aquatic.
For incense, he should not use anything produced from living beings.
For a lamp, he should not use anything except ghee or oil.
For the food offering, he should not offer what is unfit to eat.
Nor, even among edible things, the milk of a goat or a she-buffalo.
Nor the flesh of five-clawed animals, fish, or boar.

children.text: prayataśca śucir bhūtvā sarvam eva nivedayet
children.translated_text: Having become restrained and pure, he should offer everything
with his mind fixed on that, being well-disposed and free from haste and anger.

children.text: athāgniṃ parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya pariṣicya sarvataḥ pākād agram uddhṛtya juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, having swept around the fire, sprinkled around it, spread grass around it, and poured water around it, he should take the first portion from every cooked dish and offer it.

children.text: vāsudevāya saṃkarṣaṇāya pradyumnāyāniruddhāya puruṣāya satyāyācyutāya vāsudevāya ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, to <s>Pradyumna</s>, to <s>Aniruddha</s>, to the <s>Puruṣa</s>, to <s>Satya</s>, to <s>Acyuta</s>, and to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: athāgnaye somāya mitrāya varuṇāya indrāya indrāgnibhyāṃ viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ prajāpataye anumatyai dhanvantaraye vāstoṣpataye agnaye sviṣṭakṛte ca ||
children.translated_text: Then to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Mitra</s>, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to all the gods, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Anumati</s>, to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
After that, with the remainder of the food he should present a <s>bali</s> (offering).
With edible food and subsidiary eatables.
All around, to the east of the fire.

children.text: ambā nāmāsīti dulā nāmāsīti nitatnī nāmāsīti cupuṇīkā nāmāsīti sarvāsām ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "You are named <s>Ambā</s>, you are named <s>Dulā</s>, you are named <s>Nitatnī</s>, you are named <s>Cupuṇīkā</s>," for all of them.

children.text: nandini subhage sumaṅgali bhadraṃkarīti svaśriṣv abhipradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "O <s>Nandinī</s>, fortunate one, auspicious one, bringer of welfare," he should go clockwise around among his own women.
To the fixed post, to <s>Dhruvā</s>, to <s>Śrī</s>, to golden-haired <s>Śrī</s>, and to the forest trees.
At the door, to <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Adharma</s>, and to <s>Mṛtyu</s>.
At the water vessel, to <s>Varuṇa</s>.
In the mortar, saying "to <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
On the grinding stone, saying "to the <s>Maruts</s>."
Above, in the shelter, to king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and to the beings.
In the eastern half, saying "to <s>Indra</s> and to the men of <s>Indra</s>."
In the southern half, saying "to <s>Yama</s> and to the men of <s>Yama</s>."
In the western half, saying "to <s>Varuṇa</s> and to the men of <s>Varuṇa</s>."
In the northern half, saying "to <s>Soma</s> and to the men of <s>Soma</s>."
In the middle, saying "to <s>Brahman</s> and to the men of <s>Brahman</s>."
Upwards, to the sky.
By day, on the altar-ground, saying "to the beings who move by day."
At night, saying "to those who move by night."

children.text: tato dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu pitre pitāmahāya prapitāmahāya mātre pitāmahyai prapitāmahyai nāmagotrābhyāṃ ca piṇḍanirvāpaṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, on darbha grass whose tips point south, he should make an offering of <s>piṇḍas</s> to his father, grandfather, great-grandfather, mother, paternal grandmother, and paternal great-grandmother, with their names and lineages.
He should give anointing, flowers, incense, food offerings, and the like for the <s>piṇḍas</s>.
Having placed a water jar nearby, he should have auspicious benedictions recited.
He should make an offering on the ground for dogs, crows, and <s>śvapacas</s>.
And he should give alms.
And he should apply the utmost effort to honoring a guest.
He should carefully honor a guest who has arrived in the evening.
He should not let a guest stay in his house unfed.

children.text: yathā varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prabhur yathā strīṇāṃ bhartā tathā gṛhasthasyātithiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is lord among the social classes, and as a husband is lord among women, so the guest is lord for a householder.
By honoring him, he obtains heaven.
A guest who turns back from one's house with his hope broken

children.text: tasmāt sukṛtam ādāya duṣkṛtaṃ tu prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: takes away that man's merit and gives him his own demerit.

children.text: ekarātraṃ hi nivasann atithir brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who stays for one night is remembered as a guest;

children.text: anityaṃ hi sthito yasmāt tasmād atithir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: because his stay is not fixed, therefore he is called <s>atithi</s> (guest).
One should not consider as a guest a <s>vipra</s> from the same village, nor one who is merely a companion,

children.text: upasthitaṃ gṛhe vindyād bhāryā yatrāgnayo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: when he has appeared at a house where there is a wife and also the sacred fires.

children.text: yadi tv atithidharmeṇa kṣatriyo gṛham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: But if a <s>kṣatriya</s> has come to the house under the rule of guesthood,

children.text: bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu kāmaṃ tam api bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: then, when the <s>vipras</s> have eaten, he may also feed him as he wishes.
If a <s>vaiśya</s> and a <s>śūdra</s> have arrived at the household in the manner of guests,

children.text: bhojayet saha bhṛtyais tāv ānṛśaṃsyaṃ prayojayan ||
children.translated_text: he should feed them together with the servants, acting with compassion.

children.text: itarān api sakhyādīn saṃprītyā gṛham āgatān
children.translated_text: Other people too, such as friends, who have come to the house out of affection,
he should feed, along with his wife, with the regular food according to his ability.

children.text: svavāsinīṃ kumārīṃ ca rogiṇīṃ gurviṇīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A woman living in his house, a maiden, a sick woman, and a pregnant woman:
he should feed these before the guests, without deliberating.

children.text: adattvā yas tu etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṅkte 'vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But the unwise man who eats before giving food to these persons

children.text: bhuñjāno na sa jānāti śvagṛdhrair jagdhim ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: does not know, while eating, that he himself is being eaten by dogs and vultures.

children.text: bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu sveṣu bhṛtyeṣu caiva hi
children.translated_text: When the <s>vipras</s>, his own people, and his servants have eaten,

children.text: bhuñjīyātāṃ tataḥ paścād avaśiṣṭaṃ tu daṃpatī ||
children.translated_text: then afterwards the husband and wife should eat what remains.

children.text: devān pitṝn manuṣyāṃśca bhṛtyān gṛhyāśca devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the gods, the ancestors, human beings, the servants, and the domestic deities,

children.text: pūjayitvā tataḥ paścād gṛhasthaḥ śeṣabhug bhavet ||
children.translated_text: only then should a householder become an eater of the remainder.

children.text: aghaṃ sa kevalaṃ bhuṅkte yaḥ pacatyātmakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: He eats only sin who cooks for his own sake;
for this food, the eating of what remains from sacrifice, is prescribed as the food of good people.
By Vedic recitation, by the <s>agnihotra</s>, by sacrifice, and likewise by austerity,

children.text: na cāpnoti gṛhī lokān yathā tv atithipūjanāt ||
children.translated_text: a householder does not obtain the worlds as he does by honoring a guest.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātas tv atithaye pradadyād āsanodake
children.translated_text: In the evening and in the morning he should give a guest a seat and water,
and also food according to his ability, after honoring him in the prescribed way.
Shelter likewise, a bed, and an oil massage for the feet, with a lamp:
by giving each one separately, he obtains a fruit equal to the gift of a cow.
He should not eat during an eclipse of the moon or sun.
When they have been released, he should bathe and then eat.

children.text: amuktayor astaṃ gatayoḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā cāpare 'hni ||
children.translated_text: If they have set without being released, he should bathe, see them on the following day, and then eat.
He should not eat during an affliction involving cows or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Nor during a calamity of the king.
An <s>agnihotrin</s> who is away from home should eat when he thinks the <s>agnihotra</s> has been performed.
And he may do so when he thinks the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> has been performed.

children.text: parvaṇi ca yadā kṛtaṃ manyeta parva ||
children.translated_text: And on a sacred lunar day, when he thinks the rite for that sacred day has been performed.
He should not eat when food from the previous meal is undigested.
Nor at midnight.
Nor at midday.
Nor at the two twilights.
Nor while wearing wet clothes.
Nor while wearing only one garment.
Nor naked.
Nor in water.
Nor while squatting on the heels.
Nor while seated on a broken seat.
Nor while lying down.
Nor from a broken dish.
Nor in his lap.
Nor on the ground.
Nor from his hand.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ ca yatra dadyāt tan nāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not eat food to which salt has been added there.
He should not scold children.
He should not eat rich food alone.
He should not eat food from which the fat has been removed.
He should not eat parched grain by day.
Nor anything connected with sesame at night.
Nor curds and barley meal.
Nor vegetables of the <s>kovidāra</s>, banyan, pippala, or hemp plants.
He should not eat without first giving.
Nor without first making an offering into the fire.
He should not have dry feet.
Nor should his hands and mouth be dry.
And while polluted by leftovers, he should not take ghee.
He should not gaze at the moon, the sun, or the stars.
He should not touch his head.
He should not recite <s>Brahman</s>, the sacred text.
He should eat facing east.
Or facing south.
After honoring the food.
With a cheerful mind, wearing a garland and anointed.
He should not consume everything without remainder.
Except in the case of curds, honey, ghee, milk, parched-flour drink, and cakes.

children.text: nāśnīyād bhāryayā sārdhaṃ nākāśe na tathotthitaḥ
children.translated_text: He should not eat together with his wife, nor in the open air, nor likewise while standing,
nor while many people are looking on; nor should many eat from a single vessel in that way.
In an empty house, a fire-house, or a temple, in any manner,
he should not drink water from his cupped hands, and he should not practice excessive satiety.

children.text: na tṛtīyam athāśnīta na cāpathyaṃ kathaṃcana
children.translated_text: He should not eat a third time, nor anything unwholesome in any case,

children.text: nātiprage nātisāyaṃ na sāyaṃ prātar āśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not too early, not too late, and not in the evening when he has eaten in the morning.

children.text: na bhāvaduṣṭam aśnīyān na bhāṇḍe bhāvadūṣite
children.translated_text: He should not eat food tainted in intention, nor from a vessel tainted in condition,
nor while lying down, with his feet stretched out, or after assuming the avasakthikā posture.
He should not approach a woman on the eighth, fourteenth, or fifteenth lunar days.
Not after eating a <s>śrāddha</s> meal.
Not after giving one.
Not when he has been invited to a <s>śrāddha</s>.
Not while he is observing a vow.
Not while he is consecrated.
Not in temples, cremation grounds, or empty houses.
Not at the roots of trees.
Not by day.
Not at the two twilights.
Not a woman who is unclean.
Not while he himself is unclean.
Not a woman who has been anointed.
Not while he himself has been anointed.
Not a woman afflicted by illness.
Not while he himself is afflicted by illness.

children.text: na hīnāṅgīṃ nādhikāṅgīṃ tathaiva ca vayo'dhikām
children.translated_text: He should not approach a woman with deficient limbs, with extra limbs, or likewise one older in age,

children.text: nopeyād gurviṇīṃ nārīṃ dīrgham āyur jijīviṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor a pregnant woman, if he wishes to live a long life.
He should not sleep with wet feet.
Nor with his head toward the north or west.
Not naked.
Not lengthwise along a beam.
Not in the open air.
Not on a bed of palāśa wood.
Not on one made of five kinds of wood.
Not on one made from wood broken by an elephant.
Not on one made from wood struck by lightning.
Not on a broken one.
Not behind a fire.
Not on one made from a tree watered from a pot.
Not in cremation grounds, empty houses, or temples.
Not in the midst of restless movement.
Not among women.
Not on top of grain, cows, a guru, the sacred fire, or the gods.

children.text: nocchiṣṭo na divā supyāt saṃdhyayor na ca bhasmani
children.translated_text: While polluted by leftovers he should not sleep, nor by day, nor at the two twilights, nor on ashes,

children.text: deśe na ca aśucau nārdre na ca parvatamastake ||
children.translated_text: nor in an unclean place, nor in a wet place, nor on the top of a mountain.
Next, he should not despise anyone at all.

children.text: na ca hīnādhikāṅgān mūrkhān dhanahīnān avahaset ||
children.translated_text: And he should not mock those with deficient or extra limbs, fools, or those without wealth.
He should not associate with inferior people.
He should not perform an action that conflicts with Vedic study.
He should wear clothing appropriate to his age,
and to his learning, family, wealth, and country.
He should not be arrogant.
He should always be attentive to scripture and the like.
When he has the means, he should not wear old or dirty garments.
He should not say, 'It does not exist.'

children.text: na nirgandhogragandhi raktaṃ ca mālyaṃ bibhṛyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not wear a garland that is odorless, strongly scented, or red.
But he may wear even a red one if it is water-born.
And a staff made of bamboo.
And a water-pot furnished with water.
A cotton sacred thread.
And gold earrings.
He should not look at the sun when it is rising.
Nor when it is setting.
Nor when it is hidden by cloth.
Nor when it stands in a mirror or in water.
Not at midday.
Nor at the face of an angry guru.
Nor at his own shadow in oil or water.
Nor in a dirty mirror.
Nor at his wife at mealtime.
Nor at a naked woman.
Nor at anyone urinating.
Nor at an elephant that has broken loose from its tether.
Nor, while standing in an uneven place, at a fight of bulls and the like.
Nor at a madman.
Nor at an intoxicated man.
He should not throw anything impure into the fire.
Nor blood.
Nor poison.
Nor even into water.
He should not step over fire.
He should not heat his feet at it.
He should not wipe them with kuśa grass.
He should not wash them in a bronze vessel.
He should not rub one foot with the other.
He should not scratch the ground.
He should not be one who crushes clods of earth.
He should not be one who cuts grass.
He should not cut nails or hairs with his teeth.
And he should avoid gambling.
And basking in the young sun.
He should not wear clothes, shoes, garlands, or sacred threads worn by another.
He should not give counsel to a <s>śūdra</s>.
Nor leftover sacrificial food.
Nor sesame seeds.
And he should not teach him <s>dharma</s>.
Nor a vow.

children.text: na saṃhatābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ śira udaraṃ ca kaṇḍūyet ||
children.translated_text: He should not scratch his head and belly with both hands joined together.
He should not refuse curds and flowers.
He should not pull off his own garland.
He should not wake someone who is asleep.
He should not make one who is attached become disaffected.
He should not speak to a menstruating woman.
Nor to <s>mlecchas</s> and outcastes.
In the presence of fire, a deity, or a Brahmin, he should raise his right hand.
He should not point out a cow grazing in another's field.
Nor a calf while it is drinking.
He should not encourage the arrogant.
He should not live in a kingdom ruled by a <s>śūdra</s>.
Nor in one crowded with unrighteous people.
He should not dwell where there is no physician.
Nor in a place that is afflicted.
He should not stay long on a mountain.
He should not perform useless activity.
Not dance or song.
Not clapping or striking sounds.
He should not utter anything obscene.
Nor what is untrue.
Nor what is unpleasant.
He should not touch anyone on a vulnerable spot.
He should not disparage himself, if he wishes to live a long life.
He should perform the twilight worship for a long time.
He should not play with snakes or weapons.
Without cause he should not touch the bodily openings.
He should not raise another person's staff.
He should beat one who is to be disciplined for the sake of discipline.
He should strike him on the back with a split bamboo or with a rope.
He should avoid reproach of the gods, Brahmins, scriptures, and great-souled persons.
He should avoid wealth and pleasure when they conflict with <s>dharma</s> (normative duty).
And he should avoid even a <s>dharma</s> that is hated by the world.
On festival days he should perform appeasing oblations.
He should not cut even a blade of grass.
He should remain adorned.
