Thus he should be one who follows proper conduct.
The righteous conduct taught by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, and practiced by good people,
that conduct should be followed by one who desires <s>dharma</s> and has mastered his senses.
From conduct he obtains long life; from conduct, the desired course.
From conduct he obtains imperishable wealth; from conduct he destroys inauspicious marks.
Even a man devoid of all auspicious marks, if he possesses good conduct,
and is faithful and free from envy, lives for a hundred years.
He should remain established in restraint and discipline.
Restraint is declared to be control of the senses.
This world and the next belong to the restrained man.
No act at all succeeds for one who is unrestrained.

children.text: damaḥ pavitraṃ paramaṃ maṅgalyaṃ paramaṃ damaḥ
children.translated_text: Restraint is the highest purifier; restraint is the highest auspicious thing.

children.text: damena sarvam āpnoti yat kiṃcin manasecchati ||
children.translated_text: Through restraint one obtains everything, whatever one desires in the mind.
When a man travels in a chariot yoked with the half of ten, governed by the mind and following the noble path,

children.text: taṃ ced rathaṃ nāpaharanti vājinas tathāgataṃ nāvajayanti śatravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the horses do not carry off that chariot, enemies do not defeat him who has gone in that way.

children.text: āpūryamāṇam acalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat
children.translated_text: As waters enter the ocean, ever being filled yet fixed and unmoving,

children.text: tadvat kāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāmakāmī ||
children.translated_text: so all desires enter the man who attains peace; not so the man who desires desires.
Then one who wishes to perform a <s>śrāddha</s> should invite Brahmins on the preceding day.

children.text: dvitīye 'hni śuklapakṣasya pūrvāhṇe kṛṣṇapakṣasyāparāhṇe viprān susnātān svācāntān yathābhūyo vayaḥkrameṇa kuśottareṣv āsaneṣūpaveśayet ||
children.translated_text: On the second day, in the forenoon in the bright fortnight and in the afternoon in the dark fortnight, he should seat the Brahmins, well bathed and properly sipped, in order of seniority as far as possible, on seats strewn with <s>kuśa</s> grass.

children.text: dvau daive prāṅmukhau trīṃśca pitrye udaṅmukhān ||
children.translated_text: Two should face east for the divine rite, and three should face north for the ancestral rite.
Or there may be one for each on both sides.
In raw-food <s>śrāddhas</s> and optional rites, he should first offer into the fire with the first pentad of formulas.
In animal <s>śrāddhas</s>, with the middle pentad.
On new-moon days, with the last pentad.

children.text: āgrahāyaṇyā ūrdhvaṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭakāsu ca krameṇaiva prathamamadhyamottamapañcakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s>, and on the dark-half eighth days, he should use in sequence the first, middle, and last pentads.
And likewise on the days following those eighth days.
Then, with the permission of the Brahmins, he should invoke the ancestors.

children.text: apayantvasurā iti dvābhyāṃ tilaiḥ yātudhānānāṃ visarjanaṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: With the two verses beginning “Let the demons depart,” he should dismiss the <s>yātudhānas</s> with sesame seeds.

children.text: eta pitaraḥ sarvāṃstān agra ā me yantvetad vaḥ pitara ityāvāhanaṃ kṛtvā kuśatilamiśreṇa gandhodakena yās tiṣṭhantyamṛtā vāg iti yan me māteti ca pādyaṃ nivedya arghyaṃ kṛtvā nivedya cānulepanaṃ kṛtvā kuśatilavastrapuṣpālaṃkāradhūpadīpair yathāśaktyā viprān samabhyarcya ghṛtaplutam annam ādāya ādityā rudrā vasava iti vīkṣya agnau karavāṇītyuktvā tacca vipraiḥ kurv ityukte āhutitrayaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having made the invocation with the formulas beginning “Come, ancestors” and “May all those ancestors come before me; this is yours, ancestors,” he should offer foot-water with fragrant water mixed with <s>kuśa</s> and sesame, using the formulas beginning “Those who stand, immortal speech” and “What is my mother”; then, after preparing and presenting the arghya, making an anointing, and worshiping the Brahmins as far as he is able with <s>kuśa</s>, sesame, garments, flowers, ornaments, incense, and lamps, he should take food soaked in ghee, look upon it with the formula “<s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Vasus</s>,” say “Shall I make it in the fire?” and, when the Brahmins say “Do it,” offer three oblations.

children.text: ye māmakāḥ pitara etad vaḥ pitaro 'yaṃ yajña iti ca haviranumantraṇaṃ kṛtvā yathopapanneṣu pātreṣu viśeṣād rajatamayeṣv annaṃ namo viśvebhyo devebhya ityannam ādau prāṅmukhayor nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: After consecrating the oblation with the formulas “My ancestors” and “This is yours, ancestors; this is the sacrifice,” he should place the food in suitable vessels, especially silver ones, and first present it to the two facing east with “Homage to all the gods.”

children.text: pitre pitāmahāya prapitāmahāya ca nāmagotrābhyām udaṅmukheṣu ||
children.translated_text: To the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather he should present it, with their names and gotras, to those facing north.

children.text: tad adatsu brāhmaṇeṣu yan me prakāmād ahorātrair yad vaḥ kravyād iti japet ||
children.translated_text: While the Brahmins are eating it, he should recite the formulas beginning “What through my desire, by days and nights” and “What of yours, flesh-eater.”
And the histories, <s>purāṇas</s>, and dharma treatises should be recited.

children.text: ucchiṣṭasaṃnidhau dakṣiṇāgreṣu kuśeṣu pṛthivī darvir akṣitā ityekaṃ piṇḍaṃ pitre nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Near the leftovers, on <s>kuśa</s> grass with its tips turned south, he should place one <s>piṇḍa</s> for the father with the formula “The earth is the unexhausted ladle.”

children.text: antarikṣaṃ darvir akṣitā iti dvitīyaṃ piṇḍaṃ pitāmahāya ||
children.translated_text: A second <s>piṇḍa</s> for the grandfather with “The midspace is the unexhausted ladle.”

children.text: dyaur darvir akṣitā iti tṛtīyaṃ prapitāmahāya ||
children.translated_text: A third for the great-grandfather with “Heaven is the unexhausted ladle.”

children.text: ye atra pitaraḥ pretā iti vāso deyam ||
children.translated_text: A garment should be given with the formula “Those ancestors here who are departed.”
Food should be given with “Our ancestors, bestow heroic sons.”

children.text: atra pitaro mādayadhvaṃ yathābhāgam iti darbhamūle karāvagharṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: With “Here, ancestors, rejoice according to your share,” he should rub his hands at the root of the <s>darbha</s> grass.

children.text: ūrjaṃ vahantīr ityanena sodakena pradakṣiṇaṃ piṇḍānāṃ vikiraṇaṃ kṛtvā arghapuṣpadhūpālepanānnādibhakṣyabhojyāni nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: With the verse beginning “Bearing nourishment,” and with water, he should scatter offerings clockwise around the <s>piṇḍas</s>, and should present arghya, flowers, incense, anointing, food, and other eatables and dishes.
And he should present a water vessel mixed with honey, ghee, and sesame.

children.text: bhuktavatsu brāhmaṇeṣu tṛptim āgateṣu mā me kṣeṣṭhety annaṃ satṛṇam abhyukṣyānnavikiram ucchiṣṭāgrataḥ kṛtvā tṛptā bhavantaḥ sampannam iti ca pṛṣṭvā udaṅmukheṣvācamanam ādau dattvā tataḥ prāṅmukheṣu dattvā tataśca suprokṣitam iti śrāddhadeśaṃ saṃprokṣya darbhapāṇiḥ sarvaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When the Brahmins have eaten and have reached satisfaction, he should sprinkle food together with grass while saying “May it not be exhausted for me,” place the scattered food before the leftovers, ask “Are you satisfied? Is it complete?”, first give water for sipping to those facing north, then to those facing east, and then sprinkle the <s>śrāddha</s> place with “well sprinkled”; he should do everything with <s>darbha</s> in hand.

children.text: tataḥ prāṅmukhāgrato yan me rāma iti pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā pratyetya ca yathāśaktidakṣiṇābhiḥ samabhyarcya abhiramantu bhavanta ityuktvā tair ukte 'bhiratāḥ sma iti devāśca pitaraścetyabhijapet ||
children.translated_text: Then, in front of those facing east, he should circumambulate clockwise with the formula beginning “What is mine, <s>Rāma</s>,” return, honor them with gifts according to his ability, and say “May your honors be pleasing”; when they say “We are pleased,” he should recite “the gods and the ancestors.”

children.text: akṣayyodakaṃ ca nāmagotrābhyāṃ dattvā viśve devāḥ prīyantām iti prāṅmukhebhyas tataḥ prāñjalir idaṃ tanmanāḥ sumanā yāceta ||
children.translated_text: Having given inexhaustible water with the names and gotras, and having said “May the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> be pleased” to those facing east, he should then, with joined palms, intent and well disposed, request this:

children.text: dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ saṃtatir eva ca
children.translated_text: “May our givers increase, and also the Vedas and our lineage;

children.text: śraddhā ca no mā vyagamad bahu deyaṃ ca no 'stv iti ||
children.translated_text: may faith not depart from us, and may there be much for us to give.”
They should say, "So be it."

children.text: annaṃ ca no bahu bhaved atithīṃśca labhemahi
children.translated_text: "May our food be abundant, and may we obtain guests;

children.text: yācitāraśca naḥ santu mā ca yāciṣma kaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: may we have petitioners, and may we not beg from anyone."
Having received the blessings with these two verses,

children.text: vāje vāja iti ca tato brāhmaṇāṃśca visarjayet
children.translated_text: then, saying "<s>vāje vāje</s>," he should dismiss the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>;
after honoring them according to rule, accompanying them, and saluting them.

children.text: aṣṭakāsu daivapūrvaṃ śākamāṃsāpūpaiḥ śrāddhaṃ kṛtvānvaṣṭakāsv aṣṭakāvad vahnau hutvā daivapūrvam eva mātre pitāmahyai prapitāmahyai ca pūrvavad brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā dakṣiṇābhiścābhyarcyānuvrajya visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: At the <s>Aṣṭakās</s>, after performing the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite), with the divine rite first, using vegetables, meat, and cakes, and at the <s>Anvaṣṭakās</s>, as at the <s>Aṣṭakās</s>, after offering into the fire, again with the divine rite first, for his mother, paternal grandmother, and paternal great-grandmother, he should feed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> as before, honor them with gifts, accompany them, and dismiss them.
After that he should make trenches.
At their base, after setting the fire toward the east and north, there is the placing of the <s>piṇḍas</s> (ancestral food-balls).
At the base of three trenches for the men, and at the base of three trenches for the women.
He should fill the three trenches for the men with water mixed with food.
The three trenches for the women he should fill with milk mixed with food.
With curds, meat, and milk, he should fill each set of three trenches.

children.text: pūrayitvā japed etad bhavadbhyo bhavatībhyo 'stu cākṣayam ||
children.translated_text: After filling them, he should recite this: "May this be inexhaustible for you men and for you women."

children.text: pitari jīvati yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kuryāt sa yeṣāṃ pitā kuryāt teṣāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If a man performs a <s>śrāddha</s> while his father is alive, he should perform it for those for whom his father would perform it.

children.text: pitari pitāmahe ca jīvati yeṣāṃ pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When his father and grandfather are alive, he should perform it for those for whom his grandfather would perform it.

children.text: pitari pitāmahe prapitāmahe ca jīvati naiva kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When his father, grandfather, and great-grandfather are alive, he should not perform it at all.

children.text: yasya pitā pretaḥ syāt sa pitre piṇḍaṃ nidhāya pitāmahāt paraṃ dvābhyāṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If a man's father is deceased, he should place a <s>piṇḍa</s> for his father and give to the two beyond his grandfather.

children.text: yasya pitā pitāmahaśca pretau syātāṃ sa tābhyāṃ piṇḍau dattvā pitāmahapitāmahāya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If a man's father and grandfather are both deceased, he should give <s>piṇḍas</s> to those two and give one to the ancestor called the grandfather's grandfather.

children.text: yasya pitāmahaḥ pretaḥ syāt sa tasmai piṇḍaṃ nidhāya prapitāmahāt paraṃ dvābhyāṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: If a man's grandfather is deceased, he should place a <s>piṇḍa</s> for him and give to the two beyond his great-grandfather.
A wise man should perform the <s>śrāddha</s> for the maternal grandfathers also in this same way,
with alteration of the mantra according to rule; for the remaining ones, it is to be done without mantras.

children.text: amāvāsyās tisro 'ṣṭakās tisro 'nvaṣṭakā māghī prauṣṭhapady ūrdhvaṃ kṛṣṇatrayodaśī vrīhiyavapākau ceti ||
children.translated_text: The new-moon days, the three <s>Aṣṭakās</s>, the three <s>Anvaṣṭakās</s>, the <s>Māghī</s>, the <s>Prauṣṭhapadī</s>, the following dark thirteenth day, and the ripening times of rice and barley:

children.text: etāṃs tu śrāddhakālān vai nityān āha prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> has declared these to be the regular times for <s>śrāddha</s>;
one who does not perform <s>śrāddha</s> at these times falls into hell.
The solar ingress;
the two equinoxes;
especially the two solstices;
the <s>vyatīpāta</s> conjunction;
the birth asterism;
and an occasion of prosperity.

children.text: etāṃs tu śrāddhakālān vai kāmyān āha prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> has declared these to be optional times for <s>śrāddha</s>;

children.text: śrāddham eteṣu yad dattaṃ tad ānantyāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: a <s>śrāddha</s> given on these occasions is fit to become endless in its result.

children.text: saṃdhyārātryor na kartavyaṃ śrāddhaṃ khalu vicakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: The wise should certainly not perform <s>śrāddha</s> at twilight or at night;

children.text: tayor api ca kartavyaṃ yadi syād rāhudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: but even at those times it should be performed if there is an eclipse.
For a <s>śrāddha</s> given at an eclipse, lasting as long as the moon and stars,
reaches the ancestors, endowed with merit and granting all desires.

children.text: satatam āditye 'hni śrāddhaṃ kurvann ārogyam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: By always performing <s>śrāddha</s> on the day of the Sun, one obtains health.
On the day of the Moon, good fortune.
On the day of Mars, victory in battle.
On the day of Mercury, all desires.
On the day of Jupiter, the desired learning.
On the day of Venus, wealth.
On the day of Saturn, long life.
In <s>Kṛttikā</s>, heaven.
In <s>Rohiṇī</s>, offspring.
In the asterism of <s>Soma</s>, sacred brilliance.
In the asterism of <s>Rudra</s>, success in undertakings.
In <s>Punarvasu</s>, land.
In <s>Puṣya</s>, nourishment.
In the asterism of the Serpents, prosperity.
In the asterism of the Fathers, all desires.
In the asterism of <s>Bhaga</s>, good fortune.
In the asterism of <s>Aryaman</s>, wealth.
In <s>Hasta</s>, eminence among kinsmen.
In the asterism of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, handsome sons.
In <s>Svāti</s>, success in trade.
In <s>Viśākhā</s>, gold.
In the asterism of <s>Mitra</s>, friends.
In the asterism of <s>Śakra</s>, kingship.
In <s>Mūla</s>, agriculture.
In the asterism of the Waters, success in sea-voyaging.
In the asterism of the <s>Viśvadevas</s>, all desires.
In <s>Abhijit</s>, superiority.
In <s>Śravaṇa</s>, all desires.
In the asterism of the <s>Vasus</s>, salt.
In the asterism of <s>Varuṇa</s>, health.
In the asterism of <s>Aja</s>, base-metal goods.
In the asterism of <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, a house.
In the asterism of <s>Pūṣan</s>, cows.
In <s>Aśvinī</s>, horses.
In the asterism of <s>Yama</s>, long life.
On the first lunar day, a house and beautiful women.
On the second lunar day, a maiden who grants boons.
On the third lunar day, all desires.
On the fourth lunar day, cattle.
On the fifth lunar day, handsome sons.
On the sixth lunar day, victory in gambling.
On the seventh lunar day, agriculture.
On the eighth lunar day, trade.
On the ninth lunar day, cattle.
On the tenth lunar day, horses.
On the eleventh lunar day, sons possessing sacred brilliance.
On the twelfth lunar day, gold and silver.
On the thirteenth lunar day, good fortune.
On the fifteenth lunar day, all desires.
For the <s>śrāddha</s> rite of those slain by weapons, the fourteenth lunar day is praised.
There are also two verses sung by the ancestors:

children.text: api jāyeta so 'smākaṃ kule kaścin narottamaḥ
children.translated_text: "May some best of men be born in our family,
who, concentrated, in the rainy season, in the dark fortnight, on the thirteenth day,
would perform <s>śrāddha</s> with milk-rice rich in honey,

children.text: kārttikaṃ sakalaṃ māsaṃ prākchāye kuñjarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: for the whole month of <s>Kārttika</s>, and in the forward shade of an elephant."

children.text: atha na naktaṃ gṛhītenodakena śrāddhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Now he should not perform <s>śrāddha</s> at night with water that has been taken up.

children.text: kuśābhāve kuśasthāne kāśān dūrvāṃ vā dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>kuśa</s> grass is lacking, he should give <s>kāśa</s> grass or <s>dūrvā</s> grass in place of <s>kuśa</s>.
For the purpose of a garment, cotton thread should be given.
He should discard the fringe, even if it comes from an unworn garment.
Flowers that are strong-smelling, without fragrance, or born on thorny plants are unsuitable.

children.text: śuklāni sugandhīni kaṇṭakijānyapi jalajāni raktānyapi dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: He may give white, fragrant flowers, even if they grow on thorny plants, and water-born flowers, even if they are red.

children.text: vasāṃ medaṃ ca dīpārthe na dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not give fat or marrow for the purpose of a lamp.
He should give ghee or oil.
He should not give anything produced from living creatures for the purpose of incense.
He should give <s>guggulu</s> mixed with honey and ghee.
Sandalwood, saffron, camphor, agaru, and lotus products are for anointing.
He should not give salt that is directly visible.
Nor should he serve ghee, relishes, and the like with his hand.
He should give metal vessels.
Especially silver ones.
He should place there a rhinoceros horn, a <s>kutapa</s> blanket, black antelope skin, sesame, white mustard, and unbroken grains, as purifying things and things that destroy demons.

He should avoid long pepper, <s>mukundaka</s>, <s>bhūstṛṇa</s>, <s>śigru</s>, mustard, <s>surasā</s>, <s>sarjaka</s>, <s>suvarcalā</s>, pumpkin, bottle-gourd, eggplant, <s>pālakyā</s>, <s>upodakī</s>, <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, safflower, <s>piṇḍāluka</s>, and buffalo milk.
And kidney beans, lentils, stale food, and prepared salt.
He should avoid anger.
He should not shed tears.
He should not act hastily.

children.text: ghṛtādidāne taijasāni pātrāṇi khaḍgapātrāṇi phalgupātrāṇi ca praśastāni ||
children.translated_text: For the giving of ghee and the like, metal vessels, rhinoceros-horn vessels, and <s>phalgu</s>-wood vessels are commended.
On this there is a verse:
In gold or silver, or in rhinoceros horn or udumbara wood,
what is given becomes imperishable, and also when given in a <s>phalgu</s> vessel.

children.text: tilair vrīhiyavair māṣair adbhir mūlaphalaiḥ śākaiḥ śyāmākaiḥ priyaṅgubhir nīvārair mudgair godhūmaiśca māsaṃ prīyante ||
children.translated_text: With sesame, rice, barley, <s>māṣa</s> beans, water, roots and fruits, greens, <s>śyāmāka</s> millet, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, wild rice, mung beans, and wheat, the ancestors are pleased for a month.
For two months with fish meat.
For three with deer meat.
And for four with sheep meat.
For five with bird meat.
For six with goat meat.
For seven with <s>ruru</s>-deer meat.
For eight with spotted-deer meat.
For nine with gayal meat.
For ten with buffalo meat.
For eleven with the meat of a <s>tūpara</s> goat.
For a year with cow's milk or its products.
On this there is a stanza sung by the ancestors:
<s>Kālaśāka</s>, the great-scaled fish, and the meat of the <s>vārdhrīṇasa</s>,

children.text: viṣāṇavarjyā ye khaḍgā ā sūryaṃ tāṃs tu bhuṅkṣmahe ||
children.translated_text: and those rhinoceroses except for their horns: these we eat as long as the sun endures.
He should not place food on a seat.
He should not touch it with his foot.
He should not sneeze over it.
With sesame or mustard seeds he should drive away the <s>yātudhānas</s> (demons).
He should perform the <s>śrāddha</s> in an enclosed place.
He should not look at a menstruating woman.
Nor at a dog.
Nor at a filth-eating pig.
Nor at a village rooster.
He should make the <s>śrāddha</s> visible to a goat with care.
And the Brahmins should eat with speech restrained.
Not with their heads wrapped.
Not wearing sandals.
Not with their feet set upon a stool.
Those lacking limbs or having extra limbs should not see the <s>śrāddha</s>.
Nor Śūdras.
Nor fallen men.
Nor those with serious disease.

children.text: tatkālaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brāhmaṇānumatena bhikṣukaṃ vā pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: At that time he should honor a Brahmin, or, with the Brahmins' permission, a mendicant.

children.text: havirguṇān na brāhmaṇā brūyur dātrā pṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Brahmins should not speak of the qualities of the oblation, even when asked by the donor.

children.text: yāvad ūṣmā bhavatyanne yāvad aśnanti vāgyatāḥ
children.translated_text: As long as the food is warm, and as long as they eat with speech restrained,

children.text: tāvad aśnanti pitaro yāvan noktā havirguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so long the ancestors eat, as long as the qualities of the oblation have not been stated.
Having gathered food and eatables suitable for all varṇas and sprinkled them with water,
he should cast them forth before those who have eaten, scattering them on the ground.
For those who died without rites, for renouncers, and for women of the family,

children.text: ucchiṣṭaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ syād darbheṣu vikiraśca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the leftovers should be the allotted share, and whatever scattering is made on <s>darbha</s> grass.
The leavings that have fallen on the ground, for one who is straightforward and not deceitful,
that, they declare, is the ancestral allotted share of the class of servants.
In a rite for the gods he should not scrutinize a Brahmin.
In one for the ancestors he should scrutinize him carefully.
He should avoid those with deficient or excessive limbs.
And those engaged in improper occupations.
Those who practice a cat-like vow.
Those who wear religious marks in vain.
Those who live by the stars.
And temple-priests.
Physicians.
Sons of unmarried women.
Their sons.
Those who sacrifice for many patrons.
Village priests.
Those who sacrifice for Śūdras.
Those who sacrifice for persons not entitled to sacrifice.
<s>Vrātyas</s>.
Those who sacrifice for them.
Makers of festival calendars.
Informers.
Teachers for hire.
Those taught for hire.
Those nourished by Śūdra food.
Those who associate with the fallen.
Those who do not study.
Those who have lapsed from twilight worship.
Servants of the king.
Naked ascetics.
Those who quarrel with their father.
And those who abandon father, mother, teacher, sacred fire, and Vedic study.
These are said to be degraded Brahmins, defilers of the ritual row;
a learned man should carefully avoid them in the <s>śrāddha</s> rite.
Now the purifiers of the ritual row:
One who knows the <s>Triṇāciketa</s>.
One who maintains the five fires.
A chanter of the <s>Jyeṣṭha-sāman</s>.
One who has mastered the Veda.
One who has mastered even one <s>Vedāṅga</s>.
One who has mastered <s>purāṇa</s>, <s>itihāsa</s>, and grammar.
One who has mastered even one <s>dharmaśāstra</s>.
One purified by pilgrimage.
One purified by sacrifice.
One purified by austerity.
One purified by truth.
One purified by mantra.
One devoted to recitation of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
One descended from a <s>brahmadeya</s> line.
One who knows the <s>Trisuparṇa</s>.
A son-in-law.
And a daughter's son: these are fit recipients.
And especially yogins.
On this there is a stanza sung by the ancestors:

children.text: api sa syāt kule 'smākaṃ bhojayed yas tu yoginam
children.translated_text: May there be in our family one who will feed a yogin,

children.text: vipraṃ śrāddhe prayatnena yena tṛpyāmahe vayam ||
children.translated_text: a Brahmin at a <s>śrāddha</s> with care, by whom we may be satisfied.
He should not perform a <s>śrāddha</s> in a <s>mleccha</s> region.
He should not go to a <s>mleccha</s> region.
For, having drunk water at another's watering place, one attains equality with him.
The country in which the ordering of the four varṇas does not exist

children.text: sa mlecchadeśo vijñeya āryāvartas tataḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be known as a <s>mleccha</s> country; <s>Āryāvarta</s> is other than that.
Now, at <s>Puṣkara</s>, the <s>śrāddha</s> is imperishable.
and muttering, fire-offerings, and austerities.
At <s>Puṣkara</s>, by bathing alone one becomes purified from all sins.
So too at <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s>.
At the <s>Vaṭa</s>.
On <s>Amarakaṇṭaka</s> mountain.
On <s>Varāha</s> mountain.
Anywhere on the bank of the <s>Narmadā</s>.
On the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
Especially in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
At <s>Kuśāvarta</s>.
At <s>Binduka</s>.
On <s>Nīla</s> mountain.
At <s>Kanakhala</s>.
At <s>Kubjāmra</s>.
At <s>Bhṛgutuṅga</s>.
At <s>Kedāra</s>.
At <s>Mahālaya</s>.
At <s>Naḍantikā</s>.
At <s>Sugandhā</s>.
At <s>Śākaṃbharī</s>.
At the <s>Phalgu</s> tīrtha.
At <s>Mahāgaṅgā</s>.
In the village of <s>Trihalikā</s>.
At <s>Kumāradhārā</s>.
At <s>Prabhāsa</s>.
Anywhere on the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, especially.
At <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>.
And at <s>Prayāga</s>.
At the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the ocean.
Always in <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>.
Especially at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
At the hermitage of <s>Agastya</s>.
At the hermitage of <s>Kaṇva</s>.
On the <s>Kauśikī</s>.
On the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>.
At the confluence of the <s>Śoṇa</s> and the <s>Jyotiṣā</s>.
On <s>Śrīparvata</s>.
At <s>Kālodaka</s>.
At <s>Uttaramānasa</s>.
At <s>Baḍabā</s>.
At <s>Mataṅgavāpī</s>.
At <s>Saptārṣa</s>.
At <s>Viṣṇupada</s>.
At <s>Svargamārgapada</s>.
On the <s>Godāvarī</s>.
On the <s>Gomatī</s>.
On the <s>Vetravatī</s>.
On the <s>Vipāśā</s>.
On the <s>Vitastā</s>.
On the bank of the <s>Śatadrū</s>.
On the <s>Candrabhāgā</s>.
On the <s>Irāvatī</s>.
On the bank of the <s>Sindhu</s>.
At the southern <s>Pañcanada</s>.
At <s>Ausaja</s>.
And at other tīrthas such as these.
At excellent rivers.
And in all natural holy places.
On sandbanks.
At springs.
On mountains.
In groves.
In forests.
In pleasure groves.
In houses smeared with cow-dung.
In pleasing places.
And here there are verses sung by the ancestors:

children.text: kule 'smākaṃ sa jantuḥ syād yo no dadyāj jalāñjalīn
children.translated_text: May that being be born in our family who would give us handfuls of water
in rivers rich in water, especially cool ones.

children.text: api jāyeta so 'smākaṃ kule kaścin narottamaḥ
children.translated_text: May some best of men be born in our family,

children.text: gayāśīrṣe vaṭe śrāddhaṃ yo naḥ kuryāt samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who, composed in mind, would perform <s>śrāddha</s> for us at <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s>, by the <s>Vaṭa</s>.

children.text: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Many sons should be desired, if even one of them should go to <s>Gayā</s>,

children.text: yajeta vāśvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣam utsṛjet ||
children.translated_text: or should sacrifice with the horse-sacrifice, or release a blue bull.
Now, the releasing of a bull.
In the month of <s>Kārttika</s> or in <s>Āśvayuja</s>.
At the very beginning of that rite he should examine a bull.
It should be the son of a milk-giving cow whose calf is alive.
It should be endowed with every auspicious mark.
It may be blue.
Or red, with white face, tail, feet, and horns.
It should be fit to cover the herd.

children.text: tato gavāṃ madhye susamiddham agniṃ paristīrya pauṣṇaṃ caruṃ payasā śrapayitvā pūṣā gā anvetu na iha ratir iti ca hutvā vṛṣam ayaskāras tv aṅkayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, among the cows, after strewing around a well-kindled fire, cooking a <s>Pūṣan</s> oblation with milk, and offering with the formulas “May <s>Pūṣan</s> follow our cows” and “Here is delight,” the ironsmith should mark the bull.
On one side with a discus, and on the other side with a trident.

children.text: aṅkitaṃ ca hiraṇyavarṇeti catasṛbhiḥ śaṃ no devīr iti ca snāpayet ||
children.translated_text: After it has been marked, he should bathe it with the four verses beginning “golden-colored” and with “May the divine waters bring us blessing.”

children.text: snātam alaṃkṛtaṃ snātālaṃkṛtābhiścatasṛbhir vatsatarībhiḥ sārdham ānīya rudrān puruṣasūktaṃ kūśmāṇḍīśca japet ||
children.translated_text: When it has been bathed and adorned, he should bring it together with four young heifers that have also been bathed and adorned, and should recite the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, and the <s>Kūśmāṇḍīs</s>.

children.text: pitā vatsānām iti vṛṣabhasya dakṣiṇe karṇe paṭhet ||
children.translated_text: He should recite “father of calves” into the bull's right ear.
And this also:
For the bull is the blessed <s>dharma</s>, proclaimed as four-footed;

children.text: vṛṇomi tam ahaṃ bhaktyā sa me rakṣatu sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I choose him with devotion; may he protect me on every side.

children.text: etaṃ yuvānaṃ patiṃ vo dadāmyanena krīḍantīścarata priyeṇa
children.translated_text: I give you this young husband; playing with this beloved one, move about.

children.text: mā hāsmahi prajayā mā tanūbhir mā radhāma dviṣate soma rājan ||
children.translated_text: May we not be deprived of offspring, nor of our bodies; may we not fall into the power of the enemy, O king <s>Soma</s>.
He should have the bull, joined with the young heifers, placed in the northeastern direction.

children.text: hotur vastrayugaṃ dadyāt suvarṇaṃ kāṃsyam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He should give the officiating priest a pair of garments, gold, and also a bronze vessel.
The ironsmith should be given the fee he desires.
And he should feed the Brahmins with food rich in ghee.
In whatever reservoir the released bull then drinks,
that entire reservoir comes to serve his ancestors.
Wherever, being proud, it scratches the earth with its horn,
that becomes abundant food and drink presented to the ancestors.

children.text: atha vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ sakhuraṃ saśṛṅgaṃ suvarṇaśṛṅgaṃ raupyakhuraṃ mauktikalāṅgūlabhūṣitaṃ kṛtvāvike ca vastre prasārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the full moon of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, he should take a black antelope skin with hoofs and horns, give it golden horns, silver hoofs, and an ornamented tail of pearls, and spread it on woolen cloth and another cloth.
Then he should cover it with sesame seeds.
And he should make a golden navel.
He should cover it with a pair of unworn garments.
He should make it adorned with all perfumes and jewels.

children.text: catasṛṣu dikṣu catvāri taijasāni pātrāṇi kṣīradadhimadhughṛtapūrṇāni nidhāyāhitāgnaye brāhmaṇāyālaṃkṛtāya vāsoyugena pracchāditāya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having placed in the four directions four metal vessels filled with milk, curds, honey, and ghee, he should give it to an adorned Brahmin who maintains the sacred fires and is covered with a pair of garments.
And here there are verses:

children.text: yas tu kṛṣṇājinaṃ dadyāt sakhuraṃ śṛṅgasaṃyutam
children.translated_text: But whoever gives a black antelope skin, furnished with hoofs and horns,
covered with sesame seeds and garments, adorned with all jewels,
by him the earth, together with its oceans and caves, with its mountains, forests, and groves,

children.text: caturantā bhaved dattā pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bounded by the four quarters, has been given; of this there is no doubt.
Whoever, having placed sesame seeds on a black antelope skin, gives gold, honey, and ghee

children.text: dadāti yas tu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: to a Brahmin crosses beyond every evil deed.
Now, a cow that is giving birth becomes the earth.

children.text: tām alaṃkṛtāṃ brāhmaṇāya dattvā pṛthivīdānaphalam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: By giving her, adorned, to a Brahmin, he obtains the fruit of giving the earth.
Here there is a verse:
For as many ages as there are hairs on the cow with her calf, facing both ways...
Having given it, a faithful and composed man obtains heaven.
The month <s>Kārttika</s> has <s>Agni</s> as its deity.
And <s>Agni</s> is the mouth of all the gods.

children.text: tasmāt tu kārttikaṃ māsaṃ bahiḥsnāyī gāyatrījapanirataḥ sakṛd eva haviṣyāśī saṃvatsarakṛtāt pāpāt pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, during the month <s>Kārttika</s>, one who bathes outdoors, is devoted to reciting the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and eats sacrificial food only once becomes purified from sin committed over a year.
Throughout the whole month <s>Kārttika</s>, one who bathes daily and has conquered his senses,
reciting, eating sacrificial food, and restrained, is released from all sins.

children.text: mārgaśīrṣaśuklapañcadaśyāṃ mṛgaśirasā yuktāyāṃ cūrṇitalavaṇasya suvarṇanābhaṃ prastham ekaṃ candrodaye brāhmaṇāya pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: On the bright-fortnight fifteenth day of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, when it is joined with <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, at moonrise he should cause a Brahmin to receive one <s>prastha</s> of powdered salt with gold at its center.
By this act he is born possessing beauty and good fortune.

children.text: pauṣī cet puṣyayuktā syāt tasyāṃ gaurasarṣapakalkodvartitaśarīro gavyaghṛtapūrṇakumbhenābhiṣiktaḥ sarvauṣadhibhiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ sarvabījaiśca snāto ghṛtena bhagavantaṃ vāsudevaṃ snāpayitvā gandhapuṣpadhūpadīpanaivedyādibhir abhyarcya vaiṣṇavaiḥ śākrair bārhaspatyaiśca mantraiḥ pāvake hutvā sasuvarṇena ghṛtena brāhmaṇān svasti vācayet ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Pauṣī</s> full-moon day is joined with <s>Puṣya</s>, then on it, with his body rubbed with a paste of white mustard, sprinkled with a jar full of cow's ghee, and bathed with all herbs, all perfumes, and all seeds, he should bathe the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> with ghee, worship him with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and the like, offer oblations in the fire with Vaiṣṇava, Śākra, and Bārhaspatya mantras, and have Brahmins pronounce blessings with ghee accompanied by gold.
He should give a pair of garments to the officiant.
By this act he prospers.

children.text: māghī maghāyutā cet tasyāṃ tilaiḥ śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Māghī</s> full-moon day is joined with <s>Maghā</s>, then on it, after performing a <s>śrāddha</s> with sesame seeds, he becomes purified.

children.text: phālgunī phalgunīyutā cet tasyāṃ brāhmaṇāya susaṃskṛtaṃ svāstīrṇaṃ śayanaṃ nivedya bhāryāṃ manojñāṃ rūpavatīṃ draviṇavatīṃ cāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Phālgunī</s> full-moon day is joined with <s>Phalgunī</s>, then on it, after presenting to a Brahmin a well-prepared bed that has been properly spread, he obtains a wife who is pleasing, beautiful, and wealthy.
A woman likewise obtains a husband.

children.text: caitrī citrāyutā cet tasyāṃ citravastrapradānena saubhāgyam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Caitrī</s> full-moon day is joined with <s>Citrā</s>, then on it he obtains good fortune by giving variegated garments.

children.text: vaiśākhī viśākhāyutā cet tasyāṃ brāhmaṇasaptakaṃ kṣaudrayuktais tilaiḥ saṃtarpya dharmarājānaṃ prīṇayitvā pāpebhyaḥ pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Vaiśākhī</s> full-moon day is joined with <s>Viśākhā</s>, then on it, after satisfying a group of seven Brahmins with sesame seeds mixed with honey and pleasing <s>Dharmarāja</s>, he becomes purified from sins.

children.text: jyaiṣṭhī jyeṣṭhāyutā cet syāt tasyāṃ chatropānahapradānena gavādhipatyaṃ prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Jyaiṣṭhī</s> full-moon day is joined with <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, then on it he obtains lordship over cattle by giving an umbrella and sandals.

children.text: āṣāḍhyām āṣāḍhāyuktāyām annapānadānena tad evākṣayyam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: On <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>, when it is joined with <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>, by giving food and drink he obtains that same gift as imperishable.

children.text: śrāvaṇyāṃ śravaṇayuktāyāṃ jaladhenuṃ sānnāṃ vāsoyugācchāditāṃ dattvā svargam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: On <s>Śrāvaṇī</s>, when it is joined with <s>Śravaṇa</s>, after giving a water-cow, furnished with food and covered with a pair of garments, he obtains heaven.
On <s>Prauṣṭhapadī</s>, when it is joined with <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>, by giving a cow he becomes freed from all sin.

children.text: āśvayujyām aśvinīgate candramasi ghṛtapūrṇaṃ bhājanaṃ suvarṇayutaṃ viprāya dattvā dīptāgnir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: On <s>Āśvayujī</s>, when the moon is in <s>Aśvinī</s>, after giving to a Brahmin a vessel full of ghee and accompanied by gold, he becomes one with a strong digestive fire.

children.text: kārttikī kṛttikāyutā cet syāt tasyāṃ sitam ukṣāṇam anyavarṇaṃ vā śaśāṅkodaye sarvasasyaratnagandhopetaṃ dīpamadhye brāhmaṇāya dattvā kāntārabhayaṃ na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: If <s>Kārttikī</s> is joined with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, then on it, at moonrise, after giving to a Brahmin a white bull or one of another color, provided with every grain, jewel, and perfume, in the midst of lamps, he does not encounter danger in wildernesses.

children.text: vaiśākhaśuklatṛtīyāyām upoṣito 'kṣataiḥ śrīvāsudevam abhyarcya tān eva hutvā dattvā ca sarvapāpebhyaḥ pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: On the bright-fortnight third day of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, having fasted, worshiped <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s> with unbroken grains, and then offered those same grains in the fire and given them away, he becomes purified from all sins.

children.text: yacca tasminn ahani prayacchati tad akṣayyatām āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: And whatever he gives on that day becomes imperishable.

children.text: pauṣyāṃ samatītāyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣadvādaśyāṃ sopavāsas tilaiḥ snātas tilodakaṃ dattvā tilair vāsudevam abhyarcya tān eva hutvā dattvā bhuktvā ca pāpebhyaḥ pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Pauṣī</s> has passed, on the dark-fortnight twelfth day, fasting, bathed with sesame seeds, after giving sesame-water, worshiping <s>Vāsudeva</s> with sesame seeds, and then offering those same seeds in the fire, giving them away, and eating them, he becomes purified from sins.

children.text: māghyāṃ samatītāyāṃ kṛṣṇadvādaśyāṃ sopavāsaḥ śravaṇaṃ prāpya śrīvāsudevāgrato mahāvartidvayena dīpadvayaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Māghī</s> has passed, on the dark twelfth day, fasting, when the moon has reached <s>Śravaṇa</s>, he should give two lamps with two great wicks before <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇapārśve mahārajanaraktena samagreṇa vāsasā ghṛtatulām aṣṭādhikāṃ dattvā ||
children.translated_text: On the right side, after giving a measure of ghee increased by eight, together with a complete garment dyed deep red,

children.text: vāmapārśve tilatailayutāṃ sāṣṭāṃ dattvā śvetena samagreṇa vāsasā ||
children.translated_text: and on the left side, after giving sesame oil likewise increased by eight, together with a complete white garment,

children.text: etat kṛtvā yasmin rāṣṭre 'bhijāyate yasmin deśe yasmin kule tatrojjvalo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: having done this, in whatever kingdom, whatever region, and whatever family he is born, there he becomes brilliant.

children.text: āśvinaṃ sakalaṃ māsaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pratyahaṃ ghṛtaṃ pradāyāśvinau prīṇayitvā rūpabhāg bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Throughout the whole month <s>Āśvina</s>, by giving ghee every day to Brahmins and pleasing the <s>Aśvins</s>, he becomes endowed with beauty.

children.text: tasminn eva māsi pratyahaṃ gorasair brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā rājyabhāg bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In that same month, by feeding Brahmins every day with cow's milk products, he becomes endowed with kingship.

children.text: pratimāsaṃ revatīyute candramasi madhughṛtayutaṃ pāyasaṃ revatīprītyai paramānnaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā revatīṃ prīṇayitvā rūpasya bhāgī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Every month, when the moon is joined with <s>Revatī</s>, by feeding Brahmins with excellent rice pudding mixed with honey and ghee for the pleasure of <s>Revatī</s>, and by pleasing <s>Revatī</s>, he becomes endowed with beauty.

children.text: māghe māsyagniṃ pratyahaṃ tilair hutvā saghṛtaṃ kulmāṣaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā dīptāgnir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In the month <s>Māgha</s>, after offering sesame seeds into the fire every day and feeding Brahmins with <s>kulmāṣa</s> mixed with ghee, he becomes one with a strong digestive fire.

children.text: sarvāṃ caturdaśīṃ nadījale snātvā dharmarājānaṃ pūjayitvā sarvapāpebhyaḥ pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: On every fourteenth day, after bathing in river water and worshiping <s>Dharmarāja</s>, he becomes purified from all sins.
If he should desire abundant enjoyments extending to the planets, the moon, and the sun,

children.text: prātaḥsnāyī bhaven nityaṃ dvau māsau māghaphālgunau ||
children.translated_text: he should bathe in the morning every day during the two months <s>Māgha</s> and <s>Phālguna</s>.

children.text: atha kūpakartus tatpravṛtte pānīye duṣkṛtasyārdhaṃ vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: Now, for the maker of a well, when its water has begun to flow, half of his wrongdoing perishes.
The maker of a pond, always satisfied, enjoys the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
A giver of water is always satisfied.
For one who plants trees, the trees become sons in the next world.
One who gives a tree pleases the gods with the tree's flowers,
and guests with its fruits,
and visitors with its shade,
and, when the god rains, the ancestors with its water.
The builder of a bridge obtains heaven.

children.text: devāyatanakārī yasya devasyāyatanaṃ karoti tasyaiva lokam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: One who constructs a temple obtains the world of the very deity whose temple he builds.
Having made it plastered with whitewash, he shines with fame.
Having made it variegated, he obtains the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>.
By the gift of flowers he becomes prosperous.
By the gift of anointing substances, he becomes renowned.
By the gift of lamps he becomes possessed of sight and radiant everywhere.
By the gift of food he becomes strong.
By removing the deity's used offerings, he obtains the fruit of gifting a cow.
The same fruit comes from sweeping the temple, smearing it, sweeping away a Brahmin's leftovers, washing feet, and service at the proper time.
At wells, parks, tanks,

children.text: punaḥ saṃskārakartā ca labhate maulikaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: and temples of the gods, one who performs restoration again obtains the original reward.
The gift of fearlessness is greater than all gifts.
By giving that, one obtains the world one desires.
And by the gift of land likewise.

children.text: gocarmamātrām api bhuvaṃ pradāya sarvapāpebhyaḥ pūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having given even as much land as a cowhide measures, one becomes purified from all sins.
By the gift of a cow one obtains the heavenly world.
The giver of ten milk-cows obtains cow-worlds.
The giver of a hundred milk-cows obtains the worlds of <s>Brahma</s>.

children.text: suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ muktālāṅgūlāṃ kāṃsyopadohāṃ vastrottarīyāṃ dattvā dhenuromasaṃkhyāni varṣāṇi svargalokam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Having given a cow with golden horns, silver hooves, a pearl tail, a bronze milking vessel, and an upper garment of cloth, one obtains the heavenly world for as many years as there are hairs on the cow.
Especially if she is tawny.
Having given a tamed beast that bears the yoke, one becomes equal to the giver of ten milk-cows.
The giver of a horse obtains dwelling in the same world as <s>Sūrya</s>.
The giver of clothing obtains dwelling in the same world as <s>Candra</s>.
By the gift of gold, one obtains dwelling in the same world as <s>Agni</s>.
By the gift of silver, one obtains beauty.
By the gift of metal vessels, one becomes a worthy recipient of all desires.
By the gift of ghee, honey, and oil, one obtains health.
By the gift of medicines, one obtains health.
And by the gift of salt, one obtains loveliness.
By the gift of grain, one obtains satisfaction.
And by the gift of crops likewise.
The giver of food obtains everything.
By the gift of grain, one obtains good fortune.
The giver of sesame obtains the desired offspring.
By the gift of fuel, one becomes one whose fire burns brightly.
And in battle he obtains victory over all.
By the gift of a seat, one obtains a place.
By the gift of a bed, one obtains a wife.
By the gift of sandals, one obtains a chariot yoked with she-mules.
By the gift of an umbrella, one obtains heaven.
By the gift of a palm-leaf fan and a chowrie, one gains comfort on the road.
By the gift of a dwelling site, one obtains lordship over a city.

children.text: yad yad iṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāsti dayitaṃ gṛhe
children.translated_text: Whatever is most desired in the world, and whatever is dear in one's house,

children.text: tat tad guṇavate deyaṃ tad evākṣayam icchatā ||
children.translated_text: that very thing should be given to a man of good qualities by one who wishes that same thing to be imperishable.
What is given to a non-Brahmin has just that same otherworldly result.
It is twofold when given to one who merely calls himself a Brahmin.
It is thousandfold when given to one who has studied.
It is infinite when given to one who has crossed to the end of the Veda.
But the household priest is a recipient as one's own self is.
So too are one's sister, daughter, and sons-in-law.
He should not give even water to a twice-born man who follows the cat-vow,
nor to a sinful man who follows the heron-vow, nor to one who does not know the Veda, O knower of <s>dharma</s>.
One who makes a banner of <s>dharma</s>, is always greedy, deceitful, and hypocritical before the world,
injurious and plotting against all, is to be known as one who follows the cat-vow.
A twice-born man with downcast eyes, deceitful, intent on accomplishing his own ends,
a rogue and falsely humble, is devoted to the heron-vow.

children.text: ye bakavratino loke ye ca mārjāraliṅginaḥ
children.translated_text: Those in the world who follow the heron-vow, and those who bear the marks of a cat,
fall into <s>Andhatāmisra</s> because of that sinful action.

children.text: na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret
children.translated_text: He should not commit sin under the pretext of <s>dharma</s> and then practice a vow,
covering sin with the vow while deceiving women and Śūdras.
Such a Brahmin is censured after death and here by those who speak of <s>Brahman</s>;
and a vow practiced deceitfully goes to the <s>Rakṣases</s>.
One who is without the marks of an order, but lives off a livelihood by wearing the marks of that order,
takes away the sin of those who truly bear the marks, and is born in an animal womb.

children.text: na dānaṃ yaśase dadyān na bhayān nopakāriṇe
children.translated_text: One should not give a gift for fame, nor out of fear, nor to one who has done a favor,
nor to those whose occupation is dancing and singing; it is settled that a gift is for the sake of <s>dharma</s>.
When a householder sees wrinkles and gray hair, he should enter the forest stage.
Or when he sees the child of his child.
Having entrusted his wife to his sons, or being accompanied by her,
even there he should tend the sacred fires.
With what is ploughed without a plough, he should not let the five sacrifices lapse.
And he should not abandon Vedic recitation.
He should maintain celibacy.
He should wear hide and bark-garments.
And he should wear matted hair, beard, body hair, and nails.
He should bathe at the three daily junctions.
He should live like a pigeon, storing for a month or storing for a year.
If he stores for a year, he should discard what was previously stored in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>.

children.text: grāmād āhṛtya vāśnīyād aṣṭau grāsān vane vasan
children.translated_text: Or, dwelling in the forest, he may bring food from the village and eat eight mouthfuls,
using only a leaf-cup, a palāśa leaf, his hand, or a potsherd.
A forest-dweller should dry up his body with <s>tapas</s>.
In summer he should be one who practices the five fires.
In the rainy season he should lie under the open sky.
In winter he should wear wet garments.
He should eat at night.
Or he should eat every other day, every third day, or every fourth day.
He may eat flowers.
He may eat fruits.
He may eat vegetables.
Or he may eat leaves.
Or he should eat barley food once at the ends of the fortnights.
Or he should live by <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> observances.
He may pound grain with stones.
Or use his teeth as the mortar.
This whole world, divine and human, has <s>tapas</s> as its root,

children.text: tapomadhyaṃ tapo'ntaṃ ca tapasā ca tathā dhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: has <s>tapas</s> as its middle and <s>tapas</s> as its end, and likewise is sustained by <s>tapas</s>.

children.text: yad duścaraṃ yad durāpaṃ yad dūraṃ yacca duṣkaram
children.translated_text: Whatever is hard to practice, whatever is hard to obtain, whatever is far away, and whatever is difficult to do

children.text: sarvaṃ tat tapasā sādhyaṃ tapo hi duratikramam ||
children.translated_text: All that is to be accomplished is attainable through austerity, for austerity is hard to transgress.

children.text: atha triṣv āśrameṣu pakvakaṣāyaḥ prājāpatyām iṣṭiṃ kṛtvā sarvavedasaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā pravrajyāśramī syāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, when his passions have ripened in the three <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), after performing the <s>Prājāpatya</s> iṣṭi and giving all his possessions as the sacrificial fee, he should become one belonging to the order of renunciation.
Having placed the fires within himself, he should go to a village for the sake of alms.
He should practice taking alms from seven houses.
If there is no gain, he should not be distressed.
He should not beg from a beggar.

children.text: bhuktavati jane atīte pātrasaṃpāte bhaikṣam ādadyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should take alms when people have eaten and the collection of vessels has passed.
It should be in an earthen vessel, a wooden bowl, or a gourd-vessel.
And these should be purified for him with water.
He should be disturbed by gaining what has been received with special honor.
He should have an empty house as his dwelling.
Or he may have the root of a tree as his dwelling.
He should not stay a second night in a village.
He should take only a loincloth and a covering as his garment.
He should set down his foot where it has been purified by sight.
He should take water purified by a cloth.
He should speak what has been purified by truth.
He should do what has been purified by the mind.
He should not long for death, nor for life.
He should endure harsh words.
He should not despise anyone at all.
He should be without expectation.
He should be without salutation.
When one man cuts one arm with an axe, and another sprinkles the other with sandalwood,

children.text: nākalyāṇaṃ na kalyāṇaṃ tayor api ca cintayet ||
children.translated_text: he should think neither evil nor good even of those two.
He should be constantly devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
He should see the impermanence of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly transmigration).
And the impure condition of the body.
The alteration of beauty through old age.
And the affliction caused by bodily, mental, and adventitious diseases.
And by those that are innate.
Residence in the womb, in constant darkness.
And amid urine and feces.
And the experience of suffering from cold and heat there.
At the time of birth, the experience of great pain from emerging through the narrow passage of the womb.
In childhood, delusion and dependence on elders.
Many hardships arising from study.

children.text: yauvane ca viṣayāprāptāv amārgeṇa tadavāptau viṣayasevanān narake patanam ||
children.translated_text: And in youth, when objects of sense are not obtained, or when they are obtained by a wrong path, falling into hell from enjoying those objects.
Dwelling with those who are disliked and separation from those who are liked.
And very great suffering in hell.
And in the wandering through <s>saṃsāra</s>, in animal wombs.

children.text: evam asmin satatayāyini saṃsāre na kiṃcit sukham ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in this ever-moving <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no happiness at all.

children.text: yad api kiṃcit duḥkhābhāvāpekṣayā sukhasaṃjñaṃ tad apyanityam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is called happiness with reference to the absence of pain is itself impermanent.
When one is unable to attend upon that, or when it is not obtained, there is great suffering.
He should see this body as consisting of seven bodily constituents.
It consists of fat, blood, flesh, marrow-fat, bone, marrow, and semen.
It is bound over with skin.
And it is foul-smelling.
It is an abode of impurities.
Even when surrounded by hundreds of pleasures, it is subject to change.
Even when maintained with effort, it is perishable.
It is the seat of desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and envy.
It consists of earth, water, fire, wind, and ether.
It is furnished with bones, veins, arteries, and sinews.
It is full of dust and passion.
It has six layers of skin.
It is supported by three hundred and sixty bones.
Their division is as follows.
Together with the small ones, the teeth are sixty-four.
There are twenty nails.
And there are the slender bones of the hands and feet.
There are sixty joints of the fingers and toes.
Two in the heels.
Four in the ankles.
Four in the forearms.
Four in the shanks.
Two each in the knees and cheeks.
In the thighs and shoulders.
In the collarbones, palate, sockets, and pelvic plates.
There is one pubic bone.
The backbone has forty-five parts.
The neck has fifteen bones.
One is the collarbone.
Likewise the jaw.
And two are at its root.
Two are in the forehead, eyes, and cheeks.
The nose has a solid bone.
Together with swellings and plates, the ribs are seventy-two.
The chest has seventeen.
There are two temples.
And there are four skull-bones of the head.
In this body there are seven hundred veins.
Nine hundred sinews.
Two hundred arteries.
Five hundred muscles.
Of the minute arteries there are twenty-nine lakhs, nine hundred, and fifty-six.
There are three lakhs of beard-hair and head-hair follicles.
There are one hundred and seven vital spots.
Two hundred joints.
There are fifty-four crores and sixty-seven lakhs of body-hair pores.

children.text: nābhir ojo gudaṃ śukraṃ śoṇitaṃ śaṅkhakau mūrdhā kaṇṭho hṛdayaṃ ceti prāṇāyatanāṇi ||
children.translated_text: The navel, vital essence, anus, semen, blood, the two temples, the head, throat, and heart are the seats of life.

children.text: bāhudvayaṃ jaṅghādvayaṃ madhyaṃ śīrṣam iti ṣaḍaṅgāni ||
children.translated_text: The two arms, the two shanks, the trunk, and the head are the six limbs.

children.text: vasā vapā avahananaṃ nābhiḥ klomā yakṛtplīhā kṣudrāntraṃ vṛkkakau bastiḥ purīṣādhānaṃ āmāśayaḥ hṛdayaṃ sthūlāntraṃ gudam udaraṃ gudakoṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: Fat, omentum, the avahanana, the navel, lungs, liver and spleen, the small intestine, the two kidneys, the bladder, the receptacle of feces, the stomach, the heart, the large intestine, the rectum, the belly, and the rectal cavity are in it.

children.text: kanīnike akṣikūṭe śaṣkulī karṇau karṇapattrakau gaṇḍau bhruvau śaṅkhau dantaveṣṭau oṣṭhau kakundare vaṅkṣaṇau vṛṣaṇau vṛkkau śleṣmasaṃghātikau stanau upajihvā sphicau bāhū jaṅghe ūrū piṇḍike tālūdaraṃ bastiśīrṣau cibukaṃ galaśuṇḍike avaṭuścetyasmin śarīre sthānāni ||
children.translated_text: The pupils, eye-sockets, ear-shells, ears, ear-flaps, cheeks, brows, temples, gums, lips, the kakundaras, groins, testicles, kidneys, collections of phlegm, breasts, uvula, buttocks, arms, shanks, thighs, calves, palate and belly, the heads of the bladder, chin, the throat-pendants, and the throat-pit are places in this body.
Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are the sense-objects.
The nose, eyes, skin, tongue, and ear are the cognitive senses.
The hands, feet, anus, generative organ, and tongue are the active senses.
Mind, intellect, self, and the unmanifest are beyond the senses.
This body, O <s>Vasudhā</s>, is called the <s>kṣetra</s> (field).

children.text: etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajñam iti tadvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who know this call the one who knows it the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field).

children.text: kṣetrajñam api māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhāvini
children.translated_text: Know me also, O lady, as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> in all fields.
The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field should always be known by one who seeks liberation.

children.text: ūrusthottānacaraṇaḥ savye kare karam itaraṃ nyasya tālusthācalajihvo dantair dantān asaṃspṛśan svaṃ nāsikāgraṃ paśyan diśaścānavalokayan vibhīḥ praśāntātmā caturviṃśatyā tattvair vyatītaṃ cintayet ||
children.translated_text: With his feet placed upward on his thighs, placing the other hand in the left hand, with his tongue steady on the palate, not touching the teeth with the teeth, looking at the tip of his own nose and not looking toward the quarters, fearless and tranquil in self, he should contemplate the one beyond the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s> (principles).

children.text: nityam atīndriyam aguṇaṃ śabdasparśarūparasagandhātītaṃ sarvajñam atisthūlam ||
children.translated_text: He should contemplate the eternal one, beyond the senses, without qualities, beyond sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, omniscient, greater than the gross.
Pervading all, subtler than the subtle.
Having hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, and the power of all the senses everywhere.
Thus he should meditate.
For one devoted to meditation, the manifestation of yoga comes within a year.

children.text: atha nirākāre lakṣabandhaṃ kartuṃ na śaknoti tadā pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśamanobuddhyātmāvyaktapuruṣāṇāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ dhyātvā tatra labdhalakṣaḥ tatparityajyāparam aparaṃ dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: Now, if he cannot fix his attention on the formless one, then, after first meditating successively on earth, water, fire, wind, ether, mind, intellect, self, the unmanifest, and <s>puruṣa</s>, and after gaining steadiness there, he should abandon each earlier support and meditate on the next one.
In this way he should begin meditation on <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tatrāpyasamarthaḥ svahṛdayapadmasya avāṅmukhasya madhye dīpavat puruṣaṃ dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: If he is unable even there, he should meditate on <s>puruṣa</s> like a lamp in the middle of the lotus of his own heart, turned downward.

children.text: tatrāpyasamartho bhagavantaṃ vāsudevaṃ kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinam aṅgadinaṃ śrīvatsāṅkaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitoraskaṃ saumyarūpaṃ caturbhujaṃ śaṅkhacakragadāpadmadharaṃ caraṇamadhyagatabhuvaṃ dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: If he is unable even there, he should meditate on the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, crowned, wearing earrings and armlets, marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, with his chest adorned by a forest-garland, gracious in form, four-armed, holding conch, discus, mace, and lotus, with the earth situated between his feet.
Whatever he meditates on, that he attains: this is the secret of meditation.

children.text: tasmāt sarvam eva kṣaraṃ tyaktvā akṣaram eva dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned everything perishable, he should meditate only on the imperishable.

children.text: na ca puruṣaṃ vinā kiṃcid apyakṣaram asti ||
children.translated_text: And apart from <s>puruṣa</s> there is nothing at all that is imperishable.
Having attained him, one becomes liberated.

children.text: puram ākramya sakalaṃ śete yasmān mahāprabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Because the great lord occupies the whole city and lies there,
therefore he is called <s>puruṣa</s> by those who reflect on reality.
In the early and later parts of the night, the yogin, ever free from sloth,
should meditate on <s>Viṣṇu</s> as <s>puruṣa</s>, without qualities, the twenty-fifth principle.
He is the self of the principles, inaccessible, and devoid of all principles;
inactive and yet bearing all, without qualities and yet the enjoyer of qualities.

children.text: bahir antaśca bhūtānām acaraṃ caram eva ca
children.translated_text: He is outside and inside beings, unmoving and also moving;

children.text: sūkṣmatvāt tadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat ||
children.translated_text: because of his subtlety he is unknowable; he is far away and also near.

children.text: avibhaktaṃ ca bhūtena vibhaktam iva ca sthitam
children.translated_text: Undivided among beings, he stands as if divided;
he has the form of past, future, and present, devouring and bringing forth.

children.text: jyotiṣām api tajjyotis tamasaḥ param ucyate
children.translated_text: He is the light even of lights and is said to be beyond darkness;

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya dhiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: he is knowledge, the knowable, and the goal of knowledge, established in the heart of all.

children.text: iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the field, knowledge, and the knowable have been stated briefly.
My devotee, having understood this, becomes fit for my state.

children.text: ityevam uktā vasumatī jānubhyāṃ śirasā ca namaskāraṃ kṛtvovāca ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Vasumatī</s> had been addressed in this way, she bowed with her knees and head and said:

children.text: bhagavan tvatsamīpe satatam evaṃ catvāri bhūtāni kṛtālayāni ākāśaḥ śaṅkharūpī vāyuścakrarūpī tejaśca gadārūpi ambho 'mbhoruharūpi
children.translated_text: Blessed lord, these four elements have always made their abode near you: ether in the form of the conch, wind in the form of the discus, fire in the form of the mace, and water in the form of the lotus.

children.text: aham apyanenaiva rūpeṇa bhagavatpādamadhye parivartinī bhavitum icchāmi ||
children.translated_text: I too, in this very form, wish to be moving between the blessed lord's feet.
Addressed in this way, the blessed lord said, 'So be it.'
<s>Vasudhā</s>, having obtained her desire, did so.
And she praised the God of gods:
Oṃ, homage to you.
O God of gods.
O <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
O first god.

O lord of water.

O lover of <s>Brahman</s>.

O <s>Mahārājika</s>.
O <s>Caturmahārājika</s>.

children.text: stutvā tvevaṃ prasannena manasā pṛthivī tadā
children.translated_text: Then, after praising her in this way with a pleased mind, the Earth
Vasuṃdharā, having obtained her desire, spoke face to face to the goddess.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā śriyaṃ devadevasya viṣṇor gṛhītapādāṃ tapasā jvalantīm
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Śrī</s>, who had taken hold of the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god of gods, and who blazed with austerity,
the delighted goddess <s>Vasudhā</s> questioned the goddess, lovely in color like well-heated jāmbūnada gold.
O excellent one, whose lovely hands are like opened red lotuses, whose feet are held by opened red lotuses,
you who are ever established in an abode of opened red lotuses, whose color is like the middle of an opened red lotus,
O blue-lotus-eyed one, golden in color, dressed in white, with limbs adorned with jewels,
moon-faced, shining like the sun, of great power, chief of the world,

children.text: tvam eva nidrā jagataḥ pradhānā lakṣmīr dhṛtiḥ śrīr viratir jayā ca
children.translated_text: you alone are the foremost sleep of the world: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, steadfastness, prosperity, withdrawal, and victory,

children.text: kāntiḥ prabhā kīrtir atho vibhūtiḥ sarasvatī vāg atha pāvanī ca ||
children.translated_text: beauty, radiance, fame, and also majesty, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, speech, and purity,

children.text: svadhā titikṣā vasudhā pratiṣṭhā sthitiḥ sudīkṣā ca tathā sunītiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Svadhā</s>, forbearance, earth, foundation, continuance, good consecration, and likewise good conduct,

children.text: khyātir viśālā ca tathānasūyā svāhā ca medhā ca tathaiva buddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: renown, breadth, and likewise freedom from envy, <s>Svāhā</s>, intelligence, and understanding too.

children.text: ākramya sarvaṃ tu yathā trilokīṃ tiṣṭhatyayaṃ devavaro 'sitākṣi
children.translated_text: Just as this best of gods, O dark-eyed one, pervading all, stands over the three worlds,

children.text: tathā sthitā tvaṃ varade tathāpi pṛcchāmyahaṃ te vasatiṃ vibhūteḥ ||
children.translated_text: so you too stand, O giver of boons; even so, I ask you about the dwelling-place of your majesty.

children.text: ityevam uktā vasudhāṃ babhāṣe lakṣmīs tadā devavarāgrataḥsthā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, standing before the best of gods, then spoke to the Earth:

children.text: sadā sthitāhaṃ madhusūdanasya devasya pārśve tapanīyavarṇe ||
children.translated_text: I am always established beside the god <s>Madhusūdana</s>, O golden-colored one.

children.text: asyājñayā yaṃ manasā smarāmi śriyā yutaṃ taṃ pravadanti santaḥ
children.translated_text: By his command, whomever I remember in my mind, the good call that person endowed with prosperity.

children.text: saṃsmāraṇe cāpyatha yatra cāhaṃ sthitā sadā tacchṛṇu lokadhātri ||
children.translated_text: And when I am remembered, and wherever I am always present, hear that, O bearer of the world.

children.text: vasāmyathārke ca niśākare ca tārāgaṇāḍhye gagane vimeghe
children.translated_text: I dwell in the sun and the moon, in the cloudless sky rich with hosts of stars,

children.text: meghe tathā lambapayodhare ca śakrāyudhāḍhye ca taḍitprakāśe ||
children.translated_text: and likewise in the cloud, in the hanging rain-cloud, in that which is furnished with <s>Śakra</s>'s bow, and in the flash of lightning.

children.text: tathā suvarṇe vimale ca rūpye ratneṣu vastreṣv amaleṣu bhūme
children.translated_text: Likewise I dwell in gold, in spotless silver, in jewels, and in clean garments, O Earth,
in rows of white mansions and in temples adorned with banners.

children.text: sadyaḥ kṛte cāpyatha gomaye ca matte gajendre turage prahṛṣṭe
children.translated_text: I dwell in what is freshly prepared, in cow-dung, in a rutting lordly elephant, and in a delighted horse,

children.text: vṛṣe tathā darpasamanvite ca vipre tathaivādhyayanaprapanne ||
children.translated_text: likewise in a bull possessed of vigor, and in a Brahmin devoted to study.

children.text: siṃhāsane cāmalake ca bilve chatre ca śaṅkhe ca tathaiva padme
children.translated_text: I am present in a throne, in the āmalaka and bilva fruits, in an umbrella, in a conch, and likewise in a lotus,

children.text: dīpte hutāśe vimale ca khaḍga ādarśabimbe ca tathā sthitāham ||
children.translated_text: in blazing fire, in a spotless sword, and in the disk of a mirror.
I dwell in full water-pots furnished with chowries and ornamented with palm-leaf fans,

children.text: bhṛṅgārapātreṣu manohareṣu mṛdi sthitāhaṃ ca navoddhṛtāyām ||
children.translated_text: in charming sprinkling vessels, and in earth that has been newly dug up.

children.text: kṣīre tathā sarpiṣi śādvale ca kṣaudre tathā dadhni puraṃdhrigātre
children.translated_text: Likewise in milk, in ghee, in green grass, in honey, in curds, and in the body of a married woman,

children.text: dehe kumāryāśca tathā surāṇāṃ tapasvināṃ yajñahutāṃ ca dehe ||
children.translated_text: and likewise in the body of a maiden, of gods, of ascetics, and of those who have offered oblations in sacrifice.

children.text: śare ca saṃgrāmavinirgate ca sthitā mṛte svargasadaḥprayāte
children.translated_text: I am present in an arrow that has gone forth in battle, and in a dead man who has gone to the dwellers in heaven,

children.text: vedadhvanau cāpyatha śaṅkhaśabde svāhāsvadhāyām atha vādyaśabde ||
children.translated_text: in the sound of the Veda, and also in the sound of a conch, in <s>Svāhā</s> and <s>Svadhā</s>, and in the sound of musical instruments.

children.text: rājyābhiṣeke ca tathā vivāhe yajñe vare snātaśirasyathāpi
children.translated_text: I dwell in a royal consecration, likewise in a marriage, in an excellent sacrifice, and also in a head that has been bathed,

children.text: puṣpeṣu śukleṣu ca parvateṣu phaleṣu ramyeṣu saridvarāsu ||
children.translated_text: in white flowers, in mountains, in beautiful fruits, and in excellent rivers,

children.text: saraḥsu pūrṇeṣu tathā jaleṣu saśādvalāyāṃ bhuvi padmakhaṇḍe
children.translated_text: in full lakes and likewise in waters, on grassy ground, and in a cluster of lotuses,

children.text: vane ca vatse ca śiśau prahṛṣṭe sādhau nare dharmaparāyaṇe ca ||
children.translated_text: in a forest, in a calf, in a delighted child, and in a good man devoted to dharma.

children.text: ācārasevinyatha śāstranitye vinītaveṣe ca tathā suveṣe
children.translated_text: I dwell in those who observe proper conduct, who are constant in śāstra, who wear modest dress, and likewise who are well dressed,

children.text: suśuddhadānte malavarjite ca mṛṣṭāśane cātithipūjake ca ||
children.translated_text: in those with very clean teeth, free from dirt, eating clean food, and honoring guests,

children.text: svadāratuṣṭe nirate ca dharme dharmotkaṭe cātyaśanād vimukte
children.translated_text: in one content with his own wife, intent on dharma, ardent in dharma, and free from overeating,

children.text: sadā sapuṣpe sasugandhigātre sugandhalipte ca vibhūṣite ca ||
children.translated_text: always with flowers, with a fragrant body, anointed with fragrance, and adorned.

children.text: satye sthite bhūtahite niviṣṭe kṣamānvite krodhavivarjite ca
children.translated_text: I dwell in one established in truth, devoted to the welfare of beings, endowed with patience, and free from anger,

children.text: svakāryadakṣe parakāryadakṣe kalyāṇacitte ca sadā vinīte ||
children.translated_text: skilled in his own affairs and skilled in others' affairs, benevolent in mind and always modest.
I am always present among women who are well adorned, devoted to their husbands, and pleasant in speech,
not empty-handed, accompanied by sons, with their goods well guarded, and fond of offerings,
whose houses are well swept, who have conquered their senses, who are free from quarrel, and who are not greedy,

children.text: dharmavyapekṣāsu dayānvitāsu sthitā sadāhaṃ madhusūdane ca ||
children.translated_text: who care for dharma and are endowed with compassion; and I am always present in <s>Madhusūdana</s>.

children.text: nimeṣamātraṃ ca vinā kṛtāhaṃ na jātu tiṣṭhe puruṣottamena ||
children.translated_text: I never remain, even for the mere blink of an eye, separated from <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

children.text: dharmaśāstram idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ svayaṃ devena bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: This excellent <s>dharmaśāstra</s> was spoken by the god himself;

children.text: ye dvijā dhārayiṣyanti teṣāṃ svarge gatiḥ parā ||
children.translated_text: the twice-born who retain it will have the supreme course in heaven.

children.text: idaṃ pavitraṃ maṅgalyaṃ svargyam āyuṣyam eva ca
children.translated_text: This is purifying, auspicious, heaven-giving, and life-giving,
and it increases knowledge, fame, wealth, and good fortune.

children.text: adhyetavyaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ śrāvyaṃ śrotavyam eva ca
children.translated_text: It is to be studied, retained, recited, and heard,

children.text: śrāddheṣu śrāvaṇīyaṃ ca bhūtikāmair naraiḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: and at śrāddhas it should always be recited by men who desire prosperity.

children.text: ya idaṃ paṭhate nityaṃ bhūtikāmo naraḥ sadā
children.translated_text: The man who desires prosperity and always reads this daily

children.text: idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ kathitaṃ ca dhare tava ||
children.translated_text: has heard this supreme secret, told to you, O Earth.

children.text: mayā prasannena jagaddhitārthaṃ saubhāgyam etat paramaṃ yaśasyam
children.translated_text: It has been told by me, being pleased, for the welfare of the world; this is the highest good fortune and glory,
the destruction of bad dreams, endowed with much merit, an auspicious abode, an eternal <s>dharmaśāstra</s>.
